findings.title: The within-viz version chain is a phantom — DELETE depth/parent_hash/root_hash/version_count/GET-versions, keep only the atom-snapshot /diff reads
findings.evidence: api/routers/visualizations.py:110-148 (_write_root_version ALWAYS writes parent_hash=None, root_hash=set_hash_value, depth=0); :581 (version_count=1 hard-coded at remix); grep confirms version_count is NEVER $inc'd anywhere (only set to 1 at create/remix/migration); :749 and :874 both sort visualization_versions by depth which is invariantly 0; api/scripts/migrate_visualization_forks.py:121-125 writes the identical depth-0 root
findings.current_state: Every visualization holds exactly one VisualizationVersion (depth 0, parent_hash None) for its entire lifetime. No operation creates a second version on a viz's own chain — an edit mutates the live row in place (PATCH) or forks a NEW viz (remix, which starts its OWN depth-0 chain). So GET /versions always returns a one-element list, GET /provenance's `chain` is always one node, version_count is a frozen 1, and parent_hash/root_hash/depth on VisualizationVersion are dead fields. The CORE simultaneously over-builds a linear-version substrate AND under-grows it. The two database indexes (viz_slug+depth, root_hash) index columns that never vary or are never queried by range.
findings.proposed: Transpose to the shape that has consumers: DELETE VisualizationVersion.{parent_hash, root_hash, depth}, Visualization.version_count, the GET /versions endpoint + VersionEntry/VersionsResponse, and ProvenanceResponse.chain + ProvenanceNode (keep ProvenanceResponse as just the fork_breadcrumb, or rename it ForkAncestryResponse). Keep the per-viz VisualizationVersion as a flat content-addressed atom-snapshot keyed f'{viz_slug}:{set_hash}' carrying ONLY {viz_slug, set_hash, author_slug, the 5 atoms, forked_from_hash, atom_diff, created_at} — exactly what GET /diff reads. Drop the viz_slug+depth and root_hash indexes; the _id lookup is the only access path. This is the directive's elegance transposition: ship what has a reader, delete the linear-chain math nothing fills. The cross-viz fork_of breadcrumb (the real lineage) is untouched and correct.

findings.title: PATCH mutates palette_slug (a remix atom) outside the version model — set_hash + the immutable-1yr /diff ETag go stale
findings.evidence: api/models/visualization.py:207 (VisualizationUpdate.palette_slug); api/routers/visualizations.py:381-383 (PATCH does $set of palette_slug directly, never recomputes set_hash); :480 _head_set_hash falls back to recompute only when stored set_hash is empty-string; :851 /diff sets Cache-Control public,max-age=31536000,immutable keyed on the (possibly-stale) set_hash
findings.current_state: palette_slug is one of the five remix atoms (atomdiff.ATOM_KEY_ORDER) yet it is freely PATCH-able. A palette PATCH writes the new slug to the live row but leaves the stored set_hash (computed at create from the OLD palette) and the row's single VisualizationVersion snapshot untouched. The viz's true atom-set identity now disagrees with its stored set_hash. /diff serves a 1-year immutable cache entry keyed and ETagged on a set_hash that no longer reflects the atoms. A diff-viewer would render a palette change as no-change.
findings.proposed: One decision, no 'leave it': make palette_slug remix-only by DROPPING it from VisualizationUpdate (a palette change becomes a remix that mints a new child + records a palette atom-diff — coherent with the atom model, and palette is the only nullable add/remove atom so this is the cleanest demonstration of the diff vocabulary). The contract already supports this: the remix path handles palette tri-state via model_fields_set (F-08). If product genuinely needs in-place palette edits, the alternative is to make any PATCH that touches an atom re-run atomdiff.enumerate_atoms→set_hash and rewrite the row's snapshot — but that re-introduces the per-viz version growth this audit is deleting, so remix-only is the gestalt-consistent choice. Ship with a test asserting a palette change is reflected in /diff.

findings.title: GET /diff validates the `to` param on-chain then silently ignores it — to_hash is always HEAD
findings.evidence: api/routers/visualizations.py:830-839: `to` is range-checked against on_chain (:830) but `effective_from = from_ or fork_of_hash or head_hash` (:833) and both response branches hard-code to_hash=head_hash; there is no effective_to
findings.current_state: A client may pass ?to=<fork_of_hash> (which passes the on_chain validation at :830) and receive a response whose to_hash is HEAD anyway, with no error. Worse, ?from=HEAD&to=fork_hash yields identical=True (the from==head branch) — the requested direction is silently swallowed. The endpoint advertises a two-endpoint from/to interface but only honors a one-axis from→HEAD diff. Because the chain has exactly two on-chain hashes (HEAD, fork_of_hash) the harm is bounded today, but the contract is dishonest and the J-diff-shape doc (§3.2) defines toHash as 'the to version (defaults to live HEAD)' implying it is selectable.
findings.proposed: Make `to` real and small: compute effective_to = to or head_hash; if effective_from == effective_to return identical=True with from_hash=to_hash=that hash; otherwise resolve the recorded delta between the two on-chain hashes (the only non-trivial pair is {fork_of_hash, head_hash}, whose ops are the recorded atom_diff, reversed if from==head). Reject any from==to that isn't on-chain. This honors the param the doc promised without re-introducing chain-walk machinery (there are only two hashes). Folds cleanly into the W2-fix integrity pass.

findings.title: Backfill writes atom_diff=[] on a fork's root version, cementing a false 'no remix delta' if the fork's root version was never written (crash-orphan)
findings.evidence: api/scripts/migrate_visualization_forks.py:122-125 sets forked_from_hash=row.get('fork_of_hash') but atom_diff=[] unconditionally; api/routers/visualizations.py:553-596 remix writes the viz row (step 2) BEFORE the root version (step 3) — a crash between them leaves a fork row with fork_of_hash set but NO version, which the migration then backfills with an EMPTY atom_diff
findings.current_state: The §11 ordered-write sequence is viz-first (forced by the compound _id needing the child slug). If a remix crashes after the child viz insert (step 2) but before the root-version insert (step 3), the orphaned fork row carries fork_of_hash but has no VisualizationVersion. The backfill migration then mints a root version with atom_diff=[] — permanently asserting the fork is identical to its source, which is a lie (a remix that changed nothing is a 422; a real fork always has ≥1 op). /diff over that fork serves identical=True, cached immutable 1yr.
findings.proposed: When the migration backfills a row whose fork_of_hash is set, RECOMPUTE the atom_diff from the two snapshots rather than writing []: load the source viz (by fork_of, its HEAD atoms) and the orphan's own atoms, run atomdiff.diff_atoms(source_atoms, child_atoms), and persist that as the recorded delta. For an original (fork_of_hash is None) atom_diff=[] stays correct. This makes the self-heal honest. If W2-transpose deletes the linear-chain math, this still applies to the single retained snapshot. Pair with the §11 prose amend (drop the 'crash leaves no lie' overstatement; name the version-less-fork window) and a crash-window test (viz present, version absent → /diff recomputes-or-404s, never lies identical=True).

findings.title: The 7 CORE endpoints have ZERO web/src/lib/api.ts caller; gallery.publish still PATCHes visibility=public instead of POST /:slug/publish
findings.evidence: grep of web/src/lib/api.ts for remix|/forks|/provenance|/diff|/versions|publish|unpublish = 0 hits (confirmed); web/src/stores/gallery.ts:219-226 publish() sends PATCH {visibility:'public'}; web/src/lib/types.ts:225 declares version_count (a field this audit recommends deleting server-side)
findings.current_state: The remix/publish/diff/versions/provenance/forks CORE is server-only substrate — no client method or UI calls any of it (a binary inv-15 breach at HEAD). gallery.publish() routes through the generic PATCH-visibility path, bypassing the purpose-built idempotent POST /:slug/publish verb (whose entire reason to exist — re-publish-without-duplicate, in-place $set — is therefore unreached). The TS twin in types.ts even mirrors version_count, a field this audit recommends deleting; the consumer-side type would need to follow the W2-transpose.
findings.proposed: Wire the client + UI as the inv-15 close-gate: add api.ts methods for the surviving-after-transpose endpoints (remix, forks, provenance/fork-breadcrumb, diff, publish, unpublish), and re-point gallery.publish() onto POST /:slug/publish (retiring the PATCH-to-public path entirely so the verb's idempotent in-place semantics are actually exercised). Keep types.ts in lockstep with the W2-transpose deletions (drop version_count, drop the chain/depth fields). The CORE is half-shipped until a real diff-viewer + publish UI consume it. This is the deepest coherence transposition: the data model only earns its shape once a reader proves which fields are load-bearing.

findings.title: content_hash and set_hash are two content-addresses over overlapping-but-different projections; a palette/settings-only remix changes set_hash while content_hash stays identical
findings.evidence: api/routers/visualizations.py:83-97 _content_hash = digest over {image_slug, contour_hash, active_bases, n_harmonics}; api/lib/crud/atomdiff.py:112-120 set_hash = digest over the 5 atoms incl palette_slug + contour_settings + animation_settings; remix recomputes child_content_hash at :546 from the SAME subject+bases+harmonics
findings.current_state: Two distinct identities computed by the one canonical_digest primitive over different projections — by design (content_hash is the dedup/render substrate per CRUD-CONTRACT §1; set_hash is the subject-free remix identity per §1.3). But a remix that changes only palette_slug or only contour_settings/animation_settings produces a child with a DIFFERENT set_hash but the SAME content_hash as its parent. That is intentional (such a child renders identically but is a distinct remix point), yet it means content_hash is no longer a unique row key and two distinct vizzes can share it. The model is coherent but the overlap is a latent footgun if any future code treats content_hash as identity.
findings.proposed: No structural change needed — this is correct by design — but make the coherence explicit and machine-checked: add a one-line model invariant doc that content_hash is render-dedup ONLY (never identity, never unique-indexed) and set_hash is remix-identity, and assert in a test that two remixes differing only in a non-content atom (palette) share content_hash but differ in set_hash. This closes the latent footgun the W2-transpose's tighter version model would otherwise re-expose. Optionally note in the canonical_digest docstring that content_hash deliberately excludes the 3 styling atoms.

findings.title: fork_count is a denormalized counter bumped last-and-unconditionally in remix; an over-count is self-described as 'cosmetic' but the most-forked sort orders on it
findings.evidence: api/routers/visualizations.py:600 ($inc fork_count, step 4, 'self-healing — an over-count is cosmetic'); api/lib/crud/cursors.py:21 'most-forked' sort key = fork_count; the fork_count is never reconciled against the actual count of fork_of==slug children
findings.current_state: fork_count drives a user-facing sort (most-forked) yet is a fire-and-forget $inc with no reconciliation. The §11 narrative calls drift cosmetic, but the only consumer is a ranking — a drifted count mis-orders the gallery. Because the bump is the LAST step (after both inserts), a crash before it UNDER-counts (a real fork exists, count not bumped); the idempotency replay map mitigates retries but not partial crashes.
findings.proposed: Either (a) keep fork_count as an accepted-eventually-consistent counter but add a cheap reconciler (a periodic or on-read count_documents({fork_of: slug, deleted_at: None, visibility: 'public'}) that corrects drift — the same shape as the janitor), or (b) drop the denormalized counter entirely and compute most-forked via an aggregation/count when the forks collection is small (it is bounded by the public children). Given the directive's KISS lean and that forks are rare, (b) — delete the stored counter, derive on demand — is the more coherent transposition: one fewer field that can lie. Fold the decision into W2-transpose alongside the version_count deletion.

findings.title: set_hash default '' is a migration sentinel that _head_set_hash silently recomputes — acceptable transient, but no post-backfill assertion that it is gone
findings.evidence: api/models/visualization.py:145 (set_hash: str = ''); api/routers/visualizations.py:477-480 _head_set_hash falls back to recompute when stored set_hash is falsy; migration backfills it but nothing asserts zero live rows carry '' after
findings.current_state: The empty-string default lets legacy rows validate before the additive backfill runs, and _head_set_hash recomputes deterministically at read time — a sound transient, not a fallback flag. But there is no close-gate assertion that, post-backfill, no live row carries set_hash==''. A row that somehow escapes the migration (e.g., inserted between migration and a code path that doesn't stamp it) would silently recompute forever, masking a write-path gap.
findings.proposed: Keep the deterministic read-time recompute (it is honest), and add a W6 assertion / startup smoke check that count_documents({set_hash: '', deleted_at: None}) == 0 after backfill, failing the deploy gate if not. This closes the sentinel smell without introducing legacy: the recompute is a correctness floor, the assertion proves the write path always stamps it.

open_questions: After W2-transpose deletes the linear version chain, does any future tranche (L-webmcp?) actually need an edit-creates-a-version operation? If yes, the chain fields are 'delete-now-rebuild-later'; if no (the gestalt expectation: remix is the only branching), the deletion is permanent and the model is strictly simpler. The audit recommends permanent deletion absent a named consumer.

Should palette_slug becoming remix-only (A2-M2) be coordinated with value.js, whose atomdiff twin keys over PaletteColor[]? The /diff envelope is repo-neutral so the wire is unaffected, but the 'which atoms are PATCH-able vs remix-only' policy is a per-repo data-model decision — confirm value.js does not need a symmetric constraint (likely not; inv-16, it is fourier-local).

The TS twin web/src/lib/types.ts:225 already declares version_count — confirm the W2-transpose deletion sweeps the frontend types in the same wave so the consumer (M5) never compiles against a deleted field.

A3.dimension: A3 — inv-15 consumer-gap architecture (the wire-the-UI critical path for J's 7 CORE endpoints)
A3.verdict: J's CORE shipped a complete server substrate (POST /remix, /publish, /unpublish; GET /forks, /provenance, /diff, /versions — 266 api tests green) and even the hand-typed TS response twins in web/src/lib/types.ts (AtomOp, DiffResponse, ProvenanceResponse, VersionsResponse, ForkCrumb), yet web/src/lib/api.ts has ZERO callers for any of them and no store action or component touches the remix/diff/provenance/versions surface. The single live visibility mutation, gallery.publish(), is still a PATCH {visibility:"public"} (stores/gallery.ts:219-238) rather than the idempotent POST /:slug/publish — and there is no unpublish path at all. This is a binary inv-15 breach across seven endpoints: the substrate exists with no consumer. The fix is a coherent wire-the-UI layer — seven api.ts functions, a fork/provenance Pinia slice, a /v/:slug detail surface that hosts a remix action + provenance breadcrumb + version timeline, and a diff-viewer that paints atom changes via glass-ui 4.0 useTextHighlight (CSS Custom Highlight). All twins/contracts are already in place; this is consumption, not new backend design.

findings.title: publish/unpublish: replace the PATCH-visibility shim with the idempotent verb routes
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/gallery.ts:219-238 (publish() calls api.updateVisualization(slug,{visibility:'public'},etag)); api.ts has NO publishVisualization/unpublishVisualization; backend POST /api/visualizations/{slug}/{publish,unpublish} exist (visualizations.py:_visibility_verb ~line 620) with ZERO web caller; no unpublish anywhere in web/src
findings.current_state: The gallery's publish action lifts draft→public by PATCHing the visibility key — the exact intent the J.W1c spec routes through a dedicated verb. The spec's whole point (J.W1c-publish-visibility.md §3.4, §4: 'NO new row, ever; idempotent in-place $set; the verb is the WebMCP-legible binary public-membership toggle') is satisfied server-side but the client still uses the arbitrary-edit channel. Unpublish (public→unlisted) has no UI at all, so a published viz cannot be delisted without an admin or a raw visibility PATCH the contract guard would reject (public→draft is forbidden).
findings.proposed: Add api.ts: publishVisualization(slug, etag) and unpublishVisualization(slug, etag) → POST `${slug}/publish|unpublish` via apiFetchWithETag with If-Match. Re-point gallery.ts publish() onto publishVisualization and add an unpublish() action; both consume the verb's response (which carries the derived `published` boolean) to flip local entry visibility in place — no resetAndFetch round-trip. PATCH-visibility stays ONLY for the arbitrary unlisted-direct edit (§4.5). Surface a single segmented Public/Private control (glass-ui Switch or a two-state Toggle) on the /v/:slug owner header bound to entry.visibility; the control's idempotent in-place semantics mirror the endpoint exactly (re-publish never duplicates). This retires the PATCH shim with no legacy fallback.
findings.wave_hint: M-W1 (wire-the-verbs; also satisfies the J.W6 §D e2e publish/unpublish-no-duplicate gate so J can close)

findings.title: remix flow: no fork action exists — the most-forked sort writer is still unwired client-side
findings.evidence: backend POST /api/visualizations/{slug}/remix (visualizations.py remix_visualization ~line 490, fork+atom-diff+fork_count bump); api.ts has NO remixVisualization; gallery.ts has no remix action; cursors.py:21 sorts most-forked by fork_count which only the unwired remix endpoint writes; J.W1-crud-remix.md §5 consumer-1 names 'the gallery card → remix action'
findings.current_state: The remix WRITE side is the literal CORE of J (the audit's 'genuinely-new persisted shape' VisualizationVersion with atom_diff). Server-side it is complete and tested, but no client path forks a viz, so fork_count is never incremented in practice and the most-forked gallery sort remains a phantom from the user's seat. VisualizationRemix accepts atom overrides (active_bases, n_harmonics, contour_settings, animation_settings, palette_slug tri-state) and rejects a no-op with 422 urn:contract:remix-noop.
findings.proposed: Add api.ts: remixVisualization(slug, body: VisualizationRemix) → POST `${slug}/remix` with an Idempotency-Key (the create path already wires idempotencyKey through coreFetch). The remix flow is gestalt with the configurator: on /v/:slug a 'Remix' action seeds the workspace store from the source's atoms (the 5 config atoms), the user edits them in the existing controls dock, and 'Save remix' diffs current-vs-source client-side; if nothing changed, disable the button (the 422 noop becomes unreachable by construction, not a swallowed catch) — if changed, POST /remix and route to the new child's /v/:childSlug. The child is born draft (J.W1c §4), so the publish control (A3-01) is the natural next step — remix-creates-the-row, publish-flips-the-flag compose visibly. Surface the 422 remix-noop, were it ever hit, as a :user-invalid-style inline state via glass-ui useUserInvalidAria (already in /dom), never a toast-and-forget.
findings.wave_hint: M-W2 (remix flow; pairs with J.W6 §D remix e2e + fork_count-write-back assertion → unblocks J close)

findings.title: diff-viewer: GET /diff has no consumer — paint the atom-diff via glass-ui useTextHighlight (CSS Custom Highlight)
findings.evidence: backend GET /api/visualizations/{slug}/diff (visualizations.py get_diff ~line 800) returns {from_hash,to_hash,ops,identical}; DiffResponse twin exists web/src/lib/types.ts:292; NO diff api caller; J.W1-crud-remix.md §5 consumer-2 + J.WC-frontend-grand-audit.md §F mandate CSS Custom Highlight; glass-ui 4.0 ships useTextHighlight at src/composables/motion/useTextHighlight.ts (export '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion'), multi-instance-safe + readonly `supported` flag
findings.current_state: The diff endpoint emits the canonical atom-op envelope (op ∈ added/removed/changed; atom_key ∈ the 5 closed config atoms; before/after opaque). No client reads it. The design names the diff render as the prime consumer of glass-ui's CSS Custom Highlight composable, but the W1 audit pinned useTextHighlight to glass-ui 3.2.0 on /dom — in shipped 4.0.0 it lives on /motion (re-exported at the root index). The composable paints Range sets under a named Highlight styled by ::highlight(<name>), no wrapper spans.
findings.proposed: Add api.ts: getDiff(slug, {from?, to?}) → GET `${slug}/diff` with If-None-Match support (the endpoint is immutable, Cache-Control public max-age 1y, ETag `<from>:<to>`); pass the captured ETag back as If-None-Match to ride the 304. Build a DiffViewer.vue inside the /v/:slug detail: it renders the 5 config atoms in the same panel layout as the configurator, then for each AtomOp acquires a named highlight ('viz-diff-changed' | '-added' | '-removed') via useTextHighlight from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion' and sets Ranges over the changed atom's row. ::highlight(viz-diff-changed) is a value.js-toned colour pop (within proportion, per the design language). For a 'changed' contour_settings/animation_settings sub-object, field-diff it client-side (J-diff-shape §F F-06 declares whole-atom replace at the wire, field-level highlight is the client's job) and highlight only the moved sub-fields. The composable's `supported` flag is the inv-29 floor: when CSS.highlights is absent, fall through to a static added/removed/changed text label per atom (no <mark> wrapper, no !important). The diff highlights are programmatically reachable text, so the diff is screen-reader-legible (axe-clean, the §F mandate), not a pure colour diff.
findings.wave_hint: M-W3 (diff-viewer; the J.WC §F axe gate consumer)

findings.title: provenance breadcrumb: the cross-viz fork_of trail has a twin and an endpoint but no header consumer
findings.evidence: backend GET /api/visualizations/{slug}/provenance (visualizations.py get_provenance ~line 730) returns {chain: ProvenanceNode[], fork_breadcrumb: ForkCrumb[]}; ProvenanceResponse/ForkCrumb twins web/src/lib/types.ts:313-340; NO provenance api caller; J.W1-crud-remix.md §5 consumer-3 + F-03 name 'remixed from → … → original' in the viz header
findings.current_state: The endpoint returns TWO distinct walks (F-03): the within-viz version chain and the cross-viz fork_of ancestry breadcrumb, each ≤50 and cycle-guarded, and the response is ETag-able. Nothing renders either. The VisualizationView /v/:slug detail shows no lineage; a forked viz looks identical to an original even though fork_of/fork_of_hash are populated on the row.
findings.proposed: Add api.ts: getProvenance(slug) → GET `${slug}/provenance` (ETag-cached). Add a fork/provenance Pinia slice (or extend gallery.ts) holding the breadcrumb + chain keyed by slug. Render a ProvenanceBreadcrumb.vue in the /v/:slug header: the fork_breadcrumb as a horizontal 'remixed from {original} → … → this' trail of glass-ui Badge/Button links (each crumb routes to /v/{crumb.slug}), the original pinned at the head. Only render when fork_breadcrumb.length > 1 (an original shows nothing — no empty chrome). The breadcrumb is the natural sibling of the forks count: pair it with a 'N remixes' affordance that opens the children list (A3-05). Reduced-motion-honoured: crumb hover is a token-driven tint, not a transform spring.
findings.wave_hint: M-W3 (provenance header; pairs with the diff-viewer on the same detail surface)

findings.title: version timeline + forks list: /versions and /forks are unconsumed (the within-viz chain and the children list)
findings.evidence: backend GET /api/visualizations/{slug}/versions (list_versions ~line 860) returns VersionsResponse{viz_slug, versions: VersionEntry[]}; GET /{slug}/forks (list_forks ~line 690) cursor-paginated children; VersionsResponse/VersionEntry twins types.ts:325-340; NO versions/forks api caller
findings.current_state: The within-viz depth-ordered version chain (each VersionEntry carries its atom_diff) and the cross-viz public children list both answer, with twins typed, but neither has a reader. The version chain is the substrate a 'compare any two versions' diff would walk; the forks list is the most-forked sort's drill-down.
findings.proposed: Add api.ts: listVersions(slug) → GET `${slug}/versions` (≤50, no cursor — F-11) and listForks(slug, {limit,sort,cursor}) → GET `${slug}/forks` (reuse the same cursor-envelope shape as listVisualizations; the gallery's processInChunks scheduler floor applies). On /v/:slug render a VersionTimeline.vue: a depth-ordered list where each entry shows its atom_diff op-count and, on select, drives the DiffViewer (A3-03) by passing the entry's set_hash as `from`. Render a 'Remixes (fork_count)' disclosure that lazily lists /forks children as small GalleryCard tiles linking to each /v/{childSlug}. Both are read-only, ETag-friendly, and are the named drill-down consumers that make fork_count and the version chain non-phantom from the UI. Keep the timeline single-parent LINEAR (no DAG affordance) — the spec forbids merge/rebase, so the UI must not imply it.
findings.wave_hint: M-W4 (version timeline + forks drill-down; lowest-risk, builds on A3-03/04)

findings.title: No /v/:slug detail host for the J surfaces — the remix/diff/provenance/versions consumers have no page to live on
findings.evidence: router/index.ts:58 maps /v/:visualizationSlug → VisualizationView.vue (shared with /w workspace); VisualizationView.vue:105-118 has only a publish handler; GalleryCardModal.vue (gallery/GalleryCardModal.vue) emits only like/open-visualizer/set-tier — no remix/provenance/diff/version affordance; GalleryCard.vue likewise
findings.current_state: The /v/:slug route reuses the workspace component and exposes only Publish. The gallery card + modal are read-only previews. There is no surface that composes the four read consumers (provenance breadcrumb, version timeline, diff-viewer, forks list) plus the two write actions (remix, publish/unpublish) into one coherent owner/visitor view. Without it, each finding A3-01..05 is a component with no home.
findings.proposed: Make /v/:visualizationSlug a true detail surface (it already has the route + slug param). The owner sees the publish/unpublish control (A3-01) + a Remix action (A3-02); any visitor sees the provenance breadcrumb (A3-04), version timeline + diff-viewer (A3-03/05), and the forks disclosure. Architect it as a thin VisualizationDetail.vue that mounts the existing canvas renderer plus a right-hand 'lineage rail' (consistent with the J.WC §A authoring-rail-LEFT mandate — lineage is read-side, so it takes the right). The gallery card's 'open' deep-links here; a cross-page View Transition (the J.WC §E1 leaf, glass-ui View-Transitions) animates card→detail. This is the single host that converts substrate into product and is the page the J.W6 e2e drives. No new route needed — only the component's role widens; the workspace/authoring path keeps its own VisualizationView.
findings.wave_hint: M-W1 (the host scaffold lands first; the four read consumers + remix mount onto it across W2-W4)

findings.title: like() is a pure local optimistic bump with no endpoint — a latent inv-15 inversion (consumer with no substrate)
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/gallery.ts:191-200 like() does an in-memory +1 only, comment 'no dedicated toggle endpoint under the CRUD shape'
findings.current_state: This is the mirror of the J gap: a CONSUMER (the heart control) with no substrate. The like never persists; a refresh loses it and likes-sort is meaningless. It is out of the J CORE charge but is the same inv-15 disease (substrate/consumer mismatch) and should be named so it is booked, not silently tolerated.
findings.proposed: Either (a) book a POST /:slug/like idempotent counter endpoint (mirrors the publish verb's in-place $inc with an Idempotency-Key + liked_ips de-dup the model already carries) and wire api.likeVisualization, OR (b) remove the like affordance until the substrate exists (no dead optimistic UI). Given the design language favours real interaction, (a): the endpoint is a 6-line $inc/$addToSet over the existing liked_ips field the model already strips in _public_doc. Out of M's CORE; book it as a residual with an owner.
findings.wave_hint: M-residual (booked, not in CORE; or a thin M-W4 add-on if the endpoint lands)

findings.title: workspace publish path bypasses the verb too — createSnapshot→PATCH instead of save-draft→POST /publish
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:108-116 handlePublish() → store.createSnapshot() then gallery.publish(snapshot.slug,...) (the PATCH path of A3-01); workspace.ts:341 saveVisualization() creates a draft, comment 'publish path then lifts draft→public via ETag-guarded PATCH'; gallery.ts publishDraft() (line 240) creates directly at public via POST /visualizations
findings.current_state: There are two publish lineages and both avoid the verb: the workspace authoring path PATCHes a freshly-created draft to public, and publishDraft() creates straight at public. Neither exercises POST /:slug/publish, so the verb's idempotent in-place guarantee is untested from the real authoring flow.
findings.proposed: Unify on: saveVisualization() always creates the draft (already does), then handlePublish() calls the new publishVisualization(slug, etag) verb (A3-01). Delete publishDraft()'s create-at-public shortcut OR keep it strictly for the first-publish-of-a-never-saved-draft case where there is no slug yet — but once a draft slug exists, publish is always the verb. This removes the second PATCH lineage with no fallback and makes the authoring flow drive the same endpoint the e2e asserts. The 'create-then-publish' two-step is honest (draft is a real, recoverable state) and matches remix-then-publish (A3-02).
findings.wave_hint: M-W1 (folds into the A3-01 verb wiring)

glassui_asks.name: useTextHighlight export-path + version doc correction (no code change needed — adoption-ledger fix)
glassui_asks.what: fourier's J.WC audit + W1 re-ground recorded useTextHighlight as shipping on glass-ui 3.2.0 at the '/dom' subpath. In shipped glass-ui 4.0.0 it lives at src/composables/motion/useTextHighlight.ts, exported from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion' (and the root index). No glass-ui code change is requested; this is a fourier-side adoption-ledger correction so the diff-viewer (A3-03) imports the real path. Booking it as a glass-ui-facing ask so the constellation ADOPTION-ASKS row reflects the 4.0 reality, not the stale 3.2.0/dom claim.
glassui_asks.why: The diff-viewer (A3-03) is the named consumer-2 of the design; importing from a non-existent '@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom' useTextHighlight would fail the build. The composable's multi-instance contributor registry + readonly `supported` flag are exactly what the inv-29 progressive-enhancement floor needs, so the only blocker is the stale path in fourier's own docs.

glassui_asks.name: A diff-row highlight token convention (optional refinement, not a net-new primitive)
glassui_asks.what: useTextHighlight paints under a name styled by a consumer-authored ::highlight(<name>) rule. The diff-viewer needs three semantic colours (added/removed/changed). Ask: does glass-ui intend to ship a canonical set of semantic highlight tokens (e.g. --glass-highlight-added/-removed/-changed mapped to value.js diff hues) so consumers don't each invent ::highlight colours and drift? If yes, the diff-viewer binds to them; if no, fourier defines them locally (no blocker either way).
glassui_asks.why: Three repos will eventually paint diffs (fourier viz-config, value.js palette stops, any future). A shared semantic-highlight token trio would keep the colour language consistent (value.js is the colour authority) and avoid each consumer hard-coding ::highlight colours. Low priority — fourier can define locally and book the token-unification as an ADOPTION-ASK if glass-ui declines.

open_questions: Should the /v/:slug detail be a distinct VisualizationDetail.vue or should VisualizationView.vue grow a mode prop? The route already shares the component with /w; widening the component risks the workspace authoring rail colliding with the read-side lineage rail. A clean split (authoring=VisualizationView, lineage=VisualizationDetail) is cleaner but adds a component — confirm the M wave wants the split.

The diff-viewer's default /diff (no `from`) returns only the recorded remix delta (fork_of_hash→HEAD) or `identical` for an original. Compare-any-two-versions needs the version timeline to pass an on-chain `from` set_hash. Confirm the within-viz chain actually has >1 version in practice — today every viz is born depth-0 and remix creates a NEW viz (not a new version on the same viz), so /versions may only ever return one entry per viz. If so, the VersionTimeline (A3-05) collapses to a single node and the diff-viewer's only real comparison is the cross-viz fork delta — which changes whether A3-05's timeline earns its keep.

like() (A3-07): does the product want persistent likes at all, or is the optimistic local bump acceptable as a deliberate ephemeral affordance? This decides whether to book the endpoint or remove the heart.

A4.dimension: A4 — K-deploy spine coherence (the months-class babb.dev API deploy outage + observability floor)
A4.verdict: The K-deploy charter's root-cause diagnosis is CORRECT and the proposed spine (container HEALTHCHECK + depends_on:service_healthy + fail-closed green-CI gate + paging sink + inv-31) is the right idiomatic shape — but NONE of it is built yet, and the chronic has gotten WORSE since authoring (host now 44 commits behind, not 29; K.md still says 29). I confirm the two structural blind-spots at code level: (1) backend liveness is invisible to Docker — there is no HEALTHCHECK on backend/frontend/nginx (only mongo has one), and the FastAPI lifespan `await connect_db()` serially builds ~35 indexes BEFORE `/api/health` can answer, so nginx proxies to a not-yet-live backend during a cold WORKERS=1 start that easily exceeds the 60s blind poll; (2) the rollback is silent — neither scripts/deploy-hook.sh nor the deploy template emits any off-host notification, and the API webhook arm has no green-CI gate, so a red SHA still attempts a deploy. The fix must NOT be a longer blind poll. One re-grounding note: K.md's W1 bump to glass-ui ^3.2.0 is itself now stale (glass-ui is 4.0.0); the deploy spine waves W2-W4 are version-independent and should not wait on the bump's exact target.

findings.title: No container HEALTHCHECK on backend/frontend/nginx — Docker cannot know the app is live
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.prod.yml: HEALTHCHECK present ONLY on mongo (docker-compose.yml:44, prod:116). backend, frontend, nginx have NONE. api/Dockerfile production stage ends `CMD ["sh","-c","uv run --no-sync uvicorn api.main:app ... --workers ${WORKERS}"]` with no HEALTHCHECK. nginx depends_on: [backend, frontend] (docker-compose.yml:141) is bare, NOT condition: service_healthy.
findings.current_state: nginx starts as soon as backend+frontend containers START (not when they are LIVE). The deploy-hook health_gate (scripts/deploy-hook.sh:82-96) is the ONLY liveness signal, polling nginx:8100 from outside. Docker itself reports every service 'Up' the instant the process spawns, even while the backend is still building indexes and cannot serve /api/health.
findings.proposed: Add a real HEALTHCHECK to the backend production stage (curl/python one-liner GET localhost:8000/api/health, interval 5s, timeout 3s, retries 12, start_period 60s) and to nginx (GET 127.0.0.1:80/api/health through the proxy). Then make nginx `depends_on: backend: condition: service_healthy` and `frontend: condition: service_started`. The deploy-hook then waits on docker compose health, not a blind external poll. This is the idiomatic 'wait on health, not on a sleep' fix the charter names — and it lets `restart: unless-stopped` + health interact correctly (an unhealthy backend never gets proxied to).

findings.title: FastAPI lifespan blocks /api/health behind ~35 serial index builds — the root cause of the gate timeout
findings.evidence: api/main.py:42 `await connect_db()` runs inside the lifespan BEFORE `yield`. api/services/database.py connect_db() awaits ~35 create_index calls serially (images x4, contours x5, compute_cache, users/sessions, visualizations x14 incl. the new J fork/version indexes, visualization_versions x2, flags x3, admin_audit x2) AFTER a 5-retry ping with 2s*attempt backoff. /api/health (api/main.py:125-127) returns {"status":"ok"} but cannot be SERVED until lifespan startup completes.
findings.current_state: On a cold start the server accepts NO requests until every index is built. A 44-commit jump rebuilds images and cold-starts WORKERS=1 (H.β dropped from WORKERS=4); against an empty-but-fresh prod DB the index creation + connection backoff can exceed the 60s blind gate (GATE_RETRIES=30 * GATE_INTERVAL=2). The gate fails, the deploy-hook rolls back to the old SHA, migrations (which run AFTER the gate at :184-195) never execute. This is exactly why G/H/I/J never landed.
findings.proposed: Split readiness from liveness idiomatically. Either (a) move index creation into an asyncio.create_task that runs AFTER `yield` (the app serves /api/health immediately; indexes build in the background; first queries are correct because create_index is idempotent and Mongo serves reads during build), OR (b) keep the ping in lifespan but move create_index out of the startup-blocking path and gate readiness on a separate /api/ready probe. Pair with A4-01's HEALTHCHECK start_period so Docker tolerates the warm-up. NOT a longer blind GATE_RETRIES — raise that only IF paired with the HEALTHCHECK (charter §8 DECLINE stands).

findings.title: Rollback reaches no off-host sink — the silent-for-months failure mode, structurally unfixed
findings.evidence: grep of scripts/deploy-hook.sh AND deploy/templates/deploy-hook.sh for ntfy|discord|slack|curl -X POST|notify|page = ZERO matches. The three terminal states — DEPLOY OK (:198), ROLLBACK OK (:209), and 'ALERT ... no green target. Manual intervention required.' (:211) — all `log` to stdout only, which goes to journalctl -u webhook on the host. No human is paged.
findings.current_state: A rollback (or the worse no-green-ALERT state) is invisible unless someone SSHes to the host and reads journalctl. This is the F '2-month silent webhook secret' anti-pattern recurring: the deploy has been silently rolling back for months and nobody noticed. The deploy receiver exits non-zero into a log nobody watches.
findings.proposed: Add a `page()` function to deploy-hook.sh that POSTs each terminal state to a constellation-watched sink (ntfy topic / Discord / Slack webhook), URL read from a host-only untracked .env (mirror the HMAC-secret discipline: never committed). Call it on all three terminal branches. Backport the SAME function to deploy/templates/deploy-hook.sh (a new SINK_URL config var, no-op when empty) so every repo inherits it. A rollback must PAGE, not whisper. Verify a real delivery (inv-27 evidence discipline applied to the page).

findings.title: API webhook arm has no green-CI gate — a red-CI SHA still attempts a prod deploy
findings.evidence: scripts/deploy-hook.sh advances via `git fetch origin; git reset --hard origin/master` (:156-157) with NO precondition check. grep for green_ci_gate|commits/<sha>/status|gh api|GITHUB_TOKEN = ZERO. By contrast the SPA arm IS gated: .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml:34-57 is `on: workflow_run [CI] completed` and deploys only when conclusion=='success' && head_branch=='master' && event=='push'. inv-28's API half is BOOKED-not-built (named at H, carried to J/K).
findings.current_state: Asymmetric inv-28: the SPA refuses a red SHA, the API does not. The API deploy-hook will reset --hard to whatever is on origin/master and try to build+gate it, regardless of CI status. The health-gate catches a broken RUNTIME but not a SHA that failed type-check/tests/e2e but happens to boot.
findings.proposed: Add a fail-closed `green_ci_gate()` to deploy-hook.sh that queries GitHub `commits/<sha>/status` (or the checks API) BEFORE `git reset --hard`, using a host-only read-only PAT from the untracked .env. No PAT OR non-success status => refuse (return non-zero), never deploy-anyway. Refuse-to-deploy is the correct safe state, not a punt. Backport to the template (no-op when PAT unset, with a loud one-time warn). The single named human dependency = provisioning the host-only read-only PAT (operator-owned).

B2.verdict: The empty workspace is the app's worst single-screen composition: ~75% of the viewport is a dead, canvas-painted dot-grid with a forlorn ~280px dashed box marooned at center, while the entire control instrument is pinned to a narrow RIGHT rail (DEC-2 reversal target — it belongs LEFT as the authoring rail). The prior audits diagnosed this correctly but assumed a glass-ui 3.2.0 world; the re-ground changes the verb from "wait" to "adopt now" — glass-ui 4.0.0 SHIPS `asideSide="left"` AND `asideWidth` natively, so the entire left-rail flip is a one-prop adoption plus DELETING the three hand-rolled `grid-template-columns` overrides in VisualizationView (lines 322-329) that currently fight the chassis. The deeper sin is that the stage is composed by a 60-line imperative canvas-paint routine (`placeholder.ts`) that re-draws its own grid + dashed box + arrow + Fira-Code text — a bitmap re-implementation of DOM the page already owns — instead of letting a real, generous, audacious DOM dropzone claim the void. Six lenses below; the headline fix is: controls LEFT (one prop), the dropzone claims the stage as a hero (compose-the-void), and the canvas placeholder retires.

findings.title: DEC-2: controls pinned RIGHT over dead stage — flip to LEFT authoring rail via shipped asideSide (one prop, delete 3 overrides)
findings.evidence: workspace-1440x900.png / 1280x800 / 375x667 (rail top-right, ~75% dead stage); VisualizationView.vue:194 `<Configurator scroll-mode="auto">` (no asideSide); VisualizationView.vue:322-329 local `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(320px,360px)` overrides; glass-ui Configurator.vue:86,102,171-183 ships `asideSide` ('left' = grid-column + border-side flip, NO DOM reorder, no a11y regression) + Configurator.vue:95,155-164 ships `asideWidth` token band
findings.current_state: The Configurator renders aside-RIGHT (its default), and VisualizationView re-asserts that with three breakpoint-keyed `grid-template-columns` overrides (1024/1280/1536) that hard-pin stage→col1, controls→col2. The reading order is wrong: the eye lands on a vast empty grid before finding the controls it must act on. The authoring instrument (where you DO things) sits in the periphery; the result surface (where you LOOK) owns the center — inverted for an authoring tool whose first job is 'give me an image'.
findings.proposed: Set `asideSide="left"` on the Configurator (glass-ui 4.0.0 — SHIPPED, the A-3 ask is RESOLVED in-library). DELETE the three `grid-template-columns` overrides at VisualizationView.vue:322-329 entirely and let the chassis own the geometry; replace the bespoke px bands with the shipped `asideWidth` prop (e.g. `:aside-width="['360px','440px']"`) so the rail width tracks the design intent through the platform token, not local CSS. Net: ~12 lines of grid CSS deleted, the rail moves LEFT idiomatically with no DOM reorder. This is the keystone that makes the empty-state read left-rail-primary → stage-secondary, matching the populated state.

findings.title: Compose-the-void: the dropzone must claim the stage as a generous DOM hero — retire the canvas-painted placeholder
findings.evidence: lib/canvas-drawing/placeholder.ts:1-61 (imperative: draws a 40px grid, a `min(280, w*0.6)`×100px dashed roundRect, an arrow glyph, and `"Drag & drop an image here"` in `500 15px 'Fira Code'`); VisualizationView.vue:198 `canvas-clickable` + onCanvasClick (the whole stage is a click-to-upload target but renders NO visible affordance beyond the painted bitmap); workspace-1440x900.png (tiny box lost in a 1000px-wide void)
findings.current_state: The empty stage's entire affordance — grid, dashed box, arrow, copy — is rasterized onto the `<canvas>` by a 60-line draw routine. It is a bitmap re-implementation of DOM the app already has: it cannot use real type rendering (Fira-Code via canvas, not the font stack), cannot animate, cannot host a real button/aria-label, scales the box at a fixed 100px height regardless of the now-huge stage, and forces the misleading 'whole-canvas is clickable' invisible target. The void is unclaimed: 75% emptiness with a marooned 280px box reads as 'broken/empty', not 'invitation'.
findings.proposed: Delete `placeholder.ts` and the canvas-clickable invisible-target path; render the empty state as a real DOM hero that CLAIMS the stage. A `glass-quiet`/`glass-resting` centered dropzone (real `<button>`, real aria-label, real Fira-Code) sized to a generous proportion of the stage (not a fixed 100px), suffused with the design language: large audacious CM-Serif headline ('Drop a shape'), a colourful icon-palette pop on the upload glyph (within proportion), and — gated behind prefers-reduced-motion — a subtle living motion (a slow epicycle ghost tracing, since this IS a Fourier app: the void should hint at what's coming). The page's own grid/paper-texture already supplies the field, so the canvas-painted grid is pure duplication — drop it. The stage becomes the hero invitation, the LEFT rail the secondary source-strip echo.

B3.verdict: The gallery is structurally sound (cursor-paginated InfiniteScroll, content-visibility shipped on cards, glass-ui Dialog modal, debounced search) but design-flat and CORE-blind. It is the named host of the inv-15 consumer gap: the 7 remix/provenance/diff/versions/publish/unpublish endpoints have ZERO api.ts callers, the card carries no provenance/publish-state affordance at all, and `gallery.publish()` still PATCHes `{visibility:'public'}` rather than the idempotent verb. Beyond the J-blocker, the card hierarchy is monotone (every meta row is text-sm/muted-foreground — slug, time, views, likes all the same weight; no audacious typographic anchor, no colourful POP beyond the basis pills), the empty-state CTA is a DEAD link to a non-existent `/visualize` route, and several surfaces hardcode Tailwind-palette colours (`text-amber-400`, `text-red-300`) instead of the tier/semantic tokens. The fix is one M wave (card-as-provenance-object + publish-state ribbon + pops) layered on the J inv-15 wire-up.

findings.title: Card hierarchy is monotone — slug, time, views, likes all text-sm/muted-foreground; no typographic anchor

findings.proposed: Establish a 3-tier card hierarchy: (1) IDENTITY — render entry.title in cm-serif at text-base/font-semibold (fall back to slug only when title is null), the audacious anchor; (2) META — slug+time as a single muted mono caption; (3) STATS — views/likes as glass-ui <MetricCell> or <AnimatedDigit> (4.0 ships both) so counts tick rather than sit static. Lift thumbnail to opacity-100 with a subtle grid-overlay only on hover. The card becomes a typographic object, not a label stack.

findings.title: No publish-state affordance on cards or drafts — public/unlisted/draft is invisible
findings.evidence: GalleryCard.vue renders tier (featured/saved/normal) but never `visibility` (public/unlisted/draft, types.ts:210). GalleryDraftsSection.vue shows drafts in a separate collapsible but a card in the grid gives no signal of its publish state. findings.current_state: Publish state is a backend concept with no front-end affordance. A user viewing their own 'me' listing cannot tell a draft from an unlisted from a public viz at a glance, and cannot flip the flag in place from the card.
findings.proposed: Add a publish-state ribbon/dot to the card top-edge using glass-ui 4.0 <StatusDot> + <HeaderRibbon>: green=public, amber=unlisted, grey=draft. On the owner's own cards, the dot is an in-place toggle calling publish/unpublish (idempotent $set, no duplicate). Expose visibilityFilter as a segmented control in GallerySearchBar (Public / Mine / Drafts) so the 'me' path the store already supports becomes reachable. Tier (curation) and visibility (lifecycle) are orthogonal — render them on opposite card corners so they never compete.

findings.title: Hardcoded Tailwind-palette colours bypass the tier/semantic token system

findings.proposed: Replace every hardcoded Tailwind colour with the existing semantic tokens: featured→var(--tier-featured), destructive→var(--delete)/--destructive, the admin red/green/blue→the status token trio. Pull the admin semantic palette from value.js 0.12.0 (the colour authority) via the --viz-* / palette CSS vars rather than literal Tailwind ramps. One source of colour truth; theme-correct in dark mode.

findings.title: Likes are optimistic-local-only and unbounded — no server toggle, increments forever
findings.evidence: gallery.ts:189-199 like() comment: 'no dedicated toggle endpoint under the CRUD shape — optimistic local bump'; it always sets liked=true and does likes+1 with no de-dup. GalleryView.vue:124-130 tracks likedHashes in a local Set that never persists. A user can like the same card repeatedly within a session (the Set guards the heart fill but not the count bump on each call) and the count never decrements.
findings.current_state: The heart is a fiction — it bumps a local counter, never reaches the server, resets on reload, and has no unlike path. The aria-pressed toggle implies real state that does not exist.
findings.proposed: Either (a) book a real POST /:slug/like toggle endpoint (the honest fix — symmetric with views which DO increment server-side at gallery.ts:201) and make the heart a true optimistic-with-rollback toggle, or (b) if likes are intentionally vanity-only, render them as a static read-only count (no button, no aria-pressed) and remove the like-bounce affordance that promises interactivity. No half-real toggle. Recommend (a) — it completes the social loop the gallery design implies.
findings.wave_hint: M (UI honesty); backend like-endpoint is a J/K residual

findings.title: Search is slug-only — title/tags/description are unsearchable though they exist on the entity
findings.evidence: GallerySearchBar.vue:51 placeholder 'Search by slug...'; gallery.ts listVisualizations params (fetchNextPage:64-69, resetAndFetch:90-94) pass limit/sort/cursor/owner but NEVER searchQuery — the debounced watcher (GalleryView.vue:95-98) calls resetAndFetch() but the query string is dropped on the wire. title/description/tags exist (types.ts:226-228) and are indexable.

Surface tags as filterable chips beside the basis-filter row (tags exist on the entity; the basis filter already proves the chip pattern at GallerySearchBar.vue:112-127). findings.title: Tabs + search + filter-drawer hierarchy is left-aligned and cramped on wide viewports

findings.title: Card lacks animation/motion identity — only a hover-lift; no entrance stagger, no live preview

glassui_asks.name: GalleryCard provenance-cluster primitive
glassui_asks.what: A compact fork/version counter cluster (fork glyph + count, branch glyph + count, optional 'forked from' breadcrumb chip) that reads a {fork_count, version_count, fork_of} shape and renders the canonical provenance affordance. fourier needs it on every gallery card; value.js's palette gallery needs the identical thing (both inherited the fork/version substrate).
glassui_asks.why: The provenance affordance is shared across the constellation's two gallery surfaces (fourier viz + value.js palettes); building it once in glass-ui as a data-driven primitive avoids two divergent hand-rolls and keeps the fork/version visual language uniform. fourier books the ask, does not write glass-ui.

glassui_asks.name: PublishStateDot toggle affordance
glassui_asks.what: A <StatusDot>-derived in-place publish-state control: green=public, amber=unlisted, grey=draft, with an owner-only click that emits a toggle (the idempotent publish/unpublish flip-in-place). Honours prefers-reduced-motion on the state-change pulse.
glassui_asks.why: publish-two-ways (public/private, no-duplicate flip-in-place) is a constellation-wide CRUD idiom (fourier viz, value.js palettes). A shared dot+toggle primitive encodes the lifecycle visual grammar once. StatusDot exists in 4.0 but as a passive indicator; this asks for the interactive owner-toggle variant.

glassui_asks.name: Diff-viewer atom-op renderer
glassui_asks.what: A presentational component that renders a DiffResponse (ops: added/removed/changed over the 5 closed atoms) as a readable added/removed/changed list — the canonical atomdiff visual. Takes the J-diff-shape op vocab; theme-tinted (green add / red remove / amber change via value.js tokens).
glassui_asks.why: fourier and value.js both gained atom-diff in J; the /diff and /versions surfaces need an identical visual on both. A glass-ui atomdiff renderer is the single source of the diff visual language and unblocks J.W6's version-chain UI on both repos.

open_questions: Should the gallery card show entry.title (currently never rendered — slug shown instead) as the primary identity, and is title populated on existing rows or always null (would need a backend backfill / publish-time title prompt)?
Are likes intended to be a real social signal (needs POST /:slug/like toggle) or vanity-only? The store comment says no toggle endpoint exists — this is a product decision that gates B3-06.

Should visibilityFilter (Public/Mine/Drafts) collapse the separate Drafts tab into the Gallery grid via a segmented filter, or stay a distinct tab? The store already supports owner='me' but the UI splits drafts into GalleryDraftsSection — there may be intentional separation.

Does the M-wave card-redesign land BEFORE or AFTER J.W5 wires the inv-15 endpoints? The provenance affordance (B3-01) depends on the api.ts callers existing; the pure-visual hierarchy/pops (B3-03/05/09) do not. Sequencing affects whether M.W-card can ship independently.

B4.verdict: The equation pane is the most math-dense surface in the app yet its typography is the most timid: the hero equation tops out at 1.8em KaTeX inside a 10rem fixed-height clipping card, while the actual subject — the convergence animation — is driven by a hand-rolled rAF cycle-counter and a `Math.sin(performance.now())` shimmer that ignore prefers-reduced-motion entirely. The colour story is a parallel, hard-coded HSL ramp (`spectrumColor`, three notation-pill literals, three tier literals) that bypasses value.js 0.12 and the icon palette the user wants echoed. Glass/grid is honest but rests on two debts: the resurrected `.cartoon-card` dead-class shim and a `variant="default"` Compute button that renders as an opaque black blob against the glass field. This is M-wave territory: a typography-up transposition (audacious display math), a keyframes.js-owned convergence timeline, and a value.js-sourced harmonic spectrum, all proportion-governed and reduced-motion-honoured.

findings.title: Hero equation typography is timid and clipped — the math subject is undersized
findings.evidence: EquationResult.vue:77-86 caps KaTeX at 1.4em (mobile) / 1.8em (≥768px); EquationView.vue:386-390 .eq-card { height: 10rem; overflow: hidden }; screenshots equation-1440x900.png + equation-1280x800.png show f(t)≈3.3/2+Σ floating small in a vast card with dead space above/below.
findings.current_state: The closed-form Fourier series — the literal thesis of the page — renders at 1.8em in a fixed 10rem card that clips overflow. There is abundant empty space the equation does not fill. No display-grade weight, no optical scaling, no audacity. The card is sized to a worst-case tall fraction but the typical equation looks lost.
findings.proposed: Make the equation the hero. Drive KaTeX size from a fluid clamp() tied to card width (e.g. clamp(1.8rem, 4cqi, 3.2rem) via a container query on .eq-card) so the formula grows to fill, capped by proportion. Replace the fixed 10rem + overflow:hidden with a min-height + content-driven height and an honest horizontal scroll only when a single term genuinely overflows. Pair the Σ glyph with a large display-serif treatment. This is the 'large & audacious TYPOGRAPHY, math IS the subject' directive made literal.

findings.title: Convergence animation is a hand-rolled rAF cycle-counter — should be a keyframes.js timeline
findings.evidence: ConvergencePlot.vue:57-75 startLoop/stopLoop with manual loopStartTime/cycle/frac math; line 60-66 ping-pong via `cycle % 2`; lib/harmonics.ts:59-76 harmonicProgress hand-eases with easeInOutSine; golden-shimmer.ts:11-13 goldenShimmerAlpha() = Math.sin(performance.now()/200).
findings.current_state: The signature epicycle/convergence motion — the most important animation on the page — is a bespoke requestAnimationFrame loop computing elapsed/cycle/frac by hand, with a second independent Math.sin() loop for the golden shimmer. Two uncoordinated time sources, no shared clock, no orchestration tier. This is exactly the manual-engine pattern the constellation has been retiring (FLIP→View-Transitions, manual rAF→keyframes.js).
findings.proposed: Transpose the convergence sweep onto keyframes.js 4.2's orchestration tier: a single driving timeline (linear() spring or a keyed progress track) that owns `t`, with per-harmonic staggered windows expressed as orchestration offsets rather than the hand-rolled harmonicProgress slice math. The shimmer becomes a derived `--shimmer` track on the same clock so the two never drift. Canvas draw stays consumer-owned (keyframes is DOM/value-tier), but the time authority and easing move to the engine. Net: one clock, reduced-motion handled at the engine layer, ping-pong as a built-in alternate direction.

findings.title: Auto-play convergence loop ignores prefers-reduced-motion
findings.evidence: ConvergencePlot.vue:323-324 onMounted → playing.value = true; startLoop() unconditionally; the only reduced-motion guard in the file is on the curve-tooltip CSS (line 405-409). The rAF sweep + golden-shimmer.ts oscillation run regardless.
findings.current_state: On mount the plot immediately autoplays an infinite ping-pong animation plus a continuous golden shimmer, with no check of the user's reduced-motion preference. This violates the standing PROPORTION/INP/reduced-motion directive and is an a11y regression: motion-sensitive users get unstoppable canvas motion the instant the page loads.
findings.proposed: Gate autoplay on a useReducedMotion() composable (glass-ui already exposes the media query elsewhere). When reduced-motion is set: render the full converged sum statically at t=1, show the play control as an explicit opt-in, and freeze the shimmer to its base alpha. Fold this into the B4-02 keyframes transposition so the engine honours reduced-motion centrally rather than each consumer re-checking.

findings.title: Harmonic spectrum colour is a hand-rolled HSL ramp, not value.js — bypasses the colour authority
findings.evidence: lib/harmonics.ts:81-88 spectrumColor: hue = (1 - i/(total-1))*300, `hsla(${hue}, 85%, 55%, ${alpha})`; value.js is pinned ^0.10.0 (web/package.json) while 0.12.0 ships locally; only easeInOutSine is imported from value.js (harmonics.ts:5), never its palette/ramp API.
findings.current_state: The per-harmonic curve colours (the literal rainbow of the convergence plot, visible n=1…n=8 in the screenshots) come from a manual 0→300° hue sweep at fixed 85%/55%. It is not theme-aware, not perceptually uniform, and entirely parallel to value.js — the designated colour authority that fourier already depends on. The 'colourful audacious POPS like the icon palette' the user wants are hand-mixed instead of sourced.
findings.proposed: Source the harmonic spectrum from value.js 0.12's palette/ramp API (a perceptually-even hue ramp or a named harmonic palette), theme-reactive like VIZ_COLORS. Bump value.js ^0.10→^0.12 first. The ramp becomes a single source shared by the curve strokes, the legend dots, and the coefficient spectrum panel, so all three agree by construction. This both removes the literal and unlocks more audacious, intentional pops within proportion.

findings.title: Notation-pill and tier colours are duplicated hard-coded HSL literals
findings.evidence: lib/notation.ts:16-18 NOTATION_OPTIONS colours hsl(6,72%,49%)/hsl(224,58%,46%)/hsl(286,46%,47%); TIER_INFO + energyColor (notation.ts:21-52) repeat hsl(142,71%,45%)/hsl(38,92%,50%)/hsl(0,84%,60%) across three places; NotationPills.vue:24 injects them as --pill-color.
findings.current_state: Trig/Exp/Polar pill tints and the Exact/Conjectured/Approximate tier colours plus energyColor's three-band ramp are all raw HSL literals scattered across notation.ts. The green/amber/red energy ramp is duplicated between TIER_INFO and energyColor. None reference the --viz-* token system or value.js.
findings.proposed: Lift these into the token/value.js layer: notation tints become three named accent tokens (or a value.js triad), and the energy/tier ramp becomes a single value.js interpolated scale evaluated once (energyColor(e) returns a sampled point on a green→amber→red value.js ramp). Removes the duplication and makes the pops theme-consistent with the rest of the constellation.

findings.title: Compute button renders as an opaque black blob against the glass field
findings.evidence: FunctionInput.vue:143-151 <Button variant="default"> for Compute; screenshots equation-1440x900.png + equation-375x667.png show a solid black pill dominating the Function card; compute-btn hover (FunctionInput.vue:235-239) only restyles on hover, so the rest state is glass-ui's default primary fill = near-black.
findings.current_state: The single most important action on the page (Compute) uses glass-ui's `default` (primary-fill) variant, which renders as a heavy opaque black bar that visually shouts louder than the math and breaks the glass/grid/light aesthetic. It is the largest, darkest element on the left column at every breakpoint.

The button should feel like a luminous action within the glass field, not an opaque interruption — proportionate prominence via accent + size, not via a black slab.

findings.title: `.cartoon-card` dead-class shim resurrects a removed glass-ui recipe
findings.evidence: style.css:98-111 @utility cartoon-card re-binds the class glass-ui removed at C.W5; comment notes 14 sites / 13 files; the equation pane consumes it at EquationView.vue:230,239,243,251,308, FunctionInput.vue:93,175, EqCoefficientsPanel.vue:12.
findings.current_state: Every card surface on the equation pane (function card, controls card, equation card, convergence card, status banners) depends on a locally-resurrected dead class that glass-ui deliberately deleted. This is exactly the 'no dead classes, no shims' the standing directive forbids — a chronic carried since D.W4.
findings.proposed: Retire the shim by migrating the equation pane's card surfaces onto glass-ui 4.0's current card primitive / glass-surface vocabulary (the same 4.0 class-vocab adoption already in flight via the glass-subtle→glass-quiet rename). Book any missing decoration (the offset-stamp shadow + hover-lift the shim restored) as a glass-ui ask if 4.0 lacks a direct equivalent. This pane is a clean place to pilot the shim's removal.
findings.wave_hint: M (glass wave); coupled to glass-ui 4.0 adoption

findings.title: Legend overlay occludes the harmonic curves at the right edge
findings.evidence: ConvergenceLegend.vue:45-55 .legend-overlay { absolute; top-2 right-2 }; screenshots equation-1440x900 + 1280x800 show the Sum/f(x)/n=1…n=8 legend sitting directly on top of the right portion of the plot where curves pass beneath it.
findings.current_state: The legend is an opaque-ish glass card pinned over the top-right of the canvas, overlapping the very curves it annotates. At 1280 the n=… column covers a meaningful slice of the sum and high harmonics. PAD.right is only 12px (ConvergencePlot.vue:53), so the plot draws full-width under the legend.
findings.proposed: Either reserve gutter for the legend (increase PAD.right to the legend width so curves never pass beneath it), or transpose the legend into an interactive harmonic strip below/beside the plot that doubles as the colour key — turning occlusion into a deliberate, hoverable spectrum rail that pairs with the value.js ramp (B4-04). The hover-to-highlight wiring already exists; this just relocates it out of the data region.

findings.title: Inconsistent independent-variable symbol: equation card uses f(t), the rest uses f(x)
findings.evidence: screenshots show the hero card rendering `f(t) ≈ … cos(nt)`; FunctionInput.vue subtitle/labels use f(x) (CollapsibleSection title="Function" subtitle="f(x)", line 94); ConvergencePlot tooltips render `f(x) = …` (ConvergencePlot.vue:263-264); empty-state copy says f(x) (EquationView.vue:323).
findings.current_state: The backend-emitted LaTeX names the variable t while every fourier-authored label, tooltip and the expression input itself use x. The user reads f(t) in the headline equation but types x*(pi - x) and sees f(x) everywhere else — a small but real semantic incoherence on a page whose whole point is mathematical precision.
findings.proposed: Pick one variable and make it canonical end-to-end. Since the input box and all UI use x, normalise the simplify/compute LaTeX to f(x) (a backend formatting choice in api/routers/equations.py, fourier-owned). One symbol, one story.

findings.title: Per-coefficient hover popover is mouse-only and absolutely positioned, not a glass overlay primitive
findings.evidence: EquationView.vue:249-266 @mousemove/@mouseleave drive useCoeffHover; popover is a hand-placed absolute div (.coeff-popover, EquationView.vue:392-401) positioned by raw left/top px; ConvergencePlot.vue:345-354 curve-tooltip is likewise a manual absolute div positioned by clientX/clientY math.
findings.current_state: Two separate hand-rolled hover popovers (coefficient detail in the equation card, curve detail on the canvas) compute pixel positions manually and respond only to mousemove — no keyboard/focus path, no top-layer anchoring, no collision handling. They duplicate the overlay logic glass-ui 4.0's anchored-popover/top-layer substrate exists to own.
findings.proposed: Re-host both hover surfaces on glass-ui 4.0's anchored overlay primitive (popover + CSS anchor / top-layer), keyed to the hovered coefficient span / nearest curve sample. This gives collision-aware placement, top-layer z-order (no z-index juggling), and a focus/keyboard path for free, retiring two bespoke positioned divs. The canvas case needs an anchor proxy element tracking the cursor; book that as a glass-ui ask if no canvas-anchor pattern exists.

findings.title: Convergence plot grid is flat grey with no mathematical landmarks (no π ticks, no axis labels)

B5.verdict: The morph pane is the single most motion-themed surface in the app — its entire purpose is to author a 3-phase transition (settle-out → cross-fade → settle-in) — yet it is the LEAST glass/motion-suffused pane, and it ships ZERO prefers-reduced-motion handling while 10 sibling components honour it (an a11y/INP regression and a direct breach of the standing PROPORTION directive). The control hierarchy is flat and timing-centric (three identical duration cards) rather than expressing the morph as a single authored motion-curve; the harmonic grid is a cramped horizontal scroller; and the easing vocabulary is value.js polynomials/back-curves only, despite keyframes 4.2 shipping a first-class springTimingFunction + SpringProgress and glass-ui 4.0 shipping useSpring/useSpringPress/useReducedMotion/useViewTransition. The deps are 1–2 majors stale (glass-ui ^3.1 vs 4.0, keyframes ^2.2 vs 4.2), so the morph engine is built on the pre-spring world. This is the highest-leverage pane for the M tranche's motion-language thesis: re-author it as a spring-native, reduced-motion-aware, glass-gridded "motion studio."

findings.title: Morph pane has ZERO prefers-reduced-motion handling — the motion pane is the only one that ignores motion preference
findings.evidence: grep across web/src/components/morph/* and useFourierMorph.ts/useMorphConfig.ts returns no prefers-reduced-motion or useReducedMotion; meanwhile 10 components do honour it (PaperView, ContourSettings, AnimationControls, GalleryMarquee, GalleryCard, CollapsibleSection, ConvergencePlot, DarkModeToggle, VisualizationView, style.css). useFourierMorph.morphTo() unconditionally drives a keyframes Animation across all 3 phases.
findings.current_state: Clicking the morph button always runs the full settle-out/morph/settle-in tween regardless of OS motion preference. The harmonic level animates continuously via rAF-backed keyframes ticks with no static fallback.
findings.proposed: Adopt glass-ui 4.0 useReducedMotion in useFourierMorph: when reduced, morphTo() should snap directly to the target shape at highLevel (single setShape, phase stays idle, no tween) — a true no-motion path, not a shortened one. This is the canonical no-legacy gestalt: the composable owns the preference, the component stays declarative. Pairs with B5-02.
findings.wave_hint: M-wave (motion-language) — first move; also a J-blocking a11y gap

findings.title: Morph engine is pre-spring; easing vocab is value.js polynomials/back only — keyframes 4.2 springTimingFunction + glass-ui useSpring unused
findings.evidence: web/package.json pins keyframes ^2.2.0 (published 4.2.0) and glass-ui ^3.1.0 (published 4.0.0). keyframes 4.2 ships src/animation/spring.ts (SpringProgress, SpringDurationOptions) + springTimingFunction.ts; glass-ui 4.0 ships composables/motion/{useSpring,useSpringPress,useRAFLoop,curves}. lib/easings.ts EASING_PRESETS is built purely from value.js timingFunctions (linear/quad/cubic/sine/expo/circ/back). MorphPhaseConfig easing Select offers only those.
findings.current_state: The morph's three phases each pick a value.js easing from a long flat dropdown. There is no spring option — the most physically natural morph motion (mass/stiffness/damping) is unreachable, despite the engine stack now shipping it natively.
findings.proposed: Bump deps (glass-ui 4.0, keyframes 4.2, value.js 0.12 — re-ground per RUN-BOARD staleness) then add a Spring preset family to lib/easings via keyframes springTimingFunction, surfaced in the easing Select with a live spring-curve thumbnail (reuse the existing easingCurvePath SVG mechanism, render the overshoot). This makes 'morph' physically expressive and is the mathematical-morph motion language the M tranche wants.

findings.title: Control hierarchy is flat & timing-centric: three identical duration cards instead of one authored morph-curve
findings.evidence: FourierMorphDemo.vue:25-55 renders three structurally identical MorphPhaseConfig cards (Settle Out / Morph / Settle In), each a Duration number+slider + Easing select. Screenshot morph-1440x900.png shows three visually undifferentiated cards in a 3-col grid (config-grid, FourierMorphDemo.vue:258-269).
findings.current_state: The user authors the morph as three disconnected scalars. There is no single view of the whole transition timeline; the total (totalMs) only appears as a tiny chip. Nothing visually conveys that these three phases compose one continuous motion.
findings.proposed: Transpose the three cards into a single horizontal MORPH TIMELINE primitive: one track segmented into three proportional spans (widths ∝ ms), each span tinted by its phase accent (red/pink/red already in slider-color), draggable segment boundaries to retime, each segment carrying its easing-curve glyph inline. The grid/MATH directive is served by a real timeline grid; PROPORTION is literal (segment width = duration). Per-phase numeric edit stays as a popover on segment click (glass-ui popover). This is the gestalt control-hierarchy fix.

findings.title: Harmonic-level grid is a cramped horizontal scroller — buries the core MATH idea of the page

findings.proposed: Promote the ladder to a MATH-grid feature: a responsive wrap grid (CSS grid auto-fill, not overflow scroll) with the low↔high band rendered as a tinted range overlay across the selected cells (so the band is legible at a glance), audacious n= labels in the math/mono face, and the active frame popping with a glass highlight + scale. Replace #60a5fa with VIZ_COLORS.chebyshev (already imported) for the bound color. Serves grid + MATH + pops directives.

findings.title: Glass suffusion is near-absent — page leans on the .cartoon-card resurrection shim, not glass surfaces
findings.evidence: Every panel (MorphShapePreview button, all MorphPhaseConfig cards, HarmonicLevelGrid) uses .cartoon-card, a fourier-local @utility shim resurrecting a glass-ui class removed at C.W5 (style.css:98-111). findings.current_state: The most design-forward pane renders as flat cartoon-bordered cards. The 'GLASS' design-language pillar is delivered by a documented stop-gap shim with a standing cross-repo re-publish ask, not by real glass-ui 4.0 surfaces.
findings.proposed: Re-skin the morph surfaces onto glass-ui 4.0's glass surface/overlay substrate (the 4.0 glass card recipe) so the timeline, preview stage, and level grid sit on genuine layered glass — retiring the .cartoon-card shim on this pane (no-legacy). The preview stage especially wants a glass plate so the red morph stroke reads as floating. Book the shim retirement as part of the 4.0 class-vocab adoption already in-flight (the uncommitted glass-subtle→glass-quiet rename).

findings.title: Typography is timid — h1 caps at 2rem; no audacious display on the motion pane

findings.title: Colour pops are monochrome-red; misses the audacious palette directive

findings.title: Hardcoded non-token colours break the design-token discipline

findings.title: Export/Reset buttons are bespoke-styled, not glass-ui Button variants — inconsistent with the rest of the app

Is the 3-phase model (settle-out/morph/settle-in) the right abstraction, or should the M tranche collapse it into a single continuous spring morph where 'low harmonics in the middle' falls out of the curve naturally? The current model is pedagogically explicit but mechanically baroque.
