B7.verdict: The shape-extractor route (/demo/shape-extractor) is a Playwright harness page masquerading as UI: a raw div with inline styles, a `<pre>` tag dumping JSON, a `setTimeout` race, a `document.getElementById` imperative reach, and a `window.__fourierShapeData` global — all hallmarks of a debug scaffolding that was never promoted into the design language of the app it lives inside. It carries zero glass/grid/math vocabulary, no route meta, no navigation context, and renders the two SVG shapes in 200×200 bordered boxes with `1px solid #ccc`. The correct architectural move is a FULL transposition: promote it to a genuine internal tool page that suffuses the glass-card surface language, exposes the pipeline steps as animated stages (sample → contour-extract → Fourier compute), adopts `onMounted` + `nextTick` instead of `setTimeout`, replaces the `document.getElementById` reach with a Vue ref, and strips the `window.__fourierShapeData` global in favour of a Playwright-accessible `data-testid` attribute. The page is not linked from the nav, has no route meta title/description, and is only reachable by direct URL, so it is also missing discoverability context for developers.

findings.title: Route has no meta title/description — Playwright captures it as 'Fourier Analysis' default
findings.evidence: web/src/router/index.ts:108 — shape-extractor route object has no `meta:` key; all other routes carry title+description; the router's `applyRouteMeta` falls through to DEFAULT_TITLE='Fourier Analysis'
findings.current_state: Route object: `{ path: '/demo/shape-extractor', name: 'shape-extractor', component: … }` — no meta.
findings.proposed: Add `meta: { title: 'Shape Extractor — internal tool', description: 'Playwright harness: extracts SVG contour data for sun/moon morph shapes.' }` to the route definition. Optionally add a `robots: 'noindex'` meta tag via a route-guard so search bots never index a raw JSON dump page.

findings.title: Inline styles throughout — bypasses all design tokens
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:2 `style='padding: 2rem'`; :5 `style='display:flex; gap:2rem; margin:2rem 0'`; :129-137 `style='margin-top:1rem; max-height:300px; overflow:auto; font-size:0.75rem'`; :16 and :79 `style='border: 1px solid #ccc'` on the SVG elements — 5 distinct inline style blocks with no token references.
findings.current_state: The entire page layout is authored via imperative `style=` attributes, bypassing `--font-mono`, `--border`, `--card`, `--foreground`, glass-ui surface utilities, and the project's token system entirely.
findings.proposed: Replace every inline style with scoped CSS classes referencing design tokens. The SVG wrapper gets `glass-card` (glass-ui 4.0 — tier-aware surface + cartoon-surface decoration) with `border-color: var(--border)`. The output `<pre>` becomes a scrollable `glass-wash`-surfaced code block using `font-family: var(--font-mono)` and `font-size: var(--text-xs)`. The page container uses `max-width: 56rem; margin-inline: auto; padding: var(--space-8)` referencing Tailwind v4 spacing tokens.

findings.title: `setTimeout(200)` race to await SVG render — brittle and semantically wrong
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:185-190: `onMounted(() => { setTimeout(() => { extractAndOutput(); }, 200); })` — the 200ms hard-coded delay is a betting line, not a signal.
findings.current_state: The auto-extract on mount relies on a blind 200ms `setTimeout` to wait for SVG elements to be painted; this races against paint scheduling and is the primary source of intermittent Playwright capture failures.
findings.proposed: Replace with `onMounted(async () => { await nextTick(); extractAndOutput(); })`. The SVGs are reactive (driven by `computed` sun/moon geometry) and fully present in the DOM after one `nextTick` because they contain no async work — the geometry is computed synchronously. This eliminates the race at its root without a timeout.

findings.title: `document.getElementById('output')` imperative DOM reach instead of Vue ref
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:176: `const el = document.getElementById('output');` — there is no corresponding `ref` on the `<pre id='output'>` element; the component crosses into direct DOM querying for an element it already owns.
findings.current_state: The output `<pre>` is queried by ID rather than by Vue `ref`, breaking the component's reactive contract and making the ID a silent coupling between template and script.
findings.proposed: Add `const outputRef = ref<HTMLPreElement | null>(null)` and `ref='outputRef'` on the `<pre>` element. Replace `document.getElementById('output')` with `outputRef.value`. Remove the `id='output'` attribute entirely — it is only needed because the ref is absent.

findings.title: `window.__fourierShapeData` global — test coupling via ambient global is an antipattern
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:179-180: `// Also put it on window for Playwright to access` / `(window as any).__fourierShapeData = output;` — the cast through `any` and the comment name the intent: this is a test-coupling seam bypassing typed interfaces.
findings.current_state: Shape data is written to an untyped ambient global for Playwright access. No e2e spec currently reads `__fourierShapeData` (grep of web/e2e/*.spec.ts = 0 hits), so the global is dead-but-asserted-to-be-needed, and also invisible to TypeScript.
findings.proposed: If Playwright needs the data, expose it on a typed `data-testid='shape-data-output'` attribute or emit a custom event (`window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fourier:shape-data', { detail: output }))`). If no current e2e spec reads the global (confirmed: 0 grep hits), delete the `window.__fourierShapeData` assignment entirely — the `<pre>` text content is already sufficient for any Playwright `page.evaluate()` that reads `textContent`. The `any` cast is a NO-LEGACY violation regardless.

The morph page (/morph) immediately adjacent uses `var(--font-serif)`, cartoon-card surfaces, and info-chips; the shape-extractor page shares nothing.

findings.title: Two-column SVG layout clips on mobile — Moon SVG partially off-screen at 375px
findings.evidence: shape-extractor-375x667.png: the Moon `<h2>` and SVG are clipped at the right viewport edge. The container uses `display:flex; gap:2rem` with no wrapping, so two 200px SVGs + 2rem gap = ~432px minimum width, exceeding the 375px viewport. The occlusion gate in visual-baseline.spec.ts would flag this as a horizontal overflow.
findings.current_state: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:5: `style='display:flex; gap:2rem; margin:2rem 0'` — flex row with no `flex-wrap`, no `min-width: 0`, and 200px fixed widths on both SVG elements (lines 12-15, 71-76). Mobile clips the second shape.

findings.title: Extract button uses `variant='default'` glass-ui Button with no visual annotation that it auto-fires on mount
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:125-127: `<Button id='extract-btn' variant='default' size='default' @click='extractAndOutput'>Extract Shape Contours</Button>`. The button is redundant (auto-fires in `onMounted`) and un-styled to communicate its secondary/debug role versus a primary user action.
findings.current_state: The button visually presents as a primary CTA (dark fill, `variant='default'`) but auto-fires silently on mount, making the manual trigger a developer escape hatch. There is no loading/done state feedback after extraction.
findings.proposed: Downgrade to `variant='outline'` (secondary visual weight) and add a `copied`/`done` reactive state using `useClipboard` (already imported in `useMorphConfig.ts`) that toggles the label to 'Copied JSON' for 2 seconds after click — same pattern as the morph Export button. Alternatively, if the button is truly Playwright-only, add `aria-hidden='true'` and `tabindex='-1'` to remove it from the a11y tree while keeping it accessible to the test harness via `data-testid='extract-btn'`.

findings.title: Pipeline has no step/stage animation — the three phases (render → extract → dump) are invisible to the user
findings.evidence: The page performs a 3-phase operation (1. SVG geometry computed reactively, 2. `extractContours()` samples path points, 3. JSON serialized to `<pre>`) but presents it as a single button press with no animated stage indicator. The math-pipeline aesthetic of the project (morph's settle-out → morph → settle-in phases; equation's convergence animation) is entirely absent here.
findings.current_state: No pipeline state, no animation, no stage labels. The output appears instantly in a `<pre>` or is blank, with no affordance that a pipeline ran.
findings.proposed: Introduce a reactive `stage: Ref<'idle' | 'extracting' | 'done'>` and animate stage transitions with `@starting-style` (glass-ui 4.0 available, platform-native): each stage label ('Render', 'Extract', 'Serialize') becomes a `glass-wash` chip that illuminates (accent-red border + `color-mix` fill pop) as its stage completes. Use keyframes.js `useSequence` (4.2.0 on local; `^2.2.0` pin covers ≥2.2 which is satisfied by 4.x) for the step cascade — three serial 120ms delays so the pipeline reads as a genuine sequence, not an instant. This is proportion-governed: subtle ANIMATION target, not gaudy.

findings.title: `@mkbabb/glass-ui` pinned at `^3.1.0` — page cannot adopt glass-ui 4.0 primitives (glass-card, glass-wash, veil-surface) until the dep is bumped
findings.evidence: web/package.json: `'@mkbabb/glass-ui': '^3.1.0'`; npm view returns `4.0.0` as latest; glass-ui 4.0 introduced `glass-card` (top ladder rung), `veil-surface`, and the `cartoon-surface` refactor. The `cartoon-card` shim in web/src/style.css:100-110 exists precisely because `^3.1.0` ships the post-C.W5 removal. All findings above that reference glass-ui 4.0 primitives are blocked on this bump.
findings.current_state: The fourier web app is 2 major versions behind the installed glass-ui sibling (3.1.0 → 4.0.0). The `cartoon-card` shim (style.css:100) is a D.W4 stop-gap that was always meant to be retired on a glass-ui bump. The K-deploy charter (K.W4) authorises this bump but was authored against 3.2.0; the actual target is 4.0.0.
findings.proposed: Bump `@mkbabb/glass-ui` to `^4.0.0` (and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` to `^4.0.0`, `@mkbabb/value.js` to `^0.12.0`). Regen `package-lock.json`. Run `vue-tsc --build` + `vite build` to surface breaking changes. After green build: delete the `cartoon-card` shim from `web/src/style.css` (lines 97-110) — the glass-ui 4.0 `cartoon-surface` utility supersedes it at every application site. This is K.W4 with the corrected target version (4.0.0, not 3.2.0).

findings.title: SVG border uses hardcoded `#ccc` — not a design token, breaks in dark mode
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:16: `style='border: 1px solid #ccc'` (Sun SVG); line 79: same for Moon SVG. `#ccc` is `hsl(0 0% 80%)` — near-invisible on dark backgrounds and opaque/heavy on very light backgrounds. Dark mode support is absent here despite the rest of the app having full dark-mode theming via `--border`.
findings.current_state: Both SVG preview boxes use a raw hex color for their border that ignores the `--border` token and produces a fixed-lightness gray in both light and dark modes.
findings.proposed: Move the border to a scoped CSS class: `.shape-preview { border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); }`. The `--border` token is already dark-mode-aware across the project. Combined with SE-06's cartoon-card surface promotion, the border is subsumed into the glass-ui `cartoon-surface` 2px border and can be dropped as a separate declaration.

findings.title: No `content-visibility: auto` on the JSON `<pre>` output — large serialized contour data blocks layout
findings.evidence: FourierShapeExtractor.vue:129-137: the `<pre>` element with `max-height: 300px; overflow: auto` receives the full JSON serialization of sun + moon contours (128 samples × 10+ paths each = tens of kilobytes of text). There is no `content-visibility` or `contain` hint. The Lighthouse performance score would flag this as a layout-cost offscreen element.
findings.current_state: The `<pre>` dumps the entire JSON string as raw text node content into the DOM with no rendering budget hint to the browser. Since it is the only below-fold element, it creates unnecessary layout work on every paint.
findings.proposed: Add `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: 0 12rem` (matching the `max-height`) to the output element's scoped CSS class. This defers off-screen rendering cost until the user scrolls down. The `contain-intrinsic-size` prevents layout shift when the element is skipped. This is the I.γ `content-visibility` pattern already established on the morph page.

findings.title: Page not linked from any navigation surface — developer discoverability is zero
findings.evidence: grep of web/src/components/layout for 'shape-extractor' = 0 hits. The VALID_TABS set in router/index.ts (line 34) does not include '/demo/shape-extractor'. The page is only reachable by typing the URL. The visual-baseline.spec.ts knows the URL only because it is hard-coded there (line 36).
findings.current_state: The route exists and renders but is invisible to any user or developer who has not read the router source or the e2e test. This is intentional (it is an internal tool) but the intentionality is not communicated — there is no `<!-- internal: not linked from nav -->` comment or similar, and future developers may duplicate the tool.
findings.proposed: Add a comment to the route definition: `// Internal Playwright harness — not linked from nav. Direct URL only. Data available via <pre data-testid='shape-data-output'>`. This is a docs-only change costing one line. Optionally add the route to a `DEVELOPER_ROUTES` constant in the router that the nav intentionally skips but the e2e harness can enumerate.

findings.title: Typography: `<h1>` / `<h2>` carry no serif font family — visual register disconnected from every other page
findings.evidence:
shape-extractor-1440x900.png: the `

Shape Extractor (internal tool)

` renders in browser-default sans-serif (system UI), while every other page header in the app uses `var(--font-serif)` (e.g., morph's `.demo-title`: `font-family: var(--font-serif)`, FourierMorphDemo.vue:215). The `

Sun` and `

Moon` also render in default sans.
findings.current_state: FourierShapeExtractor.vue has zero CSS: no `<style>` block. All typographic styling is absent.

Set `h1 { font-family: var(--font-serif); font-weight: 400; font-size: 2rem; color: var(--foreground); margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }` and `h2 { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted-foreground); margin-bottom: 0.375rem; }` — the h2 shape labels read better as monospace metadata (matching info-chip register on the morph page) than as full-weight headings. findings.title: Audacious colour pops absent — accent-red is used on SVG strokes but nowhere in the page chrome
findings.evidence: shape-extractor-1440x900.png: the sun and moon SVG strokes render in red (correct — `stroke='red'` in the template), but the surrounding page chrome is entirely monochrome (black text on white background). Every other page in the app uses `--accent-red`, `--accent-pink`, `--accent-blue` in info chips, active states, and section decorations. The colour palette of the morph sub-system is completely absent from its own tool page.
findings.current_state: The SVG red strokes are isolated colour islands floating in an achromatic layout. The proportion principle (audacious but not gaudy) has room for a border-pop on the active shape or an accent background on the pipeline stage indicators.

After bump: delete the `cartoon-card` shim at web/src/style.css:97-110 — glass-ui 4.0 `cartoon-surface` supersedes it. open_questions: Is `window.__fourierShapeData` intentionally kept as a future Playwright hook even though no current e2e spec reads it (confirmed 0 hits in web/e2e/*.spec.ts)? If yes, it should be typed via a TypeScript `declare global` augmentation and documented; if no, it should be deleted as dead code.

Should `/demo/shape-extractor` be gated behind an environment check (`import.meta.env.DEV`) so it is unreachable in production, or is it intentionally public for inspectability? The current router registers it unconditionally.

The `@mkbabb/pencil-boil` dependency is pinned at `'latest'` in package.json (line 17). This is a non-deterministic pin that will silently drift. What is the intended pinning strategy for pencil-boil relative to glass-ui 4.0 adoption?

The morph page (`/morph`) and the shape-extractor (`/demo/shape-extractor`) share the same `sun.json` / `moon.json` data but via different pathways: morph imports the JSON statically, while the shape-extractor regenerates it via live SVG contour extraction. Should the shape-extractor output be validated against the checked-in JSON files (a golden-file diff assertion) to catch drift when the pencil-boil geometry functions change?

The `extractContours` function in `web/src/lib/svg-contours.ts` uses `getTotalLength()` and `getPointAtLength()` which require a rendered DOM (line 39-46). The `onMounted` + `nextTick` fix (SE-03) assumes the SVG is already laid out; but if the page is ever server-side rendered or tested in a non-browser environment (jsdom), these calls will throw. Is there a guard needed, or is the page permanently browser-only by design?

C1.dimension: C1 — Design-hierarchy system across control panes (title demarcation, spacing rhythm, dividers, internal structure)
C1.verdict: The control panes still speak FIVE dialects against ONE platform instrument — but the world has shifted decisively under the prior (3.1.0-era) audit: glass-ui 4.0.0 has SHIPPED every primitive that audit booked as a glass-ui-ASK. A-1 (inter-row divider) is now the `dividers` prop on ConfiguratorLayer; A-2 (title bound to a token rung) is the `.configurator-section-label` reading `--configurator-section-{size,weight}` plus the section→row→token three-rung label hierarchy; A-3 (asideSide) ships. The density axis ships with a container-style-query companion. So the WHOLE hierarchy system is now ADOPT-ONLY, fourier-local, zero glass-ui asks remaining for the four R-rules — it collapses to one chassis pass + one `^3.1.0→^4.0.0` major bump. The unified system: (1) every pane titled by `ConfiguratorLayer label/sub` — retire CollapsibleSection, the ImageUpload `<h3>` mimic, the morph `config-card-title`, the EquationPanel sans-label; (2) one rhythm = the shipped density axis + the φ ladder (NOT the prior audit's `--space-2/4` — that scale does not exist in glass-ui 4.0.0; the idiomatic axis is `density` + `--space-phi-*`); (3) one divider = the `dividers` prop for inter-row + the `.chassis-divider`/`bezel-line` groove for explicit sub-section boundaries — retire `.advanced-divider`/`.divider-line` and the equation `border-t`; (4) one two-tier altitude rule (one amber primary control per pane, secondary on `glass-quiet`). The biggest single regression is that the equation + morph routes never consume the Configurator chassis at all — they remain hand-rolled `.eq-grid`/`.config-grid` walls of `cartoon-card`s.

findings.title: No unified spacing rhythm — three hand-rolled systems; the shipped density axis sits entirely unused; section-gap ≈ control-gap so grouping reads only from borders

MorphPhaseConfig.vue:134-136 `.config-field margin-bottom 0.75rem` vs `.config-grid` gap 0.625/1rem (FourierMorphDemo.vue:258-271). HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:138,154,162-235 a third 0.5/0.75rem rhythm. findings.title: No two-tier altitude rule — every group reads at one altitude/weight with no entry point; amber primary action is not disciplined to one-per-pane
findings.evidence: equation + morph screenshots are flat walls of equal cards. FunctionInput.vue:143-151 Compute (`variant=default`, .compute-btn amber-on-hover only at :235-238) and :188-197 the Wand2 auto-toggle (.is-auto-active amber `!important` at :250-254) both carry amber emphasis in one pane. Exactly one amber control per pane — equation→Compute, morph→Export, workspace→Image/Decomposition. The remaining non-pane `cartoon-card` uses (status banners, error cards, equation card) should migrate to the canonical glass tier (`glass-quiet`/`glass-resting`/`cartoon-surface` decoration utility that glass-ui still ships) so the resurrected shim can be DELETED from style.css — closing a chronic NO-LEGACY residual. findings.title: The in-flight glass-subtle→glass-quiet rename is a partial-vocabulary touch with no committed bump — risks pinning fourier to a half-migrated 4.0.0 class vocab
findings.evidence: Working tree (uncommitted): 7 web files rename glass-subtle→glass-quiet (EquationModeToggle, ConvergenceLegend, MobileFloatingToc, PaperView, EquationPanel, GallerySearchBar). glass-ui 4.0.0 ladder lives in glass/ladder.css. package.json still pins `^3.1.0` — the rename targets the 4.0.0 vocab but the dep is not bumped, so the classes resolve against the installed 3.1.0 node_modules, not 4.0.0.
findings.current_state: A class-vocab rename is in flight ahead of the dependency bump that defines that vocab — the rename is correct for 4.0.0 but currently dangling against the pinned 3.1.0.
findings.proposed: Fold this rename INTO the M.W1 `^3.1.0→^4.0.0` bump as one atomic changeset — bump the dep, run the full class-vocab sweep (grep all glass-* tier classes against the 4.0.0 ladder), and commit together. Do not land the rename standalone. This keeps fourier's class vocabulary and its glass-ui pin in lockstep, the precondition for every C1 adoption above.
