Confirm the M-wave ordering letter and whether the dep bump (M.W1) should also absorb keyframes.js ^2.2.0→4.2.0 and value.js ^0.10.0→0.12.0, or whether C1 only needs the glass-ui major (the section-label/dividers/density/asideSide are all glass-ui-internal and do not require the keyframes/value bumps to function).

C2.dimension: Visual Incongruence — Cross-Page Surface, Border, Colour, Type, and Shadow Consistency
C2.verdict: The codebase carries at least seven distinct classes of cross-page visual incongruence. The most systemic are: (1) a rampant 1.5 px non-standard border weight (24 sites) that has no counterpart in any Tailwind or glass-ui token; (2) two competing card-surface idioms — `cartoon-card` (13+ sites) and bare `border-2 border-foreground/15 rounded-xl` (4 sites) — that do not converge on a single glass-ui `<Card>` primitive; (3) at least six divergent inline-spinner recipes across four pages with inconsistent size, border-width, and accent token; and (4) `rgba(0,0,0,N)` bespoke box-shadows scattered across 10+ components that bypass the glass-ui `--shadow-*` token family. Secondary clusters: raw `text-red-N` used for error states instead of `--destructive`; raw `border-radius: <rem>` values authored outside the `--radius-*` token ladder; and `transition-all` still alive in ImageUpload.vue. No single page is immune; every route (/, /w, /gallery, /equation, /morph, /paper, /demo/shape-extractor) carries at least one failing.

findings.title: Epidemic 1.5 px border weight — 24 sites, zero token backing
findings.evidence: grep across components/: border: 1.5px (PaperSearch.vue:51,112,258; PaperView.vue:591; BasisSelector.vue:283; SpeedSelect.vue:67; EasingPicker.vue:75; ContourSettings.vue — SelectTrigger border-[1.5px]:211; EquationPanel.vue:108 border-[1.5px]; EquationView.vue:240,285,463; FunctionInput.vue:104,123,135; FrequencyGraph.vue:189; InfoCard.vue:22; ConvergencePlot.vue:396; ConvergenceTimeline.vue:110; GalleryAdminBanner.vue:26; GalleryDraftsSection.vue:51; GalleryCardModal.vue:236; MorphPhaseConfig.vue:170; HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:183,234). 24 total.
findings.current_state: Authors reach for `border: 1.5px solid …` or `border-[1.5px]` everywhere a hairline-but-visible border is wanted. There is no `--border-width-medium` or Tailwind `border-1.5` token; the value is a magic number repeated 24 times across 16 files.
findings.proposed: Define one custom CSS property `--border-w-medium: 1.5px` in style.css (or as a `@theme` entry `--border-medium: 1.5px` so Tailwind emits `border-medium`) and replace all 24 sites. glass-ui's `glass-*` surface ladder already sets its own 1 px glass-border; any surface that overrides border weight is a non-glass hand-rolled surface whose border converges on this single token. This is a single @theme declaration + a find-and-replace pass — no glass-ui ask required.

findings.title: Two-headed card idiom: `cartoon-card` vs bare `border-2 border-foreground/15 rounded-xl`
findings.evidence: `cartoon-card` used at: BasisCanvas.vue:521, ImageUpload.vue:38, ContourPreview.vue:33, VisualizationView.vue:163, GalleryView.vue:312, AdminUserList.vue:308,362, EqCoefficientsPanel.vue:12, EquationView.vue:230,239,243,251,308, InfoCard.vue:18, FunctionInput.vue:93,175, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:2, MorphPhaseConfig.vue:2, MorphShapePreview.vue:4. Bare `border-2 border-foreground/15 rounded-xl` (no cartoon-card) at: GalleryCard.vue:71, GalleryCardModal.vue:73, VisualizationView.vue:169. PaperSidebar.vue:162-165 and PaperView.vue:522-525 use `border-radius: 0.75rem; border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 15%, transparent)` in raw CSS — identical visual intent, third spelling.
findings.current_state: Three spellings produce the same 2 px cartoon-ink card border at 15% foreground opacity + rounded-xl — one is the `cartoon-card` utility (which shims `cartoon-surface` per style.css:107-111), one is inline Tailwind, one is raw CSS. The paper/ components never reach for `cartoon-card` even though they render an identical surface.
findings.proposed: Consolidate. `cartoon-card` is the canonical spelling and should be used at all 3 sites that currently spell the border inline. For the paper article and sidebar specifically, replace the raw CSS border+radius+shadow with `cartoon-card` (the utility already carries the shadow from `cartoon-surface`). Longer term, the `cartoon-card` @utility shim (style.css:107) should be folded as a genuine glass-ui `<Card surface="cartoon">` preset — book as a glass-ui ask.

findings.title: Six divergent inline-spinner recipes across four pages
findings.evidence: EquationPanel.vue:108 — h-4 w-4 border-[1.5px] border-border border-t-primary; VisualizationView.vue:157 — h-8 w-8 border-[2.5px] border-border border-t-primary; EquationView.vue:223 — size-6 border-2 border-border border-t-primary; EquationView.vue:240 — size-3.5 border-[1.5px] border-border border-t-primary; GalleryInfiniteGrid.vue:46, AdminAuditLog.vue:120, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:152, AdminUserList.vue:278 — h-6 w-6 border-2 border-muted-foreground border-t-transparent. Four different sizes (3.5, 4, 6, 8 unit), two different accent strategies (border-t-primary vs border-t-transparent), two different track colors (border-border vs border-muted-foreground).
findings.current_state: No shared spinner primitive. Each author chose independently: size, track color, accent color, and border weight all differ. The gallery admin spinners use `border-muted-foreground / border-t-transparent` while the workspace and equation panels use `border-border / border-t-primary`.
findings.proposed: Extract a single `<SpinnerRing>` component (or `spinner-ring` @utility) that encodes: `rounded-full animate-spin border-2 border-border border-t-primary` as the ONE canonical recipe, with a `size` prop mapping to `h-4 w-4` (sm), `h-6 w-6` (md, default), `h-8 w-8` (lg). All 8 call sites replace their bespoke spinner div with this component. The gallery admin sites align onto `border-t-primary` (not `border-t-transparent`) for consistent accent.

findings.title: Bespoke `rgba(0,0,0,N)` box-shadows bypassing glass-ui `--shadow-*` token family
findings.evidence: MobileFloatingToc.vue:300 `0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`; PaperView.vue:597 `0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)`, :610 `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)`; PaperSearch.vue:114 `0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`, :261-262 `0 8px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)`; EquationPanel.vue:124 `0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)`; GlassTimeline.vue:116 `0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`; GallerySearchBar.vue:182 using `color-mix` but not the shadow token; ConvergencePlot.vue:397 `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)`; EquationView.vue:465 `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)`. AnimationControls.vue:156,181 use multi-layer `rgba` box-shadows.
findings.current_state: Glass-ui ships `--shadow-sm`, `--shadow-md`, `--shadow-lg`, `--shadow-cartoon`, `--shadow-cartoon-hover`, `--shadow-modal` (confirmed by GalleryCard.vue using `var(--shadow-cartoon)` and GalleryCardModal.vue using `var(--shadow-modal)`). 10+ sites ignore these tokens and author bespoke rgba shadows. On dark mode, all these shadows are systematically too strong.
findings.proposed: Map each site to its nearest glass-ui shadow token. The recurring `0 4px 12-16px rgba(0,0,0,0.08-0.12)` pattern matches `--shadow-md`; `0 8px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.14)` matches `--shadow-lg`. Delete the raw rgba values and substitute `box-shadow: var(--shadow-md)` etc. For AnimationControls.vue's play-btn, which intentionally uses multi-layer chromatic glow, the hover state glow (`rgba(200,100,255,…), rgba(100,180,255,…)`) is intentional design; book as a glass-ui `--shadow-glow-rainbow` token ask instead of silencing it.

findings.title: Error states use raw `text-red-400 / border-red-500` instead of `--destructive` semantic token
findings.evidence: EquationPanel.vue:34 `text-red-400` in katex error span; :110 `text-red-400 fira-code` error div; EquationView.vue:243-244 `border-red-500/30 bg-red-500/5 … text-red-400`. ContourSettings.vue correctly uses `var(--destructive)` at :416,437,438. glass-ui exports `--destructive` (confirmed: color-radius.css:100, dark-arm.css:88). The inconsistency is page-scoped: equation page uses `red-400`; workspace page uses `--destructive`.
findings.current_state: Same semantic role (compute / parse error) expressed two different ways. `text-red-400` is a fixed hue that does not adapt to the theme's destructive palette; `var(--destructive)` is the themed canonical. Admin panels (AdminFlaggedPanel, AdminAuditLog, AdminUserList) use `text-red-300/text-red-400` for the destructive-action hover affordance — also below the `--delete` token that GalleryCard correctly uses.
findings.proposed: Replace all `text-red-N / border-red-N / bg-red-N` error-state uses in equation page and EquationPanel.vue with `text-destructive / border-destructive / bg-destructive/10`. For admin panel destructive-action hovers, replace `hover:text-red-400 hover:bg-red-500/10` with `hover:text-delete hover:bg-delete/10` (the `--delete` token is already used correctly at GalleryCard.vue:178).

findings.title: Raw `border-radius: <rem>` values throughout CSS blocks, bypassing `--radius-*` token ladder
findings.evidence: PaperSearch.vue:257 `border-radius: 0.75rem`; PaperView.vue:522 `border-radius: 0.75rem`, :640 `border-radius: 0.375rem`; MobileFloatingToc.vue:243 `border-radius: 0.25rem`, :340 `border-radius: 0.375rem`; PaperSidebar.vue:162 `border-radius: 0.75rem`, :192 `border-radius: 0.25rem`; PaperArticleWindow.vue:183 `border-radius: 0.75rem`; ExportModal.vue:101 `border-radius: 0.375rem`; ContourSettings.vue:415 `border-radius: 0.5rem`, :435 `border-radius: 0.375rem`; BasisSelector.vue:304 `border-radius: 0.25rem`; EasingPicker.vue:74 `border-radius: 0.5rem`; GlassTimeline.vue:115 `border-radius: 0.25rem`; AnimationControls.vue:221 `border-radius: 0.5rem`; GallerySearchBar.vue:150 `border-radius: 0.5rem`, :181 `border-radius: 0.75rem`; EquationView.vue:464 `border-radius: 0.5rem`. Also: PaperSearch.vue uses `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` and `calc(var(--radius) - 4px)` (non-canonical arithmetic against `--radius`).
findings.current_state: Glass-ui 4.0 ships a full `--radius-*` token ladder: `--radius-xs/sm` (4px), `--radius-md` (6px), `--radius-lg = --radius` (0.625rem), `--radius-xl` (12px), `--radius-2xl` (1rem), `--radius-panel` = xl, `--radius-card` = 2xl. The most common raw values observed map: 0.25rem → `--radius-sm`; 0.375rem → between sm and md (no exact token — should round to `--radius-md`); 0.5rem → `--radius-xl` is closest non-trivial; 0.75rem → not exactly any token (between xl=12px and 2xl=16px). The `0.75rem` recurrence (paper article, sidebar, search modal) is the panel/card radius in an older token era.
findings.proposed: Audit each raw value against the glass-ui 4.0 ladder and replace with the nearest semantic token (`var(--radius-sm)`, `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--radius-panel)`, `var(--radius-card)` etc.). For the `0.75rem` group (paper article, sidebar nav, search result list) the correct semantic is `--radius-panel` (= `--radius-xl` = 12px). For `0.25rem` and `0.375rem` small-control radii, use `--radius-sm` or `--radius-md`. The `calc(var(--radius) - 2px/4px)` arithmetic in PaperSearch.vue is fragile and should also resolve to a named rung.

findings.title: Glass surface tier mismatch: `glass-quiet` used as a floating popover (EquationPanel) where `glass-floating` is semantically correct
findings.evidence: EquationPanel.vue:70 `class="eq-panel glass-quiet"` — this is an absolutely positioned overlay panel that floats above the canvas at z-index --z-controls, displaced from the document flow. ConvergenceLegend.vue:17 `class="legend-overlay glass-quiet"` — same: absolute, inside the canvas. MobileFloatingToc.vue:110,117 correctly uses `glass-resting` for the sticky bar and `glass-floating` for the dropdown. GallerySearchBar.vue:80 uses `glass-resting` for the filter drawer.
findings.current_state: The glass ladder's tier semantics are: `glass-quiet` ~0.50α for content within the page flow; `glass-resting` ~0.65α for chrome bars; `glass-floating` ~0.80α for elements that lift above the page surface (popovers, overlays, menus). The equation panel and convergence legend float above the canvas — they are visually brighter overlays but render with the quietest tier, which means on some substrates they read as underweight and potentially fail legibility.
findings.proposed: Promote EquationPanel.vue's `.eq-panel` to `glass-floating`. Promote ConvergenceLegend.vue's `.legend-overlay` to `glass-resting` (it is a persistent legend, not a transient popover — resting is appropriate). The MobileFloatingToc bar correctly uses `glass-resting`; the equation panel overlay should match `glass-floating` as used by the TOC dropdown (MobileFloatingToc.vue:133).

findings.title: `cartoon-card` on non-card elements causes redundant `rounded-lg` override (cartoon-card already sets rounded via cartoon-surface)
findings.evidence: GalleryView.vue:312 `class="cartoon-card … rounded-lg"`, AdminUserList.vue:308 `class="cartoon-card … rounded-lg … shadow-cartoon"`, AdminUserList.vue:362 `class="cartoon-card flex … rounded-lg"`. style.css:107-111 maps `cartoon-card` → `@apply cartoon-surface` (which includes the border-radius from glass-ui's cartoon surface). The extra `rounded-lg` overrides the cartoon surface's radius, creating inconsistency with other cartoon-card usages which accept the surface radius.
findings.current_state: Some cartoon-card sites inject an explicit `rounded-lg` which silently wins over whatever radius glass-ui's `cartoon-surface` sets, while other sites (ContourPreview.vue, EqCoefficientsPanel.vue, FunctionInput.vue, ImageUpload.vue etc.) accept the surface's own radius. This divergence means those three gallery/workspace panels look different from the equation panels despite using the same surface class.
findings.proposed: Remove the explicit `rounded-lg` at GalleryView.vue:312, AdminUserList.vue:308, and AdminUserList.vue:362. Trust the `cartoon-surface` radius. Also remove `shadow-cartoon` at AdminUserList.vue:308 — `cartoon-card` already inherits the shadow from `cartoon-surface` via the style.css shim, so this is a double shadow.

findings.title: `transition-all` still alive in ImageUpload.vue (three violations)
findings.evidence: ImageUpload.vue:53 `transition-all duration-200`; :67 `transition-all duration-300`; :71 `transition-all duration-200`. All other components carry the `A.W3.d` comment and use named-property transitions. CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:91 also has `transition-all duration-500 ease-out` on the bar fill.
findings.current_state: A.W3.d (from Tranche A Wave 3 pass) declared the project standard: named-property transitions only, no `transition-all`. ImageUpload.vue and CoefficientsSpectrum.vue missed the sweep. `transition-all` causes layout and paint to trigger on EVERY property change, which violates the INP budget on paint-heavy canvas pages.
findings.proposed: ImageUpload.vue:53 — replace with `transition-[transform,opacity] duration-200 ease-standard`; :67 — `transition-[opacity,transform] duration-300 ease-standard`; :71 — `transition-[background-color] duration-200 ease-standard`. CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:91 — `transition-[width] duration-500 ease-out`.

findings.title: Paper cluster uses `calc(var(--radius) - 2px/4px)` arithmetic instead of named token rungs
findings.evidence: PaperSearch.vue:52 `border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` (search input wrap), :113 `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` (results list), :128 `calc(var(--radius) - 4px)` (result rows). PaperSidebar.vue:227 `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` (sidebar links). `--radius` = 0.625rem = 10px; minus 2px = 8px = `--radius-xl`; minus 4px = 6px = `--radius-md`.
findings.current_state: The arithmetic resolves to values that already have named glass-ui tokens (`--radius-xl` for -2px, `--radius-md` for -4px) but the code writes the arithmetic instead, making it fragile: if `--radius` changes in the glass-ui theme, the paper search components silently inherit the wrong radius.
findings.proposed: Replace `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` → `var(--radius-xl)` and `calc(var(--radius) - 4px)` → `var(--radius-md)`. These are direct substitutions; the rendered pixel value is identical at the current --radius=0.625rem baseline.

findings.title: HarmonicLevelGrid uses hardcoded `#60a5fa` (blue-400) for bound-slot highlight instead of a token
findings.evidence: HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:203 `border-color: #60a5fa` (focus), :257 `border-color: #60a5fa` (is-bound state), :258 `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px rgba(96,165,250,0.2)`. This is the Tailwind blue-400 hardcoded hex, invisible to the theming layer.
findings.current_state: Every other accent in the morph page uses `var(--accent-red)` or `var(--viz-*)` tokens. The `is-bound` (morph target slot) slot uses a literal hex blue that does not adapt to dark/light mode or any future palette rebrand. The hardcoded `rgba(96,165,250,0.15)` shadow on the focus state is the same problem.
findings.proposed: Add `--accent-blue` alongside `--accent-red` in the Fourier token layer (or consume `--viz-blue` if glass-ui exports one). Replace the three hardcoded instances with `var(--accent-blue)` and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-blue) 15%, transparent)` for the shadow. If `--viz-blue` is available from glass-ui's token export, prefer it over a new local token.

findings.title: ConvergenceLegend dashed `border: 2px dashed rgba(180,180,180,0.6)` for the original-function dot is light-mode only
findings.evidence: ConvergenceLegend.vue:83 `.legend-dot--dashed { background: transparent; border: 2px dashed rgba(180,180,180,0.6); }`. The fixed grey rgba is 180/255 = 71% lightness — invisible on a dark glass-quiet surface and oversaturated against a light background.
findings.current_state: All other dots in the legend use `background: <token>` or `var(--viz-amber)`. This one dot alone uses a literal grey that does not adapt to theme. On the dark canvas, rgba(180,180,180,0.6) renders as a mid-grey dashed ring that disappears into the glass-quiet surface.
findings.proposed: Replace with `border: 2px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--muted-foreground) 60%, transparent)` — the muted-foreground token is already used for legend text and adapts correctly to both modes.

findings.title: GalleryDraftsSection uses `border-[1.5px] border-foreground/8` while GalleryCard uses `border-2 border-foreground/15` — same semantic level, different weight and opacity
findings.evidence: GalleryDraftsSection.vue:51 `rounded-lg border-[1.5px] border-foreground/8`; GalleryCard.vue:71 `border-2 border-foreground/15`. Both are first-level containers in the gallery tab. The drafts section border is lighter and thinner; the card is heavier and denser — creating a visual hierarchy inversion (the card, which is a sub-item, reads as more prominent than the drafts section container).
findings.current_state: No consistent token for gallery-tier border. Two sites in the same page use divergent border recipes. The drafts container should read as a section-level wrapper (heavier) while the card reads as an item (lighter), but the values are inverted.
findings.proposed: Align the drafts section container to `border-[1.5px] border-foreground/15` (increase opacity to match card level, as a section container) and introduce C2-01's `border-medium` token at both sites for the weight. Or rethink: use `glass-card` (glass-ui Card primitive) for the drafts container, which provides the correct section-tier surface without bespoke border recipes.

findings.title: PaperSearch.vue hand-rolls a search input field + results dropdown instead of consuming glass-ui `<Input>` + `<Command>` / `<Popover>`
findings.evidence: PaperSearch.vue:47-116 — full hand-rolled input, icon, close button, result list with bespoke `.paper-search-input-wrap`, `.paper-search-results` CSS (border, border-radius using calc(--radius), 1.5px border, rgba shadow, custom focus-within rule). glass-ui ships `<Input>` (glass surface, focus ring, border from `--glass-border-*`) and `<Command>` (searchable list with keyboard nav). The hand-rolled version lacks the glass surface adaptation, uses the fragile calc(-2px) radius, and the rgba shadow (finding C2-04).
findings.current_state: The search bar has all the visual-inconsistency problems in one component: 1.5px border, calc(--radius) arithmetic, rgba box-shadow, non-glass surface. It also means any future glass-ui form update (e.g. the new --glass-border-resting transition on focus) does not propagate here.
findings.proposed: Transpose to glass-ui `<Input>` for the search field and either `<Command>` or `<Popover>` + `<CommandList>` for the results. The `variant="ghost"` close button already uses glass-ui Button — wiring the input is a one-step alignment. This retires the entire bespoke CSS block (lines 47-116 of PaperSearch.vue styles) in favour of the glass ladder's native form surface.

glassui_asks.name: shadow-glow-rainbow token
glassui_asks.what: A `--shadow-glow-rainbow` custom property (or a `@utility shadow-glow-rainbow` class) that encodes the chromatic multi-layer glow used by AnimationControls.vue's play-btn hover state: `0 4px 20px rgba(200,100,255,0.2), 0 2px 12px rgba(100,180,255,0.15)`. The play-button is the highest-energy UI element in the app; its hover state is intentional audacious design and deserves a named, themeable token rather than hardcoded rgba.
glassui_asks.why: The current rgba values do not adapt to dark/light mode and cannot be tuned from a single override point. A glass-ui token allows fourier (and speedtest, words) to share the chromatic glow recipe without re-authoring the rgba stack.

glassui_asks.name: cartoon-card as a Card `surface` preset
glassui_asks.what: Promote the `cartoon-card` pattern to a first-class `<Card surface="cartoon">` variant in glass-ui's Card primitive, so the 2px-border + offset-stamp-shadow recipe is owned upstream, not shimmed locally via fourier's style.css:107-111.
glassui_asks.why: The shim (style.css:107) is a stop-gap documented as such. Thirteen fourier files and at least two sibling repos (speedtest, words) consume the cartoon surface idiom. Making it a first-class Card variant retires the shim and ensures the border weight, background token, and shadow evolve together under one version.

open_questions: Should `--accent-blue` be introduced as a local fourier token (mirroring `--accent-red`) or is a viz-palette slot `--viz-blue` more appropriate — does glass-ui ship such a token in 4.0?

The `0.75rem` border-radius group (paper article, sidebar nav, search results modal) does not map cleanly to any single glass-ui 4.0 token (`--radius-xl` = 12px, `--radius-2xl` = 16px; 0.75rem = 12px = --radius-xl). Confirm: should these sites migrate to `var(--radius-panel)` (= `var(--radius-xl)`)? Need the glass-ui 4.0 designer intent for document/article containers.

The `eq-toggle` (EquationModeToggle.vue) wraps two ghost buttons in a `glass-quiet` pill with `border-radius: 9999px; overflow: hidden`. This mimics a SegmentedControl but is not using glass-ui's SegmentedTabs primitive. Is SegmentedTabs the correct replacement in glass-ui 4.0, and does it support icon-only content?

C3.dimension: C3 — Glass design-language suffusion (style.css glass utilities + glass-ui 4.0 glass primitives; depth hierarchy)
C3.verdict: fourier's glass story is incoherent against glass-ui 4.0 because the entire web tree is still authored to a pre-4.0 (≈v0.7/v0.8) class vocabulary that 4.0 renamed and restructured. The in-flight uncommitted rename `glass-subtle→glass-quiet` is itself WRONG (subtle's 4.0 successor is `glass-wash`, the ~0.30α rung — the rename over-weights every touched overlay by a full rung) and is also incomplete (it leaves `glass-elevated`, a class glass-ui 4.0 DELETED, live at two sites; leaves `glass-scrubber`, a Slider variant 4.0 never shipped, at ~9 sites). Glass is simultaneously UNDER-applied (the primary content surfaces are all `cartoon-card`/Memphis-sticker, not glass — the home/workspace/equation panels read as paper stickers, no translucency, no specular, no depth) and INCONSISTENTLY hand-rolled (EquationPanel, PaperView, the legend/toggle overlays bolt raw `box-shadow`/`blur(8px)`/`color-mix` recipes onto, or instead of, ladder rungs). 4.0 ships exactly the primitives this needs — the 5-rung `{wash,quiet,resting,floating,overlay}` ladder, the orthogonal `[data-surface]={glass,veil,opaque}` decoration axis, native `cartoon-surface`/`Card surface="cartoon"`, `veil-surface` text-plates, the shipped `GlassTimeline`/`Slider` — making fourier's local shims (the `.cartoon-card` @utility in style.css) and reimplementations dead legacy under the no-shims/no-legacy directive. The right move is a single M wave that retires the v0.8 vocabulary, maps fourier onto a 3-band glass DEPTH hierarchy tied to the design-hierarchy system, and deletes every hand-rolled glass recipe.

findings.title: The uncommitted glass-subtle→glass-quiet rename is semantically wrong — subtle's 4.0 successor is glass-wash, one rung lighter
findings.evidence: git diff (7 files): -glass-subtle +glass-quiet at EquationModeToggle.vue:9, ConvergenceLegend.vue:17, PaperView.vue:393, EquationPanel.vue:70, GallerySearchBar (etc). glass-ui ladder.css:12 documents the rename map explicitly: 'wash ~0.30α + light blur (was `subtle`)' and 'quiet ~0.50α + medium blur (the missing rung)'. tokens/glass.css:137-139 confirm wash≈0.30α, quiet≈0.50α.
findings.current_state: All ~7 touched surfaces were `glass-subtle`. The in-flight rename maps them to `glass-quiet` (~0.50α, medium blur). But glass-ui 4.0 renamed `subtle`→`wash` (~0.30α), and minted `quiet` as a NEW middle rung that never existed in the old vocabulary. So the rename silently promotes every legend/toggle/equation overlay up a full opacity+blur rung — heavier, less translucent glass than authored.
findings.proposed: Map `glass-subtle`→`glass-wash` (the byte-faithful 4.0 successor), not `glass-quiet`. Then make the rung choice INTENTIONAL per the depth hierarchy in C3-08 rather than a blind 1:1 rename — most of these (legend-overlay, eq-toggle) are ambient secondary chrome that belong on `wash`; the equation read-surface (eq-panel) belongs on `quiet`. Author the rename as a vocabulary migration keyed off the ladder.css rename table, not a find/replace.

findings.title: glass-elevated is a DELETED 4.0 class still live at two overlay sites
findings.evidence: PaperSearchDropdown.vue:39 `paper-search-results glass-elevated`; EquationView.vue:261 `coeff-popover glass-elevated`. glass-ui src defines 0 `.glass-elevated` rules (grep: '0 src files'); ladder.css:12 documents 'floating ~0.80α (was `elevated`)'.
findings.current_state: `glass-elevated` no longer exists in glass-ui 4.0 — it was renamed to `glass-floating`. These two surfaces (the paper search dropdown and the coefficient popover) currently get NO glass material at all: the class resolves to nothing, so they fall back to whatever local CSS they carry. The in-flight rename pass missed them (it only touched glass-subtle).
findings.proposed: Re-point both to `glass-floating` (the popover-class rung per Card.vue:24 'floating — popover-class, login surfaces'). Better: a coeff-popover and a search dropdown are anchored overlays — adopt glass-ui's PopoverContent (which already composes `glass-floating veil-surface` via useSurfaceAxis) instead of hand-classing the rung, so the rung tracks the library.

findings.title: glass-scrubber Slider variant does not exist in glass-ui 4.0 — ~9 consumer sites pass a phantom variant
findings.evidence: `variant="glass-scrubber"` at BasisSelector.vue:170,197; EditorControlsDock.vue:117; GlassTimeline.vue:67; SliderControl.vue:83; HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:19,42; MorphPhaseConfig.vue:23; ConvergenceTimeline.vue:71. glass-ui slider/index.ts CVA variants are `standard` (default) + `spectrum` ONLY; grep 'scrubber' in glass-ui src returns 0 Slider-variant hits. Slider.vue:34 falls back to 'standard' for any unknown variant.
findings.current_state: Every fourier slider passes a variant the 4.0 Slider CVA does not define. The Slider silently coerces to `standard`, so the per-instance retint hooks (the `.A.W2.c` retint blocks in 6 files) are styling against a variant that no longer carries `glass-track`/`glass-fill`/`glass-thumb` substrate selectors. These are dead string-keys plus dead `:deep()` retint CSS — exactly the legacy the no-shims directive forbids.
findings.proposed: Drop the `variant="glass-scrubber"` string entirely (it coerces to the default already) and re-express each per-instance accent as a token override (`--slider-range`/`--slider-thumb` custom props on the wrapper) rather than `:deep()` selectors against a phantom variant. Audit whether any site actually wants `spectrum` (the colour-track variant) — the harmonic/morph sliders that paint a colour ramp are candidates. Net: delete ~6 dead retint blocks, keep colour as data via a token, not a variant.

findings.title: The .cartoon-card @utility shim in style.css is now dead legacy — 4.0 ships cartoon-surface + Card surface="cartoon" natively
findings.evidence: style.css:98-111 `@utility cartoon-card { @apply cartoon-surface; ... }` with a D.W4.a comment claiming glass-ui removed the recipe. glass-ui 4.0 SHIPS `cartoon-surface` (cards.css:33, dist/styles/cards.css) AND `Card surface="cartoon"` (Card.vue:54 CardSurface union, Card.vue:179 composes `cartoon-surface`; the retired `<CartoonCard>` was `tier="quiet" surface="cartoon"`). 25 fourier sites still consume `.cartoon-card`.
findings.current_state: The shim was authored in tranche D against a glass-ui that had momentarily removed the recipe. 4.0 re-shipped both `cartoon-surface` (the decoration utility) and the `cartoon` Card surface. The shim now re-binds `--border`/`--card` over a utility that already exists — a redundant local re-implementation of a shipped primitive, plus 25 consumer sites coupled to a fourier-local class instead of the library.
findings.proposed: Delete the `.cartoon-card` @utility from style.css. Migrate the 25 consumers: the structural cards (Image panel, equation control cards, gallery cards) become `<Card surface="cartoon">`; any bare div that just wants the sticker decoration composes `cartoon-surface` directly. This removes a no-legacy violation and re-couples fourier's signature Memphis-sticker look to the library token (`--shadow-cartoon-*`, which 4.0 defines in tokens/shadow.css) so light/dark + hover-lift track upstream.

findings.title: Primary content surfaces are sticker-cards, not glass — the GLASS design language is essentially absent from the main panels
findings.evidence: Screenshots before/workspace-1440x900.png (Image panel = 2px-border offset-shadow sticker), before/equation-1440x900.png (all 5 panels — Function, Controls, Coefficients, equation header, viz frame — are cartoon-cards, zero translucency/specular). fourier imports NO glass-ui surface component (grep: only GlassTimeline-local + useClipboard/Checkbox/Collapsible; no GlassPanel, no Card, no Dialog from @mkbabb/glass-ui).
findings.current_state: glass-ui 4.0 is a liquid-glass library (5-rung ladder, moving specular catch-light, adaptive bright-bucket tint, edge-dispersion rim) and fourier consumes almost none of it on its content surfaces — the panels are flat paper stickers. Glass appears only on transient chrome (legend overlay, search dropdown, mobile TOC). The 'GLASS' design-language pillar is under-applied to the point of absence on the routes users spend time in.
findings.proposed: Establish a 3-band glass depth hierarchy (C3-08) and apply it: the math canvas stays bare (the grid-paper substrate is the backplate), the floating control panels rise to `glass-quiet`/`glass-resting` with the specular catch-light wired (`.glass-specular-track`), and modal/popover chrome to `glass-floating`. Keep the cartoon-sticker register as the DELIBERATE accent for primary CTAs/hero cards (proportional pop) — do not glassify everything. The gestalt: glass for the floating instrument panels over the math grid, sticker for the audacious accents. This is the single highest-leverage suffusion move.

findings.title: Hand-rolled glass recipes bypass the ladder — raw box-shadow/blur/color-mix bolted onto or instead of rungs
findings.evidence: EquationPanel.vue:124 `box-shadow: 0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` on `.eq-panel` (which ALSO composes glass-quiet → double shadow source). PaperView.vue:592-597 `.mobile-toc-trigger` hand-rolls `background: color-mix(--background 92%) + backdrop-filter: blur(8px) + box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08)` (a re-implemented glass-wash). PaperView.vue:524-525, :610 raw rgba shadows. ConvergenceLegend.vue:63-79 hand-mixed fills.
findings.current_state: Several surfaces either (a) compose a ladder rung AND add a conflicting raw drop-shadow (eq-panel), or (b) hand-roll the whole glass material from scratch (mobile-toc-trigger's blur(8px)+color-mix) when a rung would do. These bypass the ladder's under-shadow/rim/grain/specular composition and the adaptive bright-bucket, so they read inconsistently and won't track `--glass-level`/dark-mode retunes.
findings.proposed: Strip the hand-rolled `box-shadow`/`backdrop-filter`/`background` from these surfaces and let the chosen rung own the material. `.eq-panel` keeps only its geometry; the rung supplies the shadow. `.mobile-toc-trigger` becomes `glass-wash` (or `glass-quiet` over text via `[data-over-content="text"]`). Where a surface sits over busy text, use the ladder's `.glass-over-text` modifier rather than a custom drop. One material source per surface — the no-fork rule the library itself enforces.

findings.title: fourier reimplemented GlassTimeline/ScrubberTimeline locally instead of consuming the shipped 4.0 primitives
findings.evidence: Local components/visualization/GlassTimeline.vue, components/equation/convergence/ConvergenceTimeline.vue, components/ui/SliderControl.vue all carry header comments describing a migration FROM `glass-track`/`glass-fill`/`glass-thumb` paints TO `<Slider variant="glass-scrubber">`. glass-ui 4.0 ships custom/timeline/GlassTimeline.vue + ScrubberTimeline.vue (variant="scrubber" default) + the `--timeline-scrubber-*` tokens (scale-paper.css:155-162).
findings.current_state: The animation scrubbers are fourier-local SFCs wrapping a phantom Slider variant, while glass-ui 4.0 ships a real `<GlassTimeline variant="scrubber">` primitive with the exact normalized-0..1 single-track model fourier needs. This is a parallel implementation of a now-shipped component — divergent glass material, no specular, and coupled to the dead `glass-scrubber` string.
findings.proposed: Replace the local GlassTimeline/ConvergenceTimeline wrappers with glass-ui's `<GlassTimeline variant="scrubber">`, threading the play-button + harmonics chrome via its slots. Where fourier needs only a labeled value slider (SliderControl), use `<Slider>` (standard variant) with a token-driven accent. Retire the local SFCs. This collapses three local timeline implementations into the one library primitive and gives them the shipped glass material + specular for free.

findings.title: No glass DEPTH hierarchy tied to the design-hierarchy system — rung choice is ad hoc per surface
findings.evidence: Across the 7 pages, rung assignment is incoherent: floating-toc-bar=glass-resting but floating-toc-dropdown=glass-floating (PaperView/MobileFloatingToc), eq-panel=glass-quiet, legend-overlay=glass-quiet (was subtle), filter-panel=glass-resting (GallerySearchBar:80), search-results=glass-elevated[dead]. No documented mapping from semantic depth → rung. glass-ui Card.vue:18-26 DOES document the intended semantics (wash=hairline chrome, quiet=ambient panels, resting=default content, floating=popover/login, overlay=modal-over-modal).
findings.current_state: There is no fourier-side depth model; each surface picked a rung by feel, several picked dead/wrong rungs. The result is a flat, arbitrary z-language where a secondary toc bar (resting) sits at the same material weight as a primary content panel, and overlays scatter across quiet/floating/elevated with no rule.
findings.proposed: Adopt a 3-band glass depth hierarchy bound to the design-hierarchy system and freeze it as an invariant: BAND 0 substrate = the bare math grid / paper (no glass). BAND 1 in-flow instrument panels (Function/Controls/Coefficients, gallery filter, equation read-surface) = `glass-quiet` for ambient + `glass-resting` for the focused/active panel (rung = focus state, wired with `.glass-specular-track` so focus wakes the catch-light). BAND 2 lifted/anchored chrome (popovers, dropdowns, search results, mobile-toc dropdown, dialogs) = `glass-floating`; true modal-over-modal = `glass-overlay`. Text-bearing overlays compose `veil-surface` (border/rim stripped). Map every existing surface onto this table in one pass; document it in INVARIANTS.md so future surfaces inherit the rule. The depth band, not local taste, picks the rung.

findings.title: Overlay/text-plate surfaces don't use the veil register — boxed glass reads as a dividing line on text plates
findings.evidence: legend-overlay (ConvergenceLegend.vue:17) and overlay-page (PaperView.vue:393) are text-legibility plates over busy backdrops but compose a bordered/rimmed rung (glass-quiet) rather than `veil-surface`. glass-ui surface-axis.css:34-60 + cards.css:50-101 define `veil` precisely for this: '--glass-bg-quiet fill+blur with the box border AND rim STRIPPED (the boxed look reads as a dividing line on a text plate)'. glass-ui PopoverContent/Command/DialogContent all compose veil via useSurfaceAxis.
findings.current_state: fourier's text overlays (the harmonic legend, the paper full-screen overlay-page, the coeff popover) carry the full boxed glass rung — border + rim — over text content, exactly the case glass-ui's veil register was minted to fix. They read as framed boxes floating on the content rather than legibility plates that darken-over and bleed in.
findings.proposed: Switch the text-bearing overlays to the veil register: `glass-quiet veil-surface` (or `<Card surface="veil">` / the anchored glass-ui overlay components which already do this). For the paper overlay-page, optionally enable `--veil-feather` (the radial mask) so the plate bleeds into the page rather than hard-edging. The data overlays (legend with its colour dots) can stay boxed since the box IS the legend chrome — apply veil only where the plate's job is pure text legibility.

findings.title: Adaptive bright-bucket / specular catch-light unused — glass over the bright math canvas can't self-darken and reads inert
findings.evidence: glass-ui ladder.css:115-219 ships the `@container style(--glass-backdrop:light)` bright-bucket (content tiers self-darken over light/near-white backdrops; muted lifts to ink for AA) and material.css:60-236 ships the pointer-anchored moving specular (`--mouse-x/--mouse-y`→`.glass-specular-track`). fourier wires neither: no `--glass-backdrop` on any panel, no `.glass-specular-track`, no `--mouse-*` writes. The math canvas + paper are near-white (screenshots).
findings.current_state: fourier's panels float over a bright cream grid/paper. The content tiers self-engage only the 4% sub-perceptual floor by default; without `--glass-backdrop: light` declared on the panels (or the adaptive auto-engage reaching them) the glass can read washed-out and low-contrast over the bright canvas, and with no specular wiring the glass is static/inert — none of the iOS-26 illuminate-from-within the library is built around.
findings.proposed: On BAND 1 instrument panels, declare `--glass-backdrop: light` (the panels float over the bright canvas — the canonical G2 case) so the adaptive darken + muted-ink lift engage and clear AA. Wire the moving specular on the focused/active panel and on interactive glass controls by composing `.glass-specular-track` and writing `--mouse-x/--mouse-y` on pointermove (a small shared composable — book as an internal util or check if glass-ui exposes a `useSpecular` hook). Honour prefers-reduced-motion (the catch-light intensity is already gated to 0 at rest). This is where the proportional 'illuminate-from-within' pop lives without becoming gaudy.

glassui_asks.name: useSpecular composable (or documented pointer-write contract)
glassui_asks.what: A tiny exported composable that wires a glass surface's `--mouse-x`/`--mouse-y` from pointermove (rAF-throttled, reduced-motion-aware) and composes `.glass-specular-track`, so a consumer gets the moving catch-light with one binding instead of hand-writing the inline-style pointer math. If one already exists internally for the dock controls, just export + document it.
glassui_asks.why: fourier (and any consumer) wants the iOS-26 illuminate-from-within on its focused panels, but the only way today is to manually write the two custom props on pointermove and remember to compose the track class. The material.css recipe is there; the ergonomic wiring is not exported. A one-line composable makes the specular the easy default rather than per-consumer boilerplate.

glassui_asks.name: Slider scrubber/spectrum variant clarity + a single-track timeline export contract
glassui_asks.what: Confirm/document the canonical path for a single-track normalized scrubber: is it `<Slider variant="standard">`, `<GlassTimeline variant="scrubber">`, or `<ScrubberTimeline>`? The three coexist and fourier has all three reimplemented locally against a non-existent `glass-scrubber` variant. A short 'use X for a value slider, Y for a media scrubber' note in the slider/timeline index would let fourier delete its local wrappers with confidence.
glassui_asks.why: fourier carries 3 local timeline SFCs and ~9 phantom `variant="glass-scrubber"` call sites precisely because the pre-4.0 variant name was deprecated without an obvious successor mapping. Pinning the canonical primitive lets fourier collapse onto the library and stop forking.

glassui_asks.name: Depth-hierarchy / rung-semantics doc surfaced for consumers
glassui_asks.what: Surface the rung→semantics table (wash=hairline chrome, quiet=ambient, resting=content, floating=popover, overlay=modal-over-modal) that currently lives only in Card.vue's prop docstring as a top-level design-language note (e.g. a `docs/glass-depth.md` or the ladder.css header). Include the veil/opaque axis and the bright-bucket opt-in.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's incoherent rung assignment (C3-08) stems partly from the semantics being buried in a component prop comment. A consumer-facing depth-hierarchy doc would let downstream apps build their depth model on the library's intended one instead of guessing.

open_questions: Is the uncommitted glass-subtle→glass-quiet rename a deliberate design re-weighting (intentionally heavier glass) or a mechanical misreading of the 4.0 rename map? If deliberate, C3-01 is moot for those sites; if mechanical, it needs reverting to glass-wash. Confirm intent with the author before the M wave codifies it.

Should fourier's signature cartoon-sticker register survive as the primary content-card look, or migrate primary panels to glass with cartoon reserved for hero/CTA accents only? This is the core gestalt call governing C3-04/C3-05/C3-08 — the depth hierarchy is materially different depending on the answer.

Does glass-ui 4.0 already export a specular-wiring composable (used by the dock controls) that fourier can import, or must the pointer-write be hand-rolled per surface? Determines whether C3-10 is a fourier task or a glassui_ask.

The M wave's glass migration interleaves with J's open consumer-gap work (the 7 CORE endpoints with no UI) and K's dep bump (the actual ^3.1.0→4.0.0 version bump that makes all of this real). Confirm ordering: the package.json bump to glass-ui 4.0.0 must land (K) BEFORE the M vocabulary migration, or the migration is authoring against a version not installed.

C4.dimension: GRID DESIGN-LANGUAGE — dot-grid/lattice motif, mathematical chrome vs dead space
C4.verdict: The grid vocabulary is split across four incoherent implementations that never cross-reference or share tokens: a Canvas2D line-grid in the workspace placeholder that reads as dead background noise; a live mathematical coordinate-grid drawn on every populated BasisCanvas frame that is legitimately valuable but visually anemic (rgba(150,150,150,0.09), unthemed); a CSS repeat-linear-gradient grid on the ContourEditorCanvas (28px pitch, themed via color-mix but at 5% opacity — barely perceptible); and an identical CSS grid on the GalleryCard image-frame (16px pitch, 4% opacity — invisible in practice). The two CSS grids are contextually appropriate as engineering-graph-paper chrome but lack identity; the Canvas2D placeholder grid is pure dead space that was already flagged in the D-audit (DA-design-A2-05) and the J-postimpl audit (D4-crosspage-hierarchy:66) without being resolved; and the coordinate-grid on the populated canvas is the one site where a mathematical lattice genuinely reinforces the MATH theme, yet it draws hardcoded anonymous grey instead of resolved CSS tokens, so it flips mode-blindly. No site uses a dot lattice. No grid communicates the project's actual mathematical identity — phase-space coordinate axes, tick-marks at integer multiples of π, unit-circle markers — the things that distinguish a Fourier-analysis canvas from a generic plotting widget.

findings.title: Workspace placeholder grid — dead space, not mathematical chrome
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/placeholder.ts:8-20; workspace-1440x900.png shows the entire ~75% stage as a wall of faint grey lines with a small dashed box floating center — the D-audit (DA-design-A2-05) and J-postimpl control-pane audit (D4-crosspage-hierarchy.md:66) both name this 'dead grid stage'
findings.current_state: drawPlaceholder() paints a pixel-space fixed 40px-pitch orthogonal line grid at rgba(150,150,150,0.07) as pure background fill behind a small dashed upload box. The grid is unscaled (ignores ViewTransform), has no origin, no axes, no axis labels, no mathematical unit annotation — it resembles engineering graph paper drained of meaning. It conveys no Fourier identity and is ignored by the user, yet occupies the dominant viewport area at every cold-open.
findings.proposed: Retire the bare line-grid entirely from the empty state. Replace the placeholder frame with an intentional mathematical scene: draw the unit circle at centre-canvas (r proportional to canvas size), the real and imaginary axes with arrow-tips and 'Re' / 'Im' italic labels (Computer Modern serif, using the font already established in grid.ts:92), and tick marks at ±1, ±i — the phase-plane of the first Fourier component. Overlay the dashed drop-zone box centered on the origin. This repurposes the empty state as a legible mathematical diagram (a 'waiting canvas' that already says something about the subject), rather than dead lines. The result draws at the same cost as the current grid, requires no new dependencies, and the empty-state value-proposition (DA-design-A2-04) is delivered graphically without added text.

findings.title: Canvas coordinate-grid — hardcoded anonymous grey, mode-blind
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/grid.ts:29 strokeStyle='rgba(150,150,150,0.09)'; grid.ts:47 axisColor='rgba(150,150,150,0.25)'; grid.ts:90 labelColor='rgba(150,150,150,0.35)'. The VIZ_COLORS system at web/src/lib/colors.ts:90 already resolves CSS custom properties to hex at mount+theme-toggle; the grid module does not participate.
findings.current_state: All three grid color layers (minor lines, axes, labels) are hardcoded RGBA grey literals that are identical in light and dark mode. On the warm-cream light background (--background ≈ hsl(24 8% 95%)) they are near-invisible (the 0.09 alpha resolves to roughly 1.07:1 contrast). On dark the same values are slightly more visible but still illegible as a mathematical reference frame. The axis labels ('x', 'y') use a hardcoded font string 'italic 13px Computer Modern Serif, Georgia, serif' rather than reading the app-global --font-sans token. The arrowheads are filled with the same axisColor, so they too are mode-blind.
findings.proposed: Extend resolveVizColors() in lib/colors.ts to resolve two additional tokens — '--foreground' (for axis lines + arrowheads) and '--muted-foreground' (for minor lines + labels) — caching them as VIZ_COLORS.foreground and VIZ_COLORS.mutedForeground. In drawGrid(), replace the three hardcoded RGBA strings: minor lines → hexToRgba(VIZ_COLORS.mutedForeground, 0.10); axes → hexToRgba(VIZ_COLORS.foreground, 0.22); labels → hexToRgba(VIZ_COLORS.foreground, 0.32). Replace the font literal with the resolved computed family (readable via getComputedStyle on document.documentElement as is done at colors.ts:23). Add π-tick annotations at ±π, ±2π, ±½π on the X-axis when the data range includes them — a Fourier-specific enhancement that makes the lattice mathematically meaningful rather than generic. This makes the grid mode-aware at near-zero cost, reuses the existing resolution plumbing, and gives the coordinate frame Fourier identity.

findings.title: Placeholder grid and populated grid are disconnected — identity break at load
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/placeholder.ts:10 uses fixed step=40px (screen pixels, ViewTransform-unaware); web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/grid.ts:7-14 uses ~40px target density but computes a data-space 'nice step' respecting scale. When epicycle data loads and drawFrame() replaces drawPlaceholderFrame(), the grid jumps from pixel-space to data-space — different pitch, different scale, sometimes dramatically different visual density.
findings.current_state: The placeholder grid and the live coordinate grid are two independent implementations with different spatial models, different step logics, and now (per C4-G2) different colors. There is no visual continuity between the empty state and the populated state — a jarring layout shift every time data first arrives, since the grid is the only persistent background element.
findings.proposed: Unify both grids under a single drawGrid() call. The placeholder frame should pass a synthetic ViewTransform with scale=1 and cx=cy=0 (so the live grid code runs at its own default density), rather than maintaining a separate pixel-space grid loop. This collapses two implementations to one, eliminates the identity break at load, and means the C4-G2 token fix automatically applies to both states.

findings.title: ContourEditorCanvas CSS grid — correct intent, wrong token discipline and invisible opacity
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/ContourEditorCanvas.vue:292-296: background: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 5%, transparent) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, ...) var(--card); background-size: 28px 28px. The 5% foreground opacity means roughly 0.2:1 contrast on the light background — below any perceptible threshold.
findings.current_state: The editor-shell uses a CSS crosshatch grid at 28px pitch to signal 'drawing surface' for the spline contour editor. The intent is correct (graph-paper chrome for a drawing tool). At 5% foreground opacity, the grid is imperceptible in light mode and barely visible in dark mode — confirmed in shape-extractor-1440x900.png where the editor area appears as a flat off-white plane. The pitch (28px) has no relationship to any design token or mathematical unit. The background-size is hardcoded without a CSS custom property.
findings.proposed: Raise the opacity to 8-10% (color-mix with var(--foreground) 8-10%) to cross the perceptibility floor without becoming overbearing. Expose the pitch as a CSS custom property --contour-grid-pitch defaulting to 24px (a divisor of the canonical 8px base grid) so it can be adjusted per breakpoint. Optionally add a centered crosshair marker (a single 1px hairline cross) at the SVG origin to reinforce the mathematical coordinate identity, drawn as an SVG <line> overlay rather than CSS, since the SVG viewBox is already present at ContourEditorCanvas.vue:231-282.

findings.title: GalleryCard image-frame grid — decorative dead space, indistinguishable from empty
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/gallery/GalleryCard.vue:239-251: background: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 4%, transparent) 1px, transparent 1px) ... var(--muted); background-size: 16px 16px. 4% foreground = ~0.16:1 on light -- sub-perceptible. gallery-1440x900.png (empty state) shows a plain muted background with no visible grid.
findings.current_state: The card image frame uses a 16px CSS crosshatch grid at 4% opacity as a placeholder background when no preview image exists. At 4% opacity this is indistinguishable from a flat muted background. It does not read as graph paper, as mathematical chrome, or as any intentional motif — it is invisible decoration. The pitch (16px) is unrelated to any other grid constant in the codebase (placeholder.ts uses 40px, ContourEditorCanvas uses 28px, grid.ts targets 40px-on-screen).
findings.proposed: Either raise to 7-8% foreground opacity so the grid reads as intentional texture (the ContourEditorCanvas pattern is the right model — it signals 'this is a mathematical surface'), or retire it entirely and replace the empty card frame with a CSS radial-gradient vignette on --muted (already a common idiom for image placeholder states). If retained, align the pitch to a shared CSS custom property (--card-grid-pitch: 20px) declared at the root so all CSS grids share one pitch token.

findings.title: Three separate grid pitch values with no shared token — incoherent lattice language
findings.evidence: placeholder.ts:10 step=40; ContourEditorCanvas.vue:296 background-size: 28px 28px; GalleryCard.vue:250 background-size: 16px 16px. No common token; no mathematical relationship between the three numbers.
findings.current_state: The three grid implementations use pitches of 40px, 28px, and 16px — three arbitrary numbers that share no mathematical relationship to each other, to the 8px Tailwind base grid, or to any Fourier-meaningful interval. The grid language reads as three disconnected decisions rather than one coherent lattice vocabulary. None of the values is exposed as a CSS custom property so they cannot respond to breakpoints or be synchronized.
findings.proposed: Establish one canonical CSS custom property --grid-pitch: 24px at the root (divisible by 8; falls between the current extremes; visually reads as graph-paper at both small and large scale). The ContourEditorCanvas grid background-size adopts --grid-pitch directly. GalleryCard uses calc(var(--grid-pitch) * 0.75) = 18px for the finer card texture. The Canvas2D placeholder and live grid target 'nice step at ~var(--grid-pitch) on screen' (40px is close enough to 24px * 1.5 that the code can stay as-is; the conceptual token is the anchor). This collapses three arbitrary numbers to one named anchor with one fractional variant — the grammar becomes readable.

findings.title: No dot-lattice / tick-mark mathematical identity at any coordinate intersection
findings.evidence: grid.ts draws continuous lines from edge to edge with no intersection markers; placeholder.ts does the same. No site in the codebase draws filled or stroked dots at grid crossings. The 'dot-grid' motif as meaningful mathematical lattice (phase-space points, Fourier series evaluation points) is completely absent.
findings.current_state: Every grid is a pure line grid — horizontal + vertical lines, no intersection markers, no dot lattice. For a Fourier-series visualizer the natural mathematical lattice is not a continuous ruled surface but a set of discrete points: sample points at t = k/N (the DFT evaluation points), or integer multiples of the frequency step in the spectrum. The 'dot-grid' as a design motif would carry mathematical meaning here — each dot is a sampling point, a coefficient index, a basis evaluation — but no grid implementation attempts this.
findings.proposed: In drawGrid() on the main BasisCanvas, at each grid line intersection where the data-space coordinates are mathematically significant (multiples of 1, multiples of π), draw a small filled circle (radius 1.5px) at the color hexToRgba(VIZ_COLORS.foreground, 0.12) instead of (or in addition to) the line crossing. This creates a dot lattice at mathematically relevant positions — the dots ARE the evaluation grid, not arbitrary pixel-pitch divisions. On the equation ConvergencePlot (equation/lib/grid.ts), draw dots at (n, amplitude_n) evaluation points in the background before curves render, reinforcing the 'this is a discrete-to-continuous series' message. These are additive Canvas2D calls within the existing drawGrid/drawPlotGrid functions.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot grid duplicates grid.ts logic in a separate module — split brain
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/lib/grid.ts is an independent implementation of drawPlotGrid() with the same niceStep() logic as the main canvas-drawing/grid.ts:9-14. Both files independently implement 'round step to 2/5/10 × magnitude'. Neither imports the other.
findings.current_state: There are two independent 'nice grid step' + 'draw grid lines' implementations: canvas-drawing/grid.ts for the BasisCanvas and equation/lib/grid.ts for the ConvergencePlot. They share the same niceStep algorithm (log10 → magnitude → 2/5/10 branch), the same rgba(150,150,150,0.07) minor-line color (the C4-G2 mode-blindness defect), and the same 60-80 line structure. Any fix to one requires the same fix to the other — a classic split-brain defect.
findings.proposed: Extract a shared lib/canvas/grid.ts that exports niceStep() and drawCartesianGrid(ctx, region, domain, colorSet) where colorSet is the resolved token set from resolveVizColors(). Both BasisCanvas and ConvergencePlot import from the shared module. The ConvergencePlot's PlotPadding interface migrates into the shared module. This is a pure consolidation — both call sites keep their current call signature via a thin adapter, net code decreases, and the C4-G2 token fix applies once.

findings.title: HarmonicLevelGrid — the legitimate grid-as-UI has no mathematical lattice identity
findings.evidence: web/src/components/morph/HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:218-225: .grid uses display:flex + overflow-x:auto rather than CSS grid; .grid-cell has fixed border-radius:0.5rem and var(--card) background with no spatial mathematical context. morph-1440x900.png shows a row of thumbnail cards — recognizable as a selector, but reads as a media-library strip rather than a mathematical harmonic lattice.
findings.current_state: The HarmonicLevelGrid is the one place in the app where 'grid' and 'mathematics' SHOULD read as one: it is literally an n-harmonic lattice — each cell IS a harmonic level, each SVG thumbnail IS the shape at that harmonic cut. But the layout is a horizontal flex scroll (not a true CSS grid), the cells are uniform square cards with no harmonic-identity decoration beyond the n=k label, and there is no spatial grammar connecting adjacent cells (no 'these are sequential harmonic refinements of each other' visual language). The mathematical lattice identity is entirely absent.
findings.proposed: Reshape the layout to a true CSS grid (grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(72px, 1fr))) so cells wrap and the spatial 2D arrangement of cells carries meaning (frequency increases left-to-right then wraps). Add a subtle background-grid behind each cell's SVG (the same --grid-pitch pattern as ContourEditorCanvas, at 6-8% opacity) so each thumbnail reads as a 'plotted on graph paper' mathematical figure. Tint the active cell's background to color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-red) 8%, var(--card)) to distinguish it spatially, not just by border-color. The SVG thumbnail strokes should inherit the harmonic-level hue from VIZ_COLORS.spectrumColor(level, maxLevel) so the grid visually encodes harmonic frequency through color as well as position.

glassui_asks.name: canvas-grid-tokens
glassui_asks.what: Expose --canvas-grid-minor-color and --canvas-grid-axis-color as light-dark-aware CSS custom properties in the token layer (scale-paper.css or color-radius.css), analogous to how --constellation-* tokens are already defined. These should be plain-hsl leaves per the Canvas2D light-dark() constraint (same proof:constellation-tokens clause c). The consumer (fourier grid.ts) reads them via getComputedStyle and caches with resolveVizColors().
glassui_asks.why: All Canvas2D grid modules currently use hardcoded rgba(150,150,150,…) because the light-dark() / var() restriction means they cannot read the ladder tokens directly. glass-ui already solved this architectural constraint for constellation tokens — the same pattern should extend to coordinate grids used by downstream Canvas2D consumers.

glassui_asks.name: graph-paper-surface-utility
glassui_asks.what: A @utility graph-paper (analogous to .paper-texture) that applies a CSS repeating-linear-gradient crosshatch at --grid-pitch using --foreground at 8% opacity. Parameterisable via --graph-paper-opacity and --graph-paper-pitch. The ContourEditorCanvas and GalleryCard image-frame are both fourier-local consumers but the pattern is general (any drawing-surface card that wants graph-paper chrome).
glassui_asks.why: Currently fourier has two independent CSS crosshatch grid implementations (ContourEditorCanvas.vue:292-296 and GalleryCard.vue:239-250) with different pitches and opacities. A shared glass-ui utility class would collapse both to one class application, tokenize the pitch and opacity, and make the graph-paper motif available to other downstream apps (slides, etc.) without each reinventing it.

open_questions: Should the mathematical dot lattice (C4-G7 proposed — dots at grid intersections at mathematically significant positions) replace the continuous line grid, or compose on top of it? The current line grid provides spatial alignment; the dot lattice provides mathematical identity. A hybrid (faint lines + dots at π-multiples) may be richer than either alone, but risks perceptual noise at high harmonic counts.

The C4-G1 proposal (replace placeholder grid with unit-circle + axes scene) means the empty state no longer signals 'you can upload here' via a graph-paper background. Should the graph-paper motif be retained at a sub-layer behind the unit circle, or removed entirely in favour of the mathematical diagram?

The ConvergencePlot (equation/lib/grid.ts) and BasisCanvas (canvas-drawing/grid.ts) share logic but draw into different coordinate systems (pad-clipped plot area vs full-canvas viewport-transformed space). The C4-G8 consolidation is architecturally correct but the PlotPadding abstraction needs care to avoid making the shared module know about both coordinate models. What is the right abstraction boundary — shared niceStep() only, or shared drawCartesianGrid() with a region parameter?

The HarmonicLevelGrid (C4-G9) currently uses display:flex for horizontal scroll on mobile. Switching to CSS grid with auto-fill wrapping breaks the 'scroll a long sequence of harmonics' mobile UX. Is the 2D-wrap layout acceptable on mobile, or should it be grid-on-desktop / flex-scroll-on-mobile via a responsive @media switch?

C5.dimension: C5 — Math-motif suffusion (mathematical notation, glyphs, lattices, epicycle iconography as intentional chrome)
C5.verdict: The math motif is half-built and unevenly applied: it is strong where it is content (KaTeX Σ equation card, the canvas epicycle render, the script-ℱ logo, NotationPills sin/eⁱ/Ae glyphs, the basis-icon set, the genuinely elegant DarkModeToggle that morphs a sun↔moon as a live Fourier epicycle path) but completely absent from the chrome that frames the app — empty states, loading spinners, dividers, section markers, and page-level ambient surface. The single largest gap is architectural, not cosmetic: five per-page Fourier-path assets (equation/gallery/morph/paper/visualize.json, ~270KB each) were pre-computed and shipped but wired into ZERO consumers, while the exact rendering machinery to display them (svg-fourier.ts + FourierMorphSvg + useFourierMorph) already ships and is proven by the toggle. Eight near-identical generic CSS border-spin spinners stand in where a partial-sum-convergence or epicycle-trace loader would be both signature and thematically literal. The remedy is a single M wave that builds one decorative epicycle/lattice chrome primitive, consumes the orphaned assets as per-route ambient signatures, and replaces the duplicated spinner — all WITHIN PROPORTION (one watermark per surface, PRM-gated, INP-safe), turning math from decoration-in-the-content into the app's quiet signature.

findings.title: Five pre-computed per-page Fourier-path assets are orphaned — generated but wired to zero consumers
findings.evidence: web/src/assets/fourier-paths/{equation,gallery,morph,paper,visualize}.json (~270KB each) exist; grep across src/**/*.{vue,ts} shows imports ONLY for sun.json + moon.json (DarkModeToggle.vue:23-24, FourierMorphDemo.vue:95-96). The five page-named JSONs have NO importer.
findings.current_state: ~1.35MB of pre-computed epicycle decompositions (named exactly for the 5 routes) sit unused. The render machinery to display them already ships and is proven: svg-fourier.ts (prepareFourierShape, pointsToSvgPath), components/decorative/FourierMorphSvg.vue, composables/useFourierMorph.ts. Someone intended a per-page epicycle signature and stopped at asset generation.
findings.proposed: Build one decorative primitive — components/decorative/EpicycleSignature.vue — taking a FourierShape and rendering it as a faint, large, single-stroke ambient watermark (low opacity, one per surface, positioned as corner/background chrome, NOT content). Drive it off the route name so each page carries its own pre-computed glyph. Gate the optional draw-on-enter trace behind prefers-reduced-motion (reuse useFourierMorph level-stepping); the static path is the floor. Consumes the dead assets, adds zero new infra. Proportion: opacity ~0.04–0.08, one per route, never over interactive content.

findings.title: Eight duplicated generic border-spin spinners where an epicycle/partial-sum loader would be signature and literal

findings.proposed: Author one shared components/decorative/EpicycleSpinner.vue: 2–3 nested rotating circles (the favicon's own concentric-epicycle vocabulary) at differing radii/phase, stroked in the viz palette, prefers-reduced-motion → static glyph or single subtle pulse. Replace all eight sites. For the two compute-bound loaders optionally trace a converging partial-sum stroke. One primitive, eight consumers, motif-literal, DRY. Proportion: small (size-6/size-8), palette-tinted not rainbow, INP-safe CSS transform.

findings.title: Empty states use generic Lucide icons + plain prose instead of math iconography
findings.evidence: Gallery empty state (GalleryView.vue:280) uses Lucide `Layers` + 'No visualizations yet.'; workspace drop-zone (VisualizationView.vue ~149) uses a Lucide up-arrow + 'Drag & drop an image here'; admin empties use ScrollText/etc. Screenshot before/gallery-1440x900.png shows the Layers glyph adrift in a vast empty pane; before/workspace-1440x900.png shows the generic arrow.

findings.proposed: Give each empty state a faint epicycle/basis motif as its hero glyph: gallery empty → the gallery.json epicycle outline (reuse C5-1's primitive) low-opacity behind the prose; workspace drop-zone → an epicycle-traced dashed boundary or a small ℱ mark rather than the stock arrow. Keep the prose (archaic register intentional), swap the icon for the signature. Proportion: one decorative glyph per empty state, muted, non-interactive.

findings.title: Section dividers and panel markers are plain rules — no math-glyph chrome
findings.evidence: ContourSettings.vue:256-262 (advanced-divider = two .divider-line + chevron), MobileFloatingToc.vue:147, ConvergenceLegend.vue:28, AppHeader.vue:108 — all plain 1–1.5px color-mix rules. Panel section labels (GalleryFeaturedCarousel.vue:24 'Featured', GalleryDraftsSection.vue:57 'My Drafts', GalleryCardModal.vue:126 'Decomposition') are cm-serif text with no glyph anchor.

findings.proposed: Introduce a tiny optional math section-mark: a small cm-serif glyph (∑, ℱ, or epicycle bullet) prefixing key panel titles, and a center-glyph divider variant (a faint ℱ/∑ centered on the rule) for major section breaks. WITHIN PROPORTION: only load-bearing titles, one glyph, sized to cap-height — signature not noise. Reuse the existing cm-serif + viz-amber treatment so it reads as intentional chrome.

findings.title: No app-level ambient math lattice/watermark — global surface is flat
findings.evidence: web/src/style.css (143 lines) has zero background-image/lattice/pattern. The graph-paper grid in before/workspace-1440x900.png comes from glass-ui's Configurator stage cell (not fourier chrome); the faint dot-grid in before/gallery-1440x900.png is also not authored in fourier. PaperView.vue:507 has the only radial-gradient (a vignette, not a math motif).
findings.current_state: The lattice/grid motif appears ONLY inside canvases (BasisCanvas drawGrid, BasisCanvas.vue:102) and incidentally via glass-ui's Configurator. Non-canvas surfaces (gallery, equation, morph, paper margins) have no ambient mathematical texture — the 'GRID + MATH' design language is in the spec but not on the ambient page.
findings.proposed: Add a single very faint global graph-paper / coefficient-lattice surface as the app's ambient floor — a CSS repeating linear-gradient (or low-opacity SVG <pattern>, the SvgFilters.vue defs precedent already proves this), tuned to read as engineering graph paper, dark-mode-aware via color-mix tokens. Unifies surfaces that today inconsistently show a grid (workspace) vs nothing (gallery). Proportion: opacity ≤ 0.04, single token-driven definition in style.css, honors dark mode; subliminal, felt-not-seen.

findings.title: Morph (and other) page header is plain text with no ℱ signature despite being the most epicycle-native surface
findings.evidence:
FourierMorphDemo.vue:4-6 `

` styled plain serif 2rem (FourierMorphDemo.vue:214). Screenshot before/morph-1440x900.png confirms a bare title over the epicycle preview. Contrast PaperView.vue:356 which brands its h1 with the script-ℱ ('ℱourier Analysis').

C6.dimension: C6 — Typography Audacity (display face, type scale, hierarchy-via-type, hero/section heads, KaTeX)
C6.verdict: fourier's typography is the single most under-realized axis against the "large and audacious" directive, and the glass-ui 4.0 re-grounding makes the fix a clean gestalt transposition rather than new bespoke work. glass-ui 4.0 ships a complete φ-ladder display system (`--type-display-1..audacious` clamps to a 352px peak, `text-display-*` / `text-hero` / `text-pane-title` / `text-title|heading|subheading` utilities, `useStaggerReveal` + `.char-stagger` kinetic) and a brand display face (Plus Jakarta Sans) — fourier consumes NONE of it. Worse, two latent breakages exist under the pending 4.0 bump: fourier vendors Fraunces (woff2, variable 100-900) yet never references it (a dead ~30KB+ font load), and `.cm-serif` — which paints the paper hero, the brand mark, and every math label — resolves via glass-ui 4.0 to `var(--font-serif-math, serif)`, a token fourier never sets, so the entire Computer Modern display voice silently degrades to system Times. The idiomatic move: rebind `--font-display` → the already-vendored Fraunces (the editorial-mathematical display voice the J design wanted, which glass-ui's Plus-Jakarta default is wrong for), set `--font-serif-math` → Computer Modern for the math/body voice, then adopt the φ-ladder utilities for a real hero + section ramp. This is the prior J-typo vision, corrected for the 4.0 reality (no Fraunces/WONK in glass-ui; it's a fourier-local display brand).

findings.title: `.cm-serif` silently degrades to system Times under glass-ui 4.0 — the paper hero, brand mark, and all math labels lose Computer Modern
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/typography/utilities.css:64-67 `@utility cm-serif { font-family: var(--font-serif-math, serif); }`; fourier web/src/style.css sets only `--font-sans` (line 14), NEVER `--font-serif-math`; `.cm-serif` is consumed at the paper H1 (PaperView.vue:354), the brand mark (AppHeader.vue:67), the mobile TOC (PaperView.vue:361), and indirectly the whole prose voice
findings.current_state: fourier still pins glass-ui ^3.1.0 where `.cm-serif` historically resolved through `--font-sans`. Under 4.0 (the pending bump) `.cm-serif` reads the brand-new `--font-serif-math` token with a bare `serif` fallback. fourier never declares it, so every CM-Serif surface — the paper hero, the ℱourier wordmark, KaTeX-adjacent math labels — falls back to the OS default serif (Times/Georgia). The defining Computer-Modern voice of a mathematics paper is lost the moment the 4.0 bump lands.
findings.proposed: In fourier's `@theme`/`:root`, set `--font-serif-math: "Computer Modern Serif", "Latin Modern Roman", "CMU Serif", Georgia, serif;` as the single source for the math/serif voice, and retire the `--font-sans` remap (line 14) — the `--font-sans` override is a 3.x-era hack that no longer feeds `.cm-serif` in 4.0 and now only shadows glass-ui's own `--font-sans` bridge. One token binds CM Serif to every `.cm-serif` site through the library's own contract; no per-component font-family literals, no shim.
findings.wave_hint: M.W1 (the glass-ui 4.0 dep-bump + token-reconciliation foundation wave; must land WITH the bump or the bump breaks the paper voice)

findings.title: Fraunces is vendored, preloaded-adjacent, and fetched — but referenced NOWHERE: a dead display-font payload
findings.evidence: web/public/fonts/fraunces/{fraunces-latin.woff2,fraunces-italic-latin.woff2} + web/public/fonts.css:44-63 declare `Fraunces` (variable wght 100 900, both styles); grep across web/src for `Fraunces`/`fraunces` returns ZERO usage — no `--font-display`, no utility, no `font-family` literal. The only display glyph (`.fourier-f`) is glass-ui-owned and reads `--font-display` (= Plus Jakarta in 4.0), not Fraunces.
findings.current_state: The G.δ.W5 self-hosting work bundled Fraunces with the intent (per docs/tranches/J/design/WC-design-typo-color.md:11-16) of making it the display voice, but no tranche ever wired it. It sits as a face the browser will fetch the instant any glyph in its unicode-range is drawn by a serif fallback — paid-for bytes, zero brand return. Meanwhile glass-ui 4.0's `--font-display` is Plus Jakarta Sans (a geometric sans), the WRONG voice for an editorial-mathematical journal.
findings.proposed: Make Fraunces the live display voice: declare `--font-stack-display`/`--font-display: "Fraunces", "Computer Modern Serif", serif` in fourier's theme (overriding glass-ui's Plus-Jakarta default at the consumer boundary — the documented rebrand lever, bridges.css:62 `--font-display: var(--font-stack-display)`). Drive its optical/wonk axes with `font-optical-sizing: auto` + a `font-variation-settings: "SOFT" 0, "WONK" 1` register on the display utilities fourier applies. This activates the dead payload AS the audacious display brand — Fraunces headlines over a Computer-Modern body is the genuine display↔body pairing the ladder provisions.
findings.wave_hint: M.W1 (foundation: bind `--font-display`→Fraunces in the same token-reconciliation that fixes F1)

findings.title: The φ-display ladder is entirely unused — every heading is a raw ad-hoc Tailwind size, capping at ~3.25rem; nothing is audacious
findings.evidence: glass-ui ships `--type-display-1..5` + `-mega/-hero/-audacious` (typography/scale.css; audacious peak 352px) and `text-display-*`/`text-hero`/`text-title`/`text-heading`/`text-subheading` (typography/semantic.css). fourier's LARGEST heading is PaperView.vue:354 `cm-serif text-4xl ... md:text-[3.25rem]`; FourierMorphDemo.vue:214-227 `.demo-title` is `text-2xl`→2rem; grep for `text-5xl/6xl/7xl/8xl` returns only that one paper site. No `text-display*`/`text-hero`/`text-pane-title` usage anywhere in src.
findings.current_state: Headings are a flat spectrum of hand-picked Tailwind rungs (`text-2xl`, `text-4xl`, `text-sm font-semibold`) with no φ-spacing, no display/body contrast, and no element ever crosses ~52px. The paper hero (screenshot paper-1280x800.png) reads as a modest centered serif line, not a display statement. There is no typographic identity that says 'large and audacious'.
findings.proposed: Adopt the glass-ui φ-ladder verbatim: paper hero `cm-serif text-4xl font-bold` → `text-display-2` (φ^(5/2) clamp, now Fraunces) with the `<span class=fourier-f>` retired (the whole line is the display face); section heads → `text-title`/`text-heading`; `.demo-title` and the (currently absent) gallery/equation page heads → `text-display-1`. One ladder, φ-spaced, display↔body contrast appears for free. No magic literals survive.

glassui_asks.name: GA-C6-1 — display-face register knob so a consumer can run a serif display voice through the φ-ladder without forking every `text-display-*` utility
glassui_asks.what: glass-ui's `text-display-*`/`text-hero`/`text-pane-title` utilities all hardcode `font-family: var(--font-display)` AND `font-weight: 600`/`font-optical-sizing: auto` tuned for Plus Jakarta Sans (a sans). A consumer like fourier that rebinds `--font-display` to a characterful serif (Fraunces, WONK/SOFT axes) gets the right family but inherits sans-tuned weight/optical defaults. Expose per-register tuning knobs — `--display-weight`, `--display-wonk` (→ `font-variation-settings`), `--display-optical` — on the display utilities so a consumer can dial the variable-axis register from tokens, not by re-authoring the utilities. This is the corrected, 4.0-era successor to the J design's stale 'glass-ui reserves Fraunces WONK=1' premise: glass-ui ships Plus Jakarta as display; the Fraunces voice is fourier-local; glass-ui should make the display ladder voice-agnostic.
glassui_asks.why: Without it, fourier must either accept Plus-Jakarta-tuned weights on its Fraunces display (wrong optical register) or re-declare every `text-display-*` utility locally (a dead-class fork — violates the no-legacy directive). A token knob keeps fourier consuming the canonical ladder while supplying its own display character. Owner: glass-ui maintainer. Non-blocking — fourier can set `font-variation-settings` on its own header elements meanwhile.
