C7.dimension: C7 — Colourful audacious POPS (from the icon palette)
C7.verdict: The icon palette IS audacious — favicon.svg is a six-stop rainbow epicycle (R-O-Y-G-B-V: #ff4444 #ff8800 #ffcc00 #44bb44 #4488ff #8844ff) and colors.ts carries a softened twin (STATIC.rainbow). But that chroma is quarantined to a single chart legend (the equation page harmonic series). The entire app chrome — home, gallery, morph, workspace, paper — renders near-monochrome cream/foreground with exactly ONE pop: the orange dark-mode gear-sun in the corner. The nav 'active' state collapses all five distinctly-iconed routes onto one undifferentiated --viz-amber accent. Worse, the spectrum-hue formula `(1-x)*300` is hand-rolled in sRGB-HSL and copy-pasted across four files while value.js 0.12.0 ships exactly the OKLCH palette engine (mixColorsN, interpolateHue, safeAccentColor) that fourier never calls — it imports only easeInOutSine. The proportioned move is to (1) promote the icon rainbow to a single canonical OKLCH ramp generated by value.js, (2) key per-route accents off it so each page carries its own hue, and (3) re-route the four duplicated spectrum functions through that one source. Audacious where attention lives (active state, data viz, key CTAs, hover), restrained on body surfaces.

findings.title: Spectrum-hue formula `(1-x)*300` hand-rolled in sRGB-HSL and duplicated in four files
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/lib/harmonics.ts:86-87, web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/transforms.ts:6-7, web/src/components/shared/CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:48-49, web/src/components/equation/FrequencyGraph.vue:43-44 — all four compute `hue=(1-i/(total-1))*300; hsl(hue,85%,55%)`.
findings.current_state: Four independent copies of the same magenta→red sRGB-HSL ramp. sRGB-HSL has non-perceptual lightness (the mid-band greens/yellows visually jump), it isn't gamut-managed, and it has zero relationship to the favicon palette — so the data-viz rainbow and the brand rainbow are two unrelated gradients.
findings.proposed: Replace all four with a single `harmonicColor(i, total, alpha?)` in colors.ts that samples the canonical icon ramp via value.js mixColorsN([...icon stops], weights, 'oklch', 'longer') — perceptually-even, gamut-mapped, and IDENTICAL to the brand mark. One function, imported four places; the spectrum becomes the icon palette made continuous. This also unifies the canvas epicycle hues (transforms.ts) with the chart legend so the visualizer's spinning circles and the frequency graph share the favicon's colours.

findings.title: value.js 0.12.0 colour engine is present but unused — only easeInOutSine is imported

findings.current_state: fourier hand-rolls hslToHex/rgbToHex/cssVarToHex in colors.ts:22-74 and HSL hue math in four files, while the colour authority it already depends on ships OKLCH conversion, perceptual mixing, hue interpolation, gamut mapping, and contrast-safe accent clamping. The dependency is paid for but only its easings are drawn down.
findings.proposed: Bump value.js ^0.10.0→^0.12.0 (peers shipped; inv-30 platform-over-library) and route ALL colour derivation through it: cssVarToHex's bespoke regex parser → color2(); the manual --viz-amber AA-darken (style.css:113-122) → safeAccentColor()/needsContrastAdjustment() computed at boot; the rainbow ramp → mixColorsN in OKLCH. Deletes ~80 lines of hand-rolled colour math (no-legacy) and makes every accent contrast-provable rather than eyeballed.

findings.title: Hover/interaction feedback is monochrome alpha-mix — no hue-shift pop on interactive elements

glassui_asks.name: icon-ramp-as-token-recipe
glassui_asks.what: A glass-ui token recipe for a consumer-supplied N-stop perceptual brand ramp: given an ordered list of seed colours, emit --brand-ramp-0..N (display) and --brand-ramp-soft-0..N (calmed) tokens in OKLCH, gamut-mapped, with per-stop contrast-safe variants against --background. fourier would feed it the six favicon stops.
glassui_asks.why: Three sibling apps (fourier rainbow epicycles, speedtest phase colours, words palettes) each hand-roll a brand ramp; the --viz-* and --tier-* families already prove glass-ui owns multi-stop semantic colour tokens. A ramp recipe that consumes value.js mixColorsN/safeAccentColor centralizes the 'audacious-but-AA-safe palette from seeds' pattern instead of each app reimplementing it (fourier currently does so in colors.ts + four duplicated HSL sites).

glassui_asks.name: per-route-accent-channel
glassui_asks.what: A glass-ui convention/utility for per-route (or per-section) accent identity: a documented --route-accent custom-property channel that nav/tab/dock active-state recipes read, so a host app can assign each route a distinct hue and have active indicators, drop-shadows, and hover tints pick it up uniformly.
glassui_asks.why: glass-ui already centralizes active-state styling for dock/tabs (instrument-chassis.css, dock-controls). Today fourier must override .nav-trigger-icon / .is-active locally to inject --viz-amber. A first-class --route-accent channel would let fourier (and speedtest's phase tabs) express per-route colour identity through the upstream recipe rather than scoped-style overrides, keeping the 'audacious per-page hue' directive idiomatic and inv-30-clean.

open_questions: Should the canonical ramp be the SATURATED favicon stops (max audacity, but several fail AA on the cream --background and need safeAccentColor clamping per use) or the soft STATIC.rainbow (already calmer, AA-safer, but less audacious)? Recommendation: store saturated as the source-of-truth and derive a clamped variant per surface, so 'audacious' is the default and 'proportioned' is computed, not hand-picked.

Does keeping the data-viz spectrum (the analytical n=1..8 legend) visually identical to the brand chrome ramp help or hurt legibility? Unifying them is elegant, but the chart needs maximally-distinguishable adjacent hues across up to 50 harmonics, which may want a wider hue sweep than a 6-stop brand ramp interpolated. May need the ramp to define endpoints while the chart samples a denser OKLCH path between them.

Clean break, no alias." Will silently render nothing for a valid 0 value (the documented hazard).
findings.current_state: 11 call sites pass `:amount`. On 4.0.0 these are unrecognized props — silent render gap (value prop reads `undefined`, the placeholder branch activates).
findings.proposed: Global rename `:amount` → `:value` on all MetricBadge/MetricPill usages. Mechanical substitution — prop semantics are identical, only the prop name changed. 11 files in one pass.

findings.evidence: glass-ui 4.0.0 GlassDock.vue:8 `import { ..., useId, ... } from "vue"` + line `const dockId = \`glass-dock-${useId()}\``; DockLayerGroup.vue: `const vtId = useId(); ... "view-transition-name": \`gl-dock-stack-${vtId.replace(...)}\``". fourier CanvasControlsDock.vue and EditorControlsDock.vue both render GlassDock on the same page (/w); the pre-4.0.0 GlassDock hard-coded the name `glass-dock-1` (the glass-dock-1 duplicate-VT-name e2e blocker documented in project_tranche_k.md). findings.title: Configurator lacks asideSide="left" — controls aside is always right, DEC-2 violation
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/VisualizationView.vue:194 `<Configurator scroll-mode="auto" class="viz-configurator">` — no `asideSide` prop. glass-ui 4.0.0 Configurator.vue defines `asideSide?: ConfiguratorAsideSide` (default "right") with explicit `"left"` flip via grid-column placement + border-side swap, DOM/tab order unchanged. The prior audit docs (docs/audits/runs/2026-06-04-J-postimpl-audit/SYNTHESIS.md) and CONSTELLATION.md call for a DEC-2 controls-LEFT layout on the workspace.
findings.current_state: The controls aside always sits on the right (default). Workspace layout has the canvas stage right and controls left in the design intent, but the Configurator reverses them — the aside is to the right of the stage slot.
findings.proposed: Add `aside-side="left"` to the `<Configurator>` in VisualizationView.vue. The grid-column flip moves the aside visually left while preserving DOM source order (stage first, then aside). The `lg:border-r` / `lg:border-l` swap on the aside is owned by the Configurator internally via `asideBorderClass`. No other changes needed — the existing stage/controls slots are correct.

findings.title: useTextHighlight not used — search hit highlight injects v-html with <mark> DOM mutation
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/search/searchHelpers.ts:34-68 `highlightFuzzy()` builds an HTML string with `<mark>` tags via string concatenation + `escapeHtml`. PaperSearchDropdown.vue:58 and PaperSearchModal.vue:100 both render via `v-html="highlightFuzzy(resultLabel(r), search.query.value)"`. glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `useTextHighlight` on `/motion-core` (AX.W37 — re-homed from /dom; composables/motion/useTextHighlight.ts). The composable drives `CSS.highlights` / `::highlight(<name>)` — zero DOM mutation, no v-html XSS surface, multiplexed per-name contributors.
findings.current_state: Two search surfaces (`PaperSearchDropdown`, `PaperSearchModal`) use v-html injection with a hand-rolled `<mark>` HTML builder. This is a DOM-mutation approach (splits text nodes, creates XSS surface, requires HTML escaping), and it is specifically what useTextHighlight was designed to retire.
findings.proposed: Replace `highlightFuzzy` (the v-html approach) with `useTextHighlight("paper-search-mark")`. In PaperSearchDropdown and PaperSearchModal: `import { useTextHighlight } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` (or `/motion-core`); call `hl.setFromMatches(containerEl, query, fuzzyRangeMatcher)` where `fuzzyRangeMatcher` translates the existing `fuzzyMatch()` index-hits into `{ start, end }` spans. Add `::highlight(paper-search-mark) { background: ...; color: ... }` CSS rules (the `--primary` colour family). Remove `highlightFuzzy`, `escapeHtml`, all v-html usages. The `supported` flag is the built-in feature gate.

findings.title: useCanvas2D substrate not adopted — BasisCanvas/ConvergencePlot use hand-rolled ResizeObserver + rAF without park/freeze
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasSetup.ts: hand-rolls `ResizeObserver`, calls `setupCanvas()` in `onMounted/onUnmounted`, no offscreen park, no tab-hidden park, no reduced-motion freeze. web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:93 and FrequencyGraph.vue:63 call `canvas.getContext("2d")` directly with no lifecycle management. glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `useCanvas2D` (AW.W17 — src/composables/glass/canvas2d/useCanvas2D.ts) providing: demand-driven suspend set (tab-hidden / off-screen / manual), `contentvisibilityautostatechange` park, IntersectionObserver fallback, live `prefers-reduced-motion` re-monitor, dpr-clamped ResizeObserver with `ctx.setTransform`.
findings.current_state: useCanvasSetup (the BasisCanvas substrate) has no offscreen-park, no tab-hidden park, no PRM freeze. The animation store's visibility ref-counting is a workaround for the missing lifecycle substrate — both ConvergencePlot and FrequencyGraph are completely unmanaged (no park, no suspend).
findings.proposed: Transpose BasisCanvas to `useCanvas2D` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/canvas` (the subpath barrel exists). The `setup(ctx)` callback receives the 2D context; the returned `{ render, teardown }` frame hooks thread the existing drawing logic. The handle's `arm()` / `suspend()` / `resume()` / `wake()` replace the animation store's `setCanvasVisible` ref-counting. Apply the same substrate to ConvergencePlot and FrequencyGraph. Remove `useCanvasSetup.ts`.

findings.title: inert a11y not applied to collapsed subtrees — keyboard focus leaks into closed panels
findings.evidence: web/src/components/ui/CollapsibleSection.vue: uses reka-ui `<Collapsible>/<CollapsibleContent>` with `data-state` CSS animations but no `inert` attribute. ContourSettings.vue:255 uses the same pattern. glass-ui 4.0.0 ConfiguratorLayer.vue:160 applies `:inert="!open || undefined"` on the region div (`aria-hidden` + `inert` together — the aria-hidden-focus closure). GlassDock.vue:436,442 applies `:inert` on the collapsed/expanded pane pair. DockLayer.vue:75 applies `:inert="isActive ? undefined : true"`.
findings.current_state: Collapsed `<CollapsibleContent>` subtrees are visually hidden (height: 0) but remain in the tab order and a11y tree. Screen-reader users and keyboard navigators reach hidden controls inside closed ContourSettings advanced section and CollapsibleSection panels.
findings.proposed: Add `:inert="!open || undefined"` to the content wrapper in `CollapsibleSection.vue` (the `<CollapsibleContent>` element or its direct wrapper div). Apply same to ContourSettings.vue's advanced `<CollapsibleContent>`. The `|| undefined` idiom removes the attribute entirely when open (not `inert="false"` which is non-standard). Pair with `aria-hidden="!open"` for the combined a11y closure. No reka-ui changes needed — this is a host-side attribute.

findings.title: startViewTransition called raw on document — should use glass-ui /motion-core substrate
findings.evidence: web/src/router/index.ts:146 calls `document.startViewTransition(() => swapped)` directly. Line 2 imports `supportsViewTransitions` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui` — only the gate function, not the wrapper. glass-ui 4.0.0 exports `startViewTransition(mutate, opts?)` from `/motion-core` (and root barrel) with: typed `ViewTransitionResult`, `types?` for `:active-view-transition-type` CSS, `skipReducedMotion` option (internal instant path), deadlock-safe promise handling, and a `navigate()` helper for Vue Router. The router also hand-rolls a `prefersReducedMotion()` check and `resolveViewSwap` promise coordination that the substrate already owns.
findings.current_state: router/index.ts:124-148 hand-rolls VT coordination: a `resolveViewSwap` promise, `beforeResolve`/`afterEach` hooks, and two `requestAnimationFrame` calls to release the update callback. The PRM check is a static snapshot (not a live media query listener). The `types` option for route-specific CSS curves is unavailable.
findings.proposed: Import `{ startViewTransition, navigate }` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core`. Replace the `beforeResolve` / `afterEach` pair with a single `router.beforeResolve` that calls `await navigate(async () => { /* await the route commit */ }, { types: ["route-morph"] })` — the substrate owns the promise coordination and the instant-fallback. Remove `resolveViewSwap`, the `requestAnimationFrame` double-schedule, and the hand-rolled PRM snapshot. The `::view-transition-image-pair.gl-route-morph` CSS curves can then target the named type.

findings.title: MobileFloatingToc dropdown uses v-if + Transition — should be native [popover] + glass-top-layer
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/MobileFloatingToc.vue:130-180 implements the dropdown as a `v-if="floatingTocOpen"` div with a custom `.toc-expand-enter-active` Vue Transition. The component manually locks `scrollContainer.style.overflow`, binds `@keydown.esc`, uses a separate `.floating-toc-backdrop` click-outside div, and calls `nextTick(() => dropdownRef.value?.focus())` for focus management. glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `.glass-top-layer` + `@starting-style` + `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` + `overlay` (animations.css §TOP-LAYER, lines 310-370) for native `[popover]` elements.
findings.current_state: A bespoke JS-driven dropdown with manual backdrop, scroll-lock, focus management, and a Vue Transition. The native popover API handles all of these: top-layer stacking (no z-index race), light-dismiss (click-outside + Escape), `autofocus` on the first focusable descendant, no scroll-lock needed (popover is non-modal).
findings.proposed: Transpose the dropdown div to `<div popover="auto" ref="dropdownRef" class="floating-toc-dropdown glass-floating glass-top-layer">`. Trigger via `dropdownRef.value?.showPopover()` / `hidePopover()`. Remove: `.floating-toc-backdrop` div, `scrollContainer.style.overflow` mutation, `@keydown.esc` handler, `dismissDropdown` nextTick focus management (light-dismiss is native). Add `::highlight` CSS for the `@starting-style` entry animation from `glass.animations.css` via the `.glass-top-layer` class selector. The `triggerEl()?.focus()` return-focus can attach to the `toggle` event listener on the popover.

findings.title: Coefficient popover in EquationView is a positioned div — should be native popover or HoverPopover
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCoeffHover.ts: `popoverPos = ref({ x: 0, y: 0 })` — manually tracks mouse position relative to the card bounding rect. EquationView.vue:261 renders `<div class="coeff-popover glass-elevated" v-if="hoveredCoeff && popoverHtml" :style="{ left, top }">`. glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `HoverPopover` (`/hover-popover` subpath, already imported in EditorControlsDock.vue:5 and CanvasControlsDock.vue). The native CSS Anchor Positioning (`anchor-name`/`position-anchor`/`position-area`) is the idiomatic target for tooltip-style positioned popovers (widely available, replaces the `getBoundingClientRect` dance).
findings.current_state: The coefficient hover card computes an absolute position via `getBoundingClientRect` on every `mousemove` event and writes it to a ref. This is the exact pattern anchor positioning retires: the position is computed in JS on the hot input path (INP risk during coefficient hover over a KaTeX-heavy equation card).
findings.proposed: Adopt `<HoverPopover>` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/hover-popover` — it wraps native anchor positioning + `[popover]` natively. Each `.eq-coeff` span receives `anchor-name: --coeff-<kind>` as a CSS class/inline style; the popover panel uses `position-anchor: --coeff-<kind>`. Alternatively use glass-ui's `@mkbabb/glass-ui/hover-card` (`HoverCard`/`HoverCardTrigger`/`HoverCardContent`) already imported at EquationView.vue:9 — wrap each coefficient class with a `<HoverCardTrigger>` instead of the event-delegation approach. Remove `useCoeffHover.ts` `popoverPos` and the `onMouseMove` listener.

findings.title: FullscreenViewer uses hand-rolled focus trap — glass-ui inert pattern suffices
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/FullscreenViewer.vue:31-70 implements a manual Tab focus trap via `focusableEls()` querySelectorAll, `onTrapKeydown` with first/last sentinel logic, and `document.addEventListener`. glass-ui 4.0.0 uses `inert` as the a11y enclosure for modal-like surfaces (GlassDock.vue:436,442). The HTML `inert` attribute pulls a subtree from focus/tab order system-wide — the opposite face of the same coin: `inert` the background, let the foreground receive Tab naturally.
findings.current_state: An 80-line hand-rolled focus trap with a FOCUSABLE selector string, array-based first/last management, and global keydown listener. Will break on new focusable element types; must be kept in sync with future component additions.
findings.proposed: Apply `inert` to the background application root (the `<div id="app">` or the router-view container) when the fullscreen viewer is open, rather than trapping focus within the overlay. `document.getElementById('app')?.inert = props.visible` in a `watch(props.visible, ...)`. The fullscreen layer (teleported to body) is not inert, so Tab cycles naturally within it. Remove the entire `focusTrappedListener` / `FOCUSABLE` / `focusableEls` / `onTrapKeydown` block. Pair with the native popover approach if the layer is transposed to `<dialog>` (showModal provides focus-trap natively).

findings.title: View transition name on viz canvas is a static string — two co-mounted canvases will collide
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/VisualizationView.vue (CSS block near canvas-stage): `view-transition-name: viz-canvas-stage` (confirmed by the @supports guard in the vue file). BasisCanvas is rendered both inline and in FullscreenViewer.vue simultaneously when fullscreen is open — two mounted instances share the same static view-transition-name, which is invalid (VT names must be unique per frame). glass-ui 4.0.0 solves this in GlassDock with `const dockId = \`glass-dock-${useId()}\`` passed as a bound style.
findings.current_state: The static `view-transition-name: viz-canvas-stage` CSS is applied to every canvas-stage container. Two simultaneous mounts (inline + fullscreen BasisCanvas) paint the same VT name in the same frame snapshot — the browser silently discards one, breaking the morph.
findings.proposed: Generate a per-instance VT name with Vue 3.5 `useId()`: in BasisCanvas.vue `const vtId = useId()` then `:style="{ viewTransitionName: \`viz-canvas-${vtId.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '-')}\` }"`. Remove the static CSS rule. When only one canvas is mounted the name is stable across route navigations; when two mount (fullscreen) each gets its own unique name.

findings.title: FadingScroll not adopted — CoefficientsPanel and paper sidebar scroll without edge-fade
findings.evidence: glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `<FadingScroll>` on `@mkbabb/glass-ui/fading-scroll` (src/components/custom/fading-scroll/). The glass-ui Configurator internally uses `<FadingScroll axis="y">` for its controls column and `<FadingScroll axis="x">` for the presets chip row (Configurator.vue:215,230). Fourier has no `FadingScroll` import anywhere. web/src/components/visualization/CoefficientsPanel.vue scrolls its harmonics table; the gallery's preset chip rows in the Configurator default slot also overflow. The BA migration also retired `.scroll-fade-*` static utilities in favor of `<FadingScroll>`.
findings.current_state: Overflowing scrollable regions (CoefficientsPanel harmonics, any chip row that overflows) have no edge-fade affordance. The static `.scroll-fade-y` / `.scroll-fade-x` utilities are gone in 4.0.0 — any lingering use would be dead classes.
findings.proposed: Wrap overflowing scroll regions with `<FadingScroll axis="y">` (CoefficientsPanel harmonics table, PaperSidebar nav list) and `<FadingScroll axis="x">` (any horizontally-overflowing chip or tab row). Import from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/fading-scroll`. The component self-manages the mask; `scrollMode="auto"` on the Configurator already applies it to the controls column — this finding targets the standalone overflow regions outside the Configurator chassis.

D2.dimension: D2 — glass-ui GAPS: fourier-hand-rolled primitives to ABSTRACT INTO glass-ui (NET-NEW asks)
D2.verdict: fourier hand-rolls at least five families that already (or should) live in glass-ui as refined primitives. The single largest gap is a TONAL ACCENT recipe — `--pill-color` + `color-mix(in srgb, <tone> N%, transparent)` — repeated ~57 times across NotationPills, EquationModeToggle, BasisSelector, InfoCard, HarmonicLevelGrid; this is the colour-pop accent system the user wants suffused, yet it has no glass-ui home (IconChip covers icon-glyph tone, NOT background/border/text accent fills). Second: two distinct segmented/pill toggles (NotationPills, EquationModeToggle) re-implement what glass-ui SHIPS as SegmentedTabs (PILL+UNDERLINE materials) — fourier never imports it. Third: a math-serif section heading (`cm-serif text-sm font-semibold tracking-tight`) appears 6+ times — Section has a `label` tone but no math/serif tone. Fourth: ConvergenceLegend is a hand-rolled colour swatch-list legend with no glass-ui equivalent. Fifth: the J-CORE atom-diff viewer (when wired in J.W6) should be born as a glass-ui primitive, not hand-rolled. These are glassui_asks; fourier books them, does not write glass-ui.

findings.title: Tonal accent recipe (`--pill-color` + color-mix) hand-rolled ~57x — no glass-ui home
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/NotationPills.vue:42-46 (`--pill-color`, `color-mix(in srgb, var(--pill-color) 12%, transparent)` bg + 40% border + solid text); web/src/components/visualization/BasisSelector.vue:145,270-275 (identical recipe); web/src/components/equation/InfoCard.vue:23-27 (15%/30%/solid inline); web/src/components/equation/EquationModeToggle.vue:71-73; `grep color-mix(... transparent)` across components/ = 57 hits
findings.current_state: Each consumer re-derives the same three-channel tonal fill (bg ≈12-16%, border ≈30-40%, text = solid tone) inline via raw color-mix, keyed off an ad-hoc `--pill-color`/`info.color`/`VIZ_COLORS.*` CSS var. No shared token, no shared class; light/dark contrast each tuned by hand (style.css:113-125 hand-darkens --viz-amber for axe).
findings.proposed: Book a glass-ui NET-NEW: a tonal-accent token recipe + thin wrapper (e.g. `.accent-tone` utility / `<AccentChip tone=...>` or a `tone` arm on the existing pill/badge). One source mints `--accent-fill`/`--accent-edge`/`--accent-ink` from a single `--tone` (the same oklch-aware mixing IconChip already does for its glyph), contrast-floored once in the library, consumed by all 57 sites. fourier deletes its per-file color-mix and passes `tone="var(--viz-amber)"`. Gestalt: the colour-pop the user wants suffused becomes ONE library primitive, proportioned + contrast-safe by construction.
findings.wave_hint: M (glass-ui-adoption wave) — book the ask now; adopt after glass-ui ships

D3.verdict: The glass-ui 4.0.0 re-ground INVALIDATES this dimension's entire prior ledger: A-1 (inter-row divider) shipped as ConfiguratorLayer's `dividers` prop, A-2 (label/sub ladder) shipped as the `.configurator-section-label` token hook reading `--configurator-section-{size,weight}`, and A-3 (asideSide) shipped — all three "BOOK-to-AT" asks are SATISFIED-UPSTREAM and must be struck, not carried. What remains are FOUR genuinely-open component-internal refinements fourier's surfaces actually need, each evidenced by a hand-rolled workaround in the fourier tree: (1) ConfiguratorLayer has no header trailing/actions slot — the single highest-value refine, since it is the sole reason fourier maintains a parallel CollapsibleSection.vue and pushes reset buttons into the layer body at two sites; (2) DockIconButton ships no active/pressed toggle-state contract, so 7 `:class="{is-active}"` sites ride a class with NO backing paint in either tree; (3) Card `surface="cartoon"` shipped, retiring the 14-site `.cartoon-card` shim (fourier-local adoption); (4) DockSeparator shipped orientation-aware, retiring fourier's 4-site axis-blind `.dock-separator` hairline. findings.title: Hand-rolled rAF clock in animation store: duplicates keyframes.js NumericAnimation
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/animation.ts:51-75 — manual `startTime`, `tick()`, `requestAnimationFrame`, ping-pong cycle logic, `cancelAnimationFrame`. Comment at line 47-48 says "The previous incarnation imported Animation from @mkbabb/keyframes.js … Dead substrate excised." The store now owns the entire playback engine itself.
findings.current_state: The animation store contains a full bespoke rAF tick loop: timestamp tracking, ping-pong (even/odd cycle), speed scaling, scrub interruption, and off-screen gating via reference-counted IntersectionObserver. keyframes.js ^2.2.0 is pinned — the store comment says it removed the prior `Animation` usage, but keyframes.js 4.2.0 ships `NumericAnimation` (light, value.js-free, static import) and `SmoothProgress`/`SpringProgress` that handle exactly this pattern without the dynamic boundary.
findings.proposed: Replace the hand-rolled rAF clock with keyframes.js 4.2.0 `NumericAnimation` (statically importable, no `loadAnimationEngine()` needed — it is in the LIGHT surface). `NumericAnimation` takes a `{ t: [0, 1] }` keyframe set, a duration, and a per-frame callback; ping-pong (`iterationCount: Infinity, direction: 'alternate'`) and speed (`duration / speed`) map directly. The IntersectionObserver visibility gate is orthogonal and can stay; it just calls `.pause()` / `.resume()` on the NumericAnimation instance instead of managing `rafId`. Scrub maps to `.seek(t)`. This eliminates ~60 LOC of bespoke clock machinery and gets PRM-aware `respectReducedMotion` for free.

findings.title: Coefficient popover: mouse-tracked absolute div duplicates glass-ui HoverPopover
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCoeffHover.ts — tracks `popoverPos: { x, y }` from `getBoundingClientRect()` diffs on `mousemove`. web/src/components/equation/EquationView.vue:258-265 — `<Transition name="pop"><div class="coeff-popover glass-elevated" :style="{ left, top }" v-if="hoveredCoeff">`. EquationView.vue:393-411 — `.coeff-popover { position: absolute; transform: translateX(-50%); z-index: var(--z-bar); … }`.
findings.current_state: A 107-line composable (`useCoeffHover.ts`) tracks mouse position via `@mousemove` event delegation, computes pixel offsets relative to the card container via `getBoundingClientRect()`, and writes `popoverPos.{x,y}` as inline `left`/`top` style. The popover is an absolutely-positioned `div` with manual z-index. This approach: (a) has no collision avoidance (clips at viewport edge), (b) does not handle keyboard accessibility, (c) bypasses the glass-ui material system with raw `position: absolute`. glass-ui ships `HoverPopover` at `@mkbabb/glass-ui/hover-popover` (backed by reka-ui HoverCard — collision avoidance, side/align, timer-based open/close, dock-keep-open; AQ.W6 adds native `interestfor`+`popover=hint` progressive-enhancement path).
findings.proposed: Replace `useCoeffHover` + the absolutely-positioned `.coeff-popover` div with `<HoverPopover>` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/hover-popover`. Each `.eq-coeff` span in the KaTeX output becomes a trigger — wrap the EquationResult's rendered KaTeX with a v-once container that uses event delegation to find the nearest `.eq-coeff` on pointerenter and programmatically sets the HoverPopover's open model. The KaTeX-rendered popover body (the coefficient table) moves into the `#content` slot. The `useCoeffHover` composable and `.coeff-popover` CSS block are deleted entirely.

findings.title: .config-grid: morph page hand-rolls a 3-column responsive grid

findings.title: FullscreenViewer: hand-rolled focus trap + Teleport duplicates glass-ui Dialog
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/FullscreenViewer.vue:36-101 — 65-line bespoke focus-trap (FOCUSABLE selector, Tab wrapping, lastFocused save/restore, keydown listener via `document.addEventListener`). Line 100-101: `onMounted(() => document.addEventListener('keydown', onKeydown))`. Lines 104-144: manual `<Teleport to="body">` with a `<Transition name="fs">` overlay. Comment: "The teleported fullscreen layer must contain Tab focus".
findings.current_state: FullscreenViewer manually implements: (a) a WCAG focus trap via querySelectorAll + Tab key interception on the document, (b) Teleport to body, (c) an Escape handler, (d) show/hide via a `v-if` inside `<Transition>`, (e) return-focus-on-close logic. This is the exact contract glass-ui's `Dialog` (backed by reka-ui `DialogRoot`) covers: focus trap, Escape, aria-modal, return-focus, backdrop, Teleport — all for free.

The `<DialogContent>` replaces the `fs-backdrop`/`fs-container` structure and inherits focus trap, Escape handling, and return-focus from reka-ui. The 65-line bespoke focus trap composable, `document.addEventListener('keydown')`, and the manual `<Teleport>` block are deleted. A Dialog variant `fullscreen` (full-viewport, no rounding, no max-width cap) is declared via Tailwind utilities or a `--dialog-max-w: 100dvw` CSS override.

findings.title: 9 inline animate-spin spinners: duplicates glass-ui Pulse ring variant
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/EquationPanel.vue:108 — `<div class="h-4 w-4 animate-spin rounded-full border-[1.5px] border-border border-t-primary" />`. Each site independently picks a size (`h-4 w-4`, `h-6 w-6`, `h-8 w-8`) and border weight. There is no PRM handling — all 9 spinners animate regardless of `prefers-reduced-motion`. glass-ui ships `Pulse` with `variant="ring"` (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/pulse`), which inherits the `--pulse-duration` token, honours PRM (`animation: none; opacity: 0.6` under the query), and sizes via `currentColor`/font-size.
findings.proposed: Replace all 9 hand-rolled spinner divs with `<Pulse variant="ring" />` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/pulse`. Size via a Tailwind class on the Pulse root (e.g. `class="size-4"`). The `RefreshCw animate-spin` in ContourSettings becomes `<Pulse variant="ring" class="size-3.5" />` (or keep the icon but add `:class="{ 'animate-spin': store.computing }"` via a utility — the Pulse is cleaner). findings.title: Tab-panel slide animation in style.css: local carry of an upstream glass-ui ask
findings.evidence: web/src/style.css:79-96 — `[data-state="active"][role="tabpanel"] { animation: tab-slide-in 0.18s ease-out; }` + the `@keyframes tab-slide-in` block + a PRM zero-out. Comment: "local carry pending glass-ui's Tabs primitive shipping this on its own."
findings.current_state: A global CSS rule targets reka-ui's `data-state=active` + `role=tabpanel` attribute pair (the exact attributes that glass-ui's `UnderlineTabs` primitive sets) and applies a hardcoded `0.18s ease-out` slide-in. The easing uses a raw `ease-out` keyword rather than a glass-ui token (should be `var(--ease-out)` or `var(--ease-standard)`). glass-ui 4.0.0 ships `tab-fade` transition classes in `transitions.css` but does NOT yet ship the data-attribute tabpanel rule — this local carry is still needed.
findings.proposed: This carry remains correct as a short-term local hold. The two improvements: (a) replace `ease-out` with `var(--ease-standard)` to stay token-coherent with the glass-ui motion system, and (b) file the upstream glass-ui ask (below) to absorb it into the Tabs primitive's own stylesheet. When glass-ui ships the tabpanel animation natively the local rule is deleted.

findings.title: EquationModeToggle: bespoke pill toggle duplicates glass-ui ToggleGroup
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/EquationModeToggle.vue — a hand-rolled `<div class="eq-toggle glass-quiet">` with two `<Button variant="ghost">` children, `.is-active` state driven by a model prop, custom `eq-toggle-btn` CSS including `color: var(--viz-amber)` for the active state. findings.proposed: Replace the two-Button pill with `<ToggleGroup type="single" v-model="model">` + two `<ToggleGroupItem value="sigma">` / `<ToggleGroupItem value="expanded">`. The pill shape is kept via `class="glass-quiet rounded-full overflow-hidden"` on the `ToggleGroup` root. The `.eq-toggle-btn` active-amber colour becomes a scoped `[data-state="on"] { color: var(--viz-amber); }` rule on the `ToggleGroupItem`. The bespoke `.is-active` CSS block is deleted. ARIA role and keyboard navigation are inherited from reka-ui.

findings.title: MobileFloatingToc dropdown + GallerySearchBar filter panel: bespoke absolutely-positioned overlays vs. native popover
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/MobileFloatingToc.vue:293-313 — `.floating-toc-dropdown { position: absolute; top: 100%; z-index: 2; }` with a `.floating-toc-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1; }` click-away shim. web/src/components/visualization/gallery/GallerySearchBar.vue:165-183 — `.filter-anchor { position: absolute; top: 100%; z-index: var(--z-bar); }`. Both overlays: no collision avoidance, hard-coded z-index integers, manual click-away logic.
findings.current_state: Two separate dropdown-style overlays are hand-rolled using absolute positioning + a backdrop div. MobileFloatingToc.vue uses `position: fixed` for the backdrop (blocks interaction with the rest of the page) and a manual `@click.away` pattern via a ref + outside-click handler. GallerySearchBar uses a simpler `v-if` + Transition. Neither implementation has viewport-edge collision avoidance. glass-ui ships `Popover`/`PopoverContent` (reka-ui PopoverRoot, full collision avoidance, Escape, outside-click, top-layer positioning) and the native `popover` attr path via glass-ui's top-layer grammar.
findings.proposed: Transpose both overlays to `<Popover>` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/popover`. For MobileFloatingToc: the TOC bar button becomes `<PopoverTrigger as-child>` wrapping the existing `Button`, the dropdown content becomes `<PopoverContent side="bottom" align="start">`. The `.floating-toc-backdrop` div and its manual z-index stacking are deleted — reka-ui handles outside-dismiss and focus-return. For GallerySearchBar: the filter drawer's `<Transition>` + `.filter-anchor` wrapper become `<PopoverContent side="bottom" align="start">` inside a `<Popover>`. The Transition entry/exit animation is replaced by glass-ui's `popover-animate` class or the `@starting-style` CSS carried in glass-ui 4.0's overlay grammar.

findings.title: AnimationControls play button: bespoke rainbow glass pill bypasses glass-ui material system
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/AnimationControls.vue:139-187 — `.play-btn` has hardcoded `background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.15), …)`, `backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.4)`, `-webkit-backdrop-filter`, `border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.25)`, `color: #fff`, bespoke `::before` rainbow gradient with `@keyframes rainbow-drift`, bespoke `::after` specular, `transform: scale(1.08)` on `:hover`, `transform: scale(0.93)` on `:active`, a literal `transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.3s, border-color 0.3s` (raw bezier, not token). It is a raw `<button>` element, not a glass-ui Button.
findings.current_state: The play button is a fully bespoke glass pill with hardcoded RGBA colours, a raw `backdrop-filter`, a rainbow gradient animation keyed on `is-playing`, and hardcoded scale transforms on hover/active. It bypasses the glass-ui material system (`--glass-*` tokens, `glass-{tier}` class ladder, `cartoon-surface` or `glass-card` wrapper), the `--spring-*` motion tokens, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` check is only applied to the rainbow animation — the `transform: scale` hover/active is not gated.
findings.proposed: Transpose to `<Button variant="glass" size="icon" class="play-btn">` from glass-ui. The glass material (blur, border, specular `::before`) comes from `glass-pill` or `glass-btn` (glass-ui surfaces.css). The rainbow `is-playing` state maps to a `Pulse aura` overlay (`<Pulse variant="aura" intensity="vivid" class="rounded-full" />` inside the button, gated by `:class="{ 'opacity-100': anim.playing, 'opacity-0': !anim.playing }"`) — this replaces the hand-rolled `::before` gradient drift and is PRM-aware out of the box. Hover scale becomes `cartoon-surface`'s `translate: var(--lift-sm)` or a `hover-scale` utility from glass-ui. The raw `transition:` line is replaced by glass-ui's `--duration-normal` + `--spring-smooth` tokens. The `-webkit-backdrop-filter` prefix is deleted (Baseline 2022).

findings.title: Dep pins two major versions stale: glass-ui ^3.1.0 vs 4.0.0, keyframes.js ^2.2.0 vs 4.2.0
findings.evidence: web/package.json: `@mkbabb/glass-ui: "^3.1.0"`, `@mkbabb/keyframes.js: "^2.2.0"`, `@mkbabb/value.js: "^0.10.0"`. `npm view @mkbabb/glass-ui version` → 4.0.0; `npm view @mkbabb/keyframes.js version` → 4.2.0; `npm view @mkbabb/value.js version` → 0.12.0. RUN-BOARD.md (docs/constellation/tri-tranche-run/) treats glass-ui 3.3.0 as the uncleared hinge E1 — stale; 4.0.0 shipped. Every finding in this audit (D4-01 through D4-11) uses glass-ui 4.0 primitives that are already published but unreachable behind the ^3.1.0 pin.

Run `npm install`, then run `vue-tsc --noEmit` + `npm run build` to surface any API-shape changes introduced in the major bumps. findings.title: useOffsetPagination: local fork of a retired glass-ui subpath
findings.evidence: web/src/composables/useOffsetPagination.ts:9-13 — comment says "Forked verbatim from glass-ui v0.9.3 source … at glass-ui v1.0 cut — the upstream subpath @mkbabb/glass-ui/pagination was retired (zero production consumers across the constellation). Per MIGRATION.md §3.1 the canonical migration is 'copy from v0.9.3 source.'" Used at AdminAuditLog.vue:26 and AdminUserList.vue:54.
findings.current_state: An 83-line composable is a verbatim copy of a pre-v1.0 glass-ui composable, kept because the upstream subpath was retired. The copy adds a maintenance burden: if the active-loader fetch shape evolves, this fork drifts silently. glass-ui's `InfiniteScroll` + `useInfiniteScroll` cover the cursor/sentinel-based pattern but not the jump-to-page admin use case.
findings.proposed: This composable is correctly local given the retired subpath — no glass-ui primitive matches the active-loader-shaped contract. The finding is to add a doc comment update noting this is intentional and bounded to the 2 admin call sites. If/when glass-ui ships a `usePagedLoader` composable (a glass-ui ask below), this composable is retired in favour of it. No immediate code change required beyond the comment.

findings.title: PaperView teleport-overlay: bespoke fixed-position radial gradient backdrop instead of glass-ui Dialog backdrop
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperView.vue:316 — `<div class="teleport-overlay" />`. Lines 502-514: `.teleport-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: var(--z-overlay); background: radial-gradient(…); opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 180ms var(--ease-out-expo); will-change: opacity; }`. The overlay is never explicitly triggered — it is always `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` in the current codebase (the JS that was supposed to drive it is absent).
findings.current_state: A `div.teleport-overlay` with `will-change: opacity` sits in the DOM on every paper page visit, occupying a GPU layer permanently for an effect that is never triggered (opacity stays at 0 — the JS writer is absent from PaperView.vue's script block). It is dead weight: a GPU compositing layer, a `will-change` hint, and 12 lines of scoped CSS for zero visual effect.
findings.proposed: Delete the `<div class="teleport-overlay" />` element and its `.teleport-overlay` scoped style block entirely. If the overlay effect was intended for a future search-modal backdrop, it should be deferred to when that feature is implemented — likely via glass-ui Dialog's built-in backdrop (which the PaperSearchModal already uses via `<Teleport to="body">`). The permanent GPU layer is pure waste.

glassui_asks.name: tab-panel-animation
glassui_asks.what: Ship `[data-state="active"][role="tabpanel"]` slide-in animation natively inside the Tabs primitive's stylesheet (or via an `animations.css` rule keyed on the same data-attributes reka-ui's TabsContent sets). Token: `var(--ease-standard)` for the easing, `0.18s` or `var(--duration-fast)` for duration. Include `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; }` guard. Once shipped, the identical local carry in `fourier/web/src/style.css:83-96` is deleted.
glassui_asks.why: Fourier carries this animation locally as an acknowledged interim hold (style.css comment: 'local carry pending glass-ui's Tabs primitive shipping this on its own'). It is the only cross-app CSS rule that targets reka-ui internals from outside the primitive — a fragile coupling that belongs inside the primitive's own stylesheet.

glassui_asks.name: usePagedLoader
glassui_asks.what: Ship a `usePagedLoader<T>` composable (subpath `@mkbabb/glass-ui/pagination` or merged into the main barrel) with the active-loader contract: `fetchFn: (limit, offset) => Promise<{ data: T[]; total: number }>`, `pageSize?`, and a `loadPage(p?)` imperative. This is the shape `fourier/web/src/composables/useOffsetPagination.ts` forks from glass-ui v0.9.3.
glassui_asks.why: Fourier holds a verbatim fork of a composable that glass-ui retired at v1.0 with no replacement. The fork covers a legitimate pagination shape (admin jump-to-page with an active fetch) that vueuse's `useOffsetPagination` does not cover (passive state, external total ref). Shipping this upstream ends the fork and brings the admin pagination under glass-ui's maintenance.

glassui_asks.name: viz-amber-token-contrast
glassui_asks.what: Rebaseline the light-mode `--viz-amber` token from `hsl(35 70% 42%)` (≈3.54:1, WCAG AA fail) to `hsl(35 76% 35%)` (≈4.6:1, AA pass). Dark-mode stays `hsl(37 73% 67%)` (already compliant). fourier carries a `:root { --viz-amber: hsl(35 76% 35%); }` override in style.css (D.W4.d) with an explicit comment calling it a local stop-gap until glass-ui rebaselines.
glassui_asks.why: The override is a colour-contrast fix (axe audit finding) that fourier carries locally against glass-ui's shipped token. It belongs in glass-ui so all constellation consumers inherit the fix without per-app overrides.

open_questions: D4-02 (rAF → NumericAnimation): keyframes.js 4.2.0 NumericAnimation accepts a `TimingFunction` (callable) for the ping-pong easing, but the animation store's `ANIMATION_EASINGS` map produces callables from value.js — confirm that after the dep bump (D4-12) the `getEasingFn()` return type satisfies keyframes.js 4.2.0's `TimingFunction | Easing` union before committing the store transposition.

D4-06 (FullscreenViewer → Dialog): glass-ui's DialogContent applies `max-width` and `rounded-xl` by default. The fullscreen viewer needs full-viewport coverage. Confirm whether glass-ui 4.0's Dialog accepts a `variant='fullscreen'` prop or whether the override must be via `--dialog-max-w: 100dvw; --dialog-radius: 0` CSS custom properties on the DialogContent element.

D4-03 (coefficient popover → HoverPopover): The trigger for the coefficient popover is a KaTeX-rendered `span` inside a `v-html` block — there is no Vue component boundary around each coefficient. Confirm the interop path: does reka-ui's HoverCardTrigger accept a raw DOM element reference (via `as-child` + a wrapper span), or does this require a different strategy (e.g. a Popover with manual open/close driven by the existing event-delegation approach)?

D4-12 (dep bump): glass-ui 4.0.0 is a major version. The K-deploy tranche (project_tranche_k.md) booked this bump as K.W4 and specifically called out the `glass-dock-1` duplicate VT-name e2e blocker as unblocked by it. Confirm whether bumping glass-ui ^4.0.0 in isolation (without the full K.W4 wave) introduces any API breaks in the 11 currently-used glass-ui subpaths (`/button`, `/slider`, `/configurator`, `/tooltip`, `/hover-card`, `/tabs`, `/dropdown-menu`, `/select`, `/collapsible`, `/dock`, `/infinite-scroll`).

D4-11 (play button glass): The rainbow-drift `::before` is a design signature of the animation controls — audacious, proportioned, intentional (per the standing design directive). Confirm whether a `Pulse aura` overlay achieves the same 'rainbow while playing' read, or whether the bespoke multi-stop gradient animation is design-load-bearing and should stay as a scoped exception while the other glass violations (backdrop-filter bypass, raw colours, non-token transitions) are remediated.

E1.dimension: E1 — Mathematical-Animation Opportunities (the Fourier signature motion language)
E1.verdict: The app is motion-CORRECT on the platform axes (View-Transitions route-morph, IntersectionObserver rAF-gating, ping-pong convergence loop) but motion-ABSENT on the orchestration/signature axis — exactly the thesis the J.WC motion spec already wrote ("Convergence is the motion signature… used at ZERO sites"). For a Fourier project the single most under-exploited brand asset is the math itself as motion: the partial-sum settling onto its target, the epicycle chain drawing its own trace, harmonics accumulating one beat at a time, spectral bars rising in amplitude order. The renderers already COMPUTE every quantity these reveals need (precomputed trail, partial_sums per level, amplitude-sorted spectrum, harmonicProgress sweep) — they are simply snapped to a flat appear or driven by raw performance.now() oscillators with no reduced-motion guard. The siblings now ship the precise primitives (keyframes 4.2.0 DrawSVG + MotionPath; glass-ui 4.0 useStaggerReveal/useCountup/useSpring) and fourier consumes essentially none of them. The highest-leverage M wave is a single "convergence-reveal" motion grammar applied at first-paint of every canvas + spectrum, plus harmonic-accumulation staggers — audacious within proportion, PRM-honoured, INP-safe.

findings.title: No signature reveal: every canvas/spectrum snaps to a flat appear — the partial sum never visibly converges onto its target
findings.evidence: BasisCanvas.vue drawFrame() renders the full chain immediately on data arrival (watcher A clears trail + redraws, no entrance choreography); ConvergencePlot.vue onMounted just sets t=0; playing=true; startLoop() (line 324). docs/tranches/J/design/WC-design-motion.md §2 already names 'the series converging onto the title' as THE one memorable reveal and notes the orchestration tier is used at ZERO sites.
findings.current_state: On compute, the epicycle chain, ghost path, and partial-sum curve all appear fully-formed in one frame; the only entrance motion anywhere is the convergence ping-pong loop that plays AFTER paint. There is no moment where the viewer watches N=1 grow to N=full.
findings.proposed: Add ONE 'convergence reveal' as the brand signature: on first paint of a fresh dataset, drive anim.t (or a dedicated reveal clock) from 0→1 with a keyframes.js spring so the partial sum literally settles onto the ghost target — harmonics accumulate, the curve tightens, the tip lands. Drive it through keyframes 4.2.0's Animation/Sequence (already the morph engine) so it is one orchestrated graph, not a hand-rolled rAF. Terminal state = full curve at rest, so PRM/reduced-motion reveals instantly (inv-29 floor). This is the gestalt move E6 ties to: the math IS the motion.
findings.wave_hint: M (signature-motion wave) — the headline; feeds E6

findings.title: keyframes.js 4.2.0 ships DrawSVG + MotionPath — the two primitives built for epicycle tracing — and fourier consumes neither
findings.evidence: keyframes.js dist/keyframes.d.ts exports DrawSVG (stroke-dashoffset sweep over path length, 'G.W13') and MotionPath (offset-distance over an author offset-path, 'F.W12'). grep across web/src shows zero DrawSVG/MotionPath/drawSVG usage. FourierMorphSvg.vue renders a static <path> with no draw-on; the trail in trail.ts is a manually-pushed point array.
findings.current_state: The morph route paints SVG shapes with no stroke-reveal; the epicycle trace is a Canvas2D point-buffer redrawn each frame. The single most on-brand effect for a Fourier demo — a curve drawing itself along its arc-length — is hand-absent despite the engine shipping it.
findings.proposed: Use keyframes DrawSVG to make the morph/decorative Fourier glyph (FourierMorphSvg) draw-on at mount (stroke-dashoffset 0→full over ~900ms spring), and use MotionPath to send a comet/tip token gliding along the reconstructed contour as the partial sum completes. Both are CSS-native (offset-path / stroke-dasharray) so they are GPU-cheap and PRM-collapsible. This retires the bespoke shimmer-glow tip in favour of a platform-native, arc-length-true trace.

findings.title: Two canvas oscillators pulse forever off raw performance.now() with NO reduced-motion guard (tip glow + golden shimmer)
findings.evidence: epicycles.ts:280 drawTipDot glowAlpha = 0.2 + 0.1*Math.sin(performance.now()/300); golden-shimmer.ts goldenShimmerAlpha() = 0.85 + 0.15*Math.sin(performance.now()/200). grep for 'reduced|matchMedia|prefers' in golden-shimmer.ts returns nothing. These animate purely as a function of wall-clock — they keep pulsing even when anim.playing is false (any redraw re-samples now()).
findings.current_state: The tip-dot halo and the golden hover-shimmer breathe continuously, decoupled from the animation clock and unconditioned on prefers-reduced-motion — a standing inv-29 (progressive-enhancement floor) gap and a subtle correctness smell (motion when the user paused).
findings.proposed: Route both oscillators through a single shared motion-phase source gated on prefers-reduced-motion (matchMedia, cached + listener) AND on anim.playing — when reduced-motion or paused, return the steady-state alpha (no sin term). Idiomatically, derive the phase from the same clock the convergence reveal uses so all canvas motion shares one heartbeat rather than three independent now() reads. findings.title: Spectral bars 'pop in' via flat CSS transition-all instead of rising in amplitude order (harmonic-accumulation stagger)
findings.evidence: CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:91 bar fill uses 'transition-all duration-500 ease-out' on width; the TransitionGroup 'coeff-list' (lines 147-163) slides rows in via translateX with a flat per-row transition — no index-staggered onset. FrequencyGraph.vue draw() paints all bars in one pass each frame; bars never animate their height on data arrival.

findings.proposed: Apply glass-ui 4.0 useStaggerReveal (staggerMs ≈ 55, amplitude-descending order so the dominant harmonic lands first) to the CoefficientsSpectrum rows, and animate FrequencyGraph bar heights from 0→target with a per-bar staggered spring (keyframes stagger()) keyed on the amplitude-sorted index. This is 'stagger = harmonic accumulation' from the motion spec, applied where it is most literally true. PRM: reveal-immediately fallback already built into useStaggerReveal.

findings.title: Convergence numeric readouts (energy %, N=k/total) jump discretely — no convergence-as-counter motion
findings.evidence: EquationPanel.vue MetricBadge :amount=(energy*100).toFixed(1) updates as a plain reactive string; ConvergenceTimeline.vue timeline-count renders N={{activeCount}}/{{total}} as a raw span; BasisCanvas label `N = ${level}` (drawEpicycleFrame:197) is drawn text. findings.title: animation store: bespoke rAF loop duplicates RAFPlayback exactly
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/animation.ts:51-81 — hand-rolled startLoop()/stopRAF() with a module-level rafId: number | null, a closure-captured startTime, and a manual ping-pong fold. The comment at line 46 reads 'Manual rAF loop with alternate (ping-pong).'
findings.current_state: The store implements the entire RAFPlayback contract from scratch: generation-guarded handle, start-time seed, ping-pong cycle fold (cycle % 2 === 0 ? frac : 1 − frac), speed scaling, watch(speed, …) restart, and IntersectionObserver gating added as a separate layer on top. 110 lines for what RAFPlayback.loop() + a Sequence with yoyo(true).repeat(Infinity) provides in ~8 lines, with none of the generation-guard correctness.
findings.proposed: Replace the rAF loop body with a RAFPlayback instance (light import, zero value.js cost). The ping-pong is Sequence.yoyo(true).repeat(Infinity) driving a single dummy Animation whose interpFrames emits the normalized t. Speed scaling is sequence.timeScale(speed). Visibility gating stays as the IntersectionObserver ref-count (call sequence.pause()/resume() from setCanvasVisible). The store shrinks from 147 to ~60 lines and gains the generation guard, bind-proof stop, and correct pause/resume contract for free.

findings.title: useCurveTransition: bare rAF loop with hand-rolled easing instead of RAFPlayback.play()
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:36-53 — startTransition() constructs a raw rAF loop: let rafId: number | null = null; rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); with a manual elapsed/DURATION progress formula. Easing is easeInOutSine from value.js called directly as a JS function.
findings.current_state: The transition loop has no generation guard. If startTransition() is called twice in rapid succession (function-switch before the 500ms settles), the first rafId leaks — the returned cancel is for the second loop but the first keeps firing. The easing is a bare JS fn (t: number) => number with no CSS twin, so the spring compositor path is permanently unavailable.
findings.proposed: Replace with const pb = new RAFPlayback(); pb.play(500, (progress) => { state.progress = springTimingFunction({ response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.86 }).fn(progress); onFrame(); }, { respectReducedMotion: true }). RAFPlayback.play() is generation-guarded; a new call to startTransition cancels the previous one by calling pb.stop() first. The springTimingFunction Easing carries a .css twin if WAAPI delegation is ever needed. Cancel is pb.stop().

findings.title: ConvergencePlot: third independent rAF loop — identical ping-pong pattern as animation store
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:57-73 — startLoop()/stopLoop() with its own rafId: number | null, loopStartTime: number | null, and the identical cycle % 2 === 0 ? frac : 1 − frac ping-pong. This is a verbatim structural copy of the animation store loop.
findings.current_state: ConvergencePlot owns its own local t ref and plays independently from the main animation store. The loop has the same correctness risks as E3-02: no generation guard, no reduced-motion snap, no visibility gating (the convergence plot burns rAF even when scrolled below the fold).
findings.proposed: Transpose to RAFPlayback.loop() + the same ping-pong Sequence pattern as E3-02 proposes for the store, OR use RAFPlayback.play(animDuration / speed, onTick) where onTick receives normalized progress and the ping-pong is handled by watching the play promise and re-calling with the mirrored phase. Add respectReducedMotion: true to the play call. Wire an IntersectionObserver on canvasRef to park/resume the playback, matching the I.γ pattern already proven in BasisCanvas.vue.

findings.title: useCanvasHover: two independent rAF loops (scale lerp + shimmer) should be SpringProgress + RAFPlayback.drive()
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-81 — updateHoverScale() is a hand-rolled exponential lerp loop (currentScale += diff * 0.12) with hoverAnimFrame: number | null. shimmerTick() is a second independent rAF loop with shimmerRafId: number | null. Total: four raw rAF handle sites in one file.
findings.current_state: The scale lerp at diff * 0.12 is an ad-hoc exponential smoother — SmoothProgress with damping: 0.12 is the precise equivalent, but without the generation guard or the settle threshold (the loop runs until Math.abs(diff) < 0.002 with a bespoke check). The shimmer loop is a pure redraw ticker with no physics; it runs at full 60fps any time any basis is hovered, regardless of whether the shimmer value is changing.
findings.proposed: Scale animation: replace with const scaleSpring = new SpringProgress({ response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.86 }); scaleSpring.play((value) => { currentScale = value; onRedraw(); }); then scaleSpring.target = hoverScale on enter, scaleSpring.target = baseScale on leave. The spring auto-settles — no hoverAnimFrame handle needed. Shimmer: the shimmer is a time-varying alpha from a clock, not a spring; it should ride the main animation store clock (anim.t already ticks at 60fps when playing) via a Vue watch instead of its own loop. If the shimmer needs an independent clock, RAFPlayback.loop() replaces the manual shimmerTick with one generation-guarded entry.

findings.title: useFourierMorph: three-phase morph driven by Animation as a bare progress ticker — replace with Sequence
findings.evidence: web/src/composables/useFourierMorph.ts:122-143 — createTweenAnimation() constructs an Animation with useWAAPI: false and addFrame('0%', { v: '0px' }, callback) purely to get a rAF-driven progress ticker. Three sequential await new Promise() wrappers chain the settle-out / morph / settle-in phases manually.
findings.current_state: Using the heavy CSS engine (loaded via loadAnimationEngine()) purely as a rAF driver is an architectural mismatch — the engine does CSS keyframe parsing + value.js interpolation for a variable that is never applied to the DOM (v: '0px' → '1px' is discarded; only the raw time is used). The three-phase chain cannot be scrubbed, cannot be reversed, and leaks the Animation instance if the component unmounts mid-phase (currentAnim.stop() in stopAnim() handles most cases but there is a race in the await chains).
findings.proposed: Replace with three NumericAnimation instances (LIGHT, zero value.js cost at import time — the heavy CSS engine is no longer needed at all for this path): const phase1 = new NumericAnimation({ v: [0, 1] }, { duration: settleOutMs, timingFunction: springTimingFunction(...) }); const seq = new Sequence().add(phase1).add(phase2).add(phase3); await seq.play(). Each child's onFrame drives the matching interpolation callback. seq.stop() in onUnmounted replaces the three-way currentAnim teardown. The Sequence is scrub-capable and reverse-capable for free. The loadAnimationEngine() dynamic import is eliminated from this path entirely.

findings.title: Easing catalog backed by raw value.js function imports — blocks the spring linear() compositor path
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/easings.ts:10-16 imports easeInOutSine, easeInOutCubic, easeInOutQuad, easeInOutExpo, easeInOutCirc directly as TimingFunction values from @mkbabb/value.js. ANIMATION_EASINGS stores them as plain EasingFn = (t: number) => number entries with no css field. useCurveTransition.ts:8 imports easeInOutSine directly.
findings.current_state: The ANIMATION_EASINGS record stores callable functions only — there is no Easing = { fn, css } pair. This means: (1) the animation store's easedT = ANIMATION_EASINGS[easing.value].fn(t.value) is correct for JS interpolation but the CSS twin is never available; (2) if any future path uses these easings with WAAPI, the compositor will receive 'linear' instead of the faithful CSS curve; (3) the spring linear() compositor path (springTimingFunction's .css field) is architecturally invisible.
findings.proposed: Migrate ANIMATION_EASINGS entries to typed Easing = { fn, css } pairs. For the standard curves, the CSS twin is a cubic-bezier() literal (value.js's timingFunctions carry a .css sibling — use it). Add two spring presets using springTimingFunction({ response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.86 }) and springTimingFunction({ response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6 }) which produce typed Easing with .fn and .css: 'linear(…)' — these become the 'spring' and 'bounce' options in the UI picker. The animation store's easedT computation is unchanged (it reads .fn). WAAPI paths automatically get the faithful CSS twin.

findings.title: usePointDrag: bespoke pointer-event state machine — replace with Draggable
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/usePointDrag.ts:1-67 — hand-rolls pointer capture (e.target as Element).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId), dragStartIdx, dragPrevPt tracking, and manual dx/dy accumulation. No velocity sampling, no fling, no spring settle.
findings.current_state: The contour-editor drag is a plain bespoke pointer state machine. It correctly uses pointer capture but lacks any spring-follow or release-velocity fling. The magnet-falloff influence radius is bespoke influence propagation that runs per-move synchronously. There is no reduced-motion handling.
findings.proposed: The influence-propagation logic (neighbor falloff) is specific enough to stay; but the pointer-capture boilerplate should delegate to Draggable for each axis. For the magnet drag: const dragX = new Draggable({ axis: 'x', transform: (c) => c - rect.left }); const dragY = new Draggable({ axis: 'y', … }); dragX.attach(svgEl); dragX.subscribe((vx) => { points[idx].x = vx; propagate(idx, dx, dy); }). Release-velocity fling gives the editor a natural flick-and-settle feel with zero spring code. Draggable.detach() replaces the manual removeEventListener teardown.

findings.title: GalleryMarquee: CSS-keyframe marquee is not stagger-aware — stagger() enables per-card reveal on entry
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/gallery/GalleryMarquee.vue:116-133 — marquee-scroll-left / marquee-scroll-right are infinite CSS keyframe animations on .marquee-inner. Cards enter the viewport all-at-once with no stagger; the DOM-duplicate trick (v-for with 'dup-' key) runs both tracks at fixed 45s/50s regardless of card count.
findings.current_state: The marquee is a CSS animation loop — correct for the infinite scroll. But when the gallery first mounts or the user scrolls to reveal the marquee, every card in both tracks appears simultaneously. There is no per-card stagger on entry (opacity/translateY reveal). stagger() from keyframes.js 4.x is a pure delay-distribution function (light, zero value.js import) that produces per-index delay offsets handed to an AnimationGroup or to individual CSS transitions.
findings.proposed: Keep the CSS infinite marquee for the scroll loop. Add a mount-entry stagger for the initial reveal: on GalleryMarquee mounted, collect the .marquee-item elements, compute const delay = stagger(items.length, { each: 30, from: 'first', ease: springTimingFunction({ response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.8 }).fn }). Apply delay(i, items.length) as a CSS custom property --stagger-delay on each item; the item's own CSS transition uses it: transition: opacity 0.4s var(--ease-standard) var(--stagger-delay, 0ms), transform 0.4s …. Reduces to pure CSS execution after the delay assignment — no per-frame JS.

findings.title: PaperView scroll navigation: six raw rAF calls in useScrollNavigation — ScrollTimeline opportunity
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/useScrollNavigation.ts:89,106,138,159,163,187 — six requestAnimationFrame() calls implementing: overlay paint timing, teleport correction loop (up to 20 frames), short-jump smooth scroll timing. PaperView.vue:171 adds a seventh for progressRaf (scroll progress read).
findings.current_state: The teleport correction loop (lines 130-165) polls up to 20 frames checking if the scroll position has stabilized within STABILITY_PX=6. This is a bespoke convergence loop with no back-off and no settle threshold. The progressRaf in PaperView.vue reads scrollTop each frame to compute a reading-progress indicator.
findings.proposed: Teleport correction: the loop polls for DOM stability — RAFPlayback.loop() with a generation guard replaces the manual frame counter and eliminates the stale-cancel risk when navigateTo() is called twice quickly. ScrollTimeline for progress: the scroll-progress read in PaperView.vue is exactly the ScrollTimeline.tick() use case — const tl = new ScrollTimeline({ getScrollY: () => scroller.scrollTop, getViewportHeight: () => scroller.clientHeight, threshold: 1.0 }); call tl.tickDt(dt) in a RAFPlayback.loop() and read tl.progress. The built-in SmoothProgress smoother inside ScrollTimeline eliminates the manual debounce logic.

findings.title: springLinearStops / springTimingFunction not used anywhere — --spring-* tokens are dark
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'springLinear\|springTiming' /Users/mkbabb/Programming/fourier-analysis/web/src returns zero hits. glass-ui 4.0.0 regenerates its --spring-* CSS custom properties from springLinearStops at build time; fourier never calls either function.
findings.current_state: fourier's CSS uses --ease-standard, --ease-in, --ease-out from glass-ui tokens but never the --spring-* spring tokens. AnimationControls.vue line 196 uses var(--ease-standard) for icon-swap transitions; the play button hover/active transitions at lines 155/181 use transition: transform 0.2s, which is bare cubic-bezier. The epicycle hover scale lerp (diff * 0.12 per frame) is physics without a CSS twin.
findings.proposed: Use springTimingFunction({ response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.86 }) for the epicycle hover scale spring (replaces the bespoke diff*0.12 lerp — see E3-05). For CSS transitions on interactive elements (play button, panel open/close), use springLinearStops({ response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.86 }) to emit a linear() string that rides the compositor. A small helper const springEase = springLinearStops({ response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.86 }) assigned at module init produces the CSS string once; apply it as transition-timing-function in scoped styles.

findings.title: FourierMorphSvg SVG path draw-in should use DrawSVG instead of a timed CSS stroke-dashoffset
findings.evidence: web/src/components/decorative/FourierMorphSvg.vue — SvgFilters.vue line 51 uses requestAnimationFrame for an SVG timing trigger. The decorative SVG path has stroke-based rendering but no computed stroke-dashoffset animation. The draw-in effect (if present) would be a raw CSS animation.
findings.current_state: The fourier morph SVG in the decorative layer has no keyframes.js-driven draw-in. Any stroke animation is either always-visible or CSS-only without the getTotalLength() normalization. DrawSVG from keyframes.js 4.1+ provides: one getTotalLength() read, stroke-dasharray = L, stroke-dashoffset swept L → 0, WAAPI-eligible, with from/to percent control and respectReducedMotion built in.
findings.proposed: On component mount, const { fromDrawSVG } = await loadAnimationEngine(); const anim = fromDrawSVG(pathEl, { duration: 1200, timingFunction: springTimingFunction({ response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.9 }), from: 0, to: 1, respectReducedMotion: true }); await anim.play(). The path draws in with a spring settle on the stroke tip. A ViewTimeline (createNativeTimeline({ kind: 'view', subject: pathEl })) can make the draw-in scroll-driven on Chromium, falling back to the rAF path on other engines via the same call.

findings.title: GalleryCard panel open/close uses CSS transition without spring easing — flip() opportunity
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/gallery/GalleryCard.vue uses a v-show / CSS transition for the expanded card detail panel. AnimationControls.vue play button lines 155-181 use transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.3s — cubic-bezier implicit. No spring easing on any layout-changing panel transition.
findings.current_state: Panel expand/collapse is CSS transition with no easing specification (default ease) or a bare 0.2s duration. The FLIP pattern (measure First rect → mutate → measure Last rect → invert → play) is not used anywhere in fourier despite it being the idiomatic solution for layout-changing transitions where the Before and After geometry differ.
findings.proposed: For gallery card expand/collapse: const spring = springTimingFunction({ response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8 }); await flip(cardEl, () => cardEl.classList.toggle('expanded'), { duration: 400, timingFunction: spring }). flip() batches the two getBoundingClientRect reads (no layout thrash), inverts the transform, and plays with the spring overshoot. For the shared-element transition when a card opens into a modal: flipShared(cardEl, modalEl, { duration: 350, timingFunction: spring }) animates cardEl onto modalEl's rect — Motion layoutId equivalent, zero GSAP dependency.

findings.title: animate() single-call front door not used — every animation site constructs Animation by hand
findings.evidence: useFourierMorph.ts:149 calls new AnimationCtor({ duration, iterationCount, timingFunction, fillMode, useWAAPI }) followed by .addFrame().addFrame().parse(). This is the four-step manual lifecycle. The animate() front door (shipped in 4.0, published in 4.2) collapses it to one call.
findings.current_state: The morph composable loads the engine, extracts the Animation constructor, and manually builds CSS keyframe animations. Any future animation site will repeat this same four-step boilerplate. The animate() dispatch (CSS string / keyframe map / vars array / MotionPath spec) is not available at ^2.2.0 and is not used at all in fourier.
findings.proposed: After the ^4.2.0 bump: const { animate } = await loadAnimationEngine(); const anim = animate(el, { v: ['0px', '1px'] }, { duration: ms, timingFunction: easing, useWAAPI: false }); anim.play(). For the morph path, NumericAnimation (LIGHT, synchronous) is even simpler and avoids the dynamic import entirely for non-CSS interpolation. Reserve animate() for actual DOM-targeting animations (the play button rainbow, the gallery card entry, SVG path reveals).

findings.title: PaperView reading progress uses raw rAF + scroll listener instead of ScrollTimeline
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperView.vue:171 — progressRaf = requestAnimationFrame(writeProgress) with line 185 cancelAnimationFrame(progressRaf). The pattern samples scrollTop to compute a reading progress percentage.
findings.current_state: The progress read is a raw rAF loop attached separately from the teleport correction loops in useScrollNavigation. There is no smoothing (ScrollTimeline's built-in SmoothProgress is absent), no boundary snap, and no reduced-motion handling. On browsers that support native scroll-driven, createNativeTimeline({ kind: 'scroll', source: scroller }) would move the progress computation to the compositor thread.
findings.proposed: Replace with const tl = new ScrollTimeline({ getScrollY: () => scroller.scrollTop, getViewportHeight: () => scroller.scrollHeight, threshold: 1.0, smoothing: false }). Sample in a RAFPlayback.loop(): tl.tick(); progressValue.value = tl.progress. On Chromium, createNativeTimeline({ kind: 'scroll', source: scroller }) provides a native AnimationTimeline; fourier attaches a zero-duration Animation to it via the additive WAAPI bridge to drive a CSS @property reading-progress off the compositor. Falls back to the JS sampler on Firefox/Safari.

findings.title: No reduced-motion handling on any non-CSS animation site
findings.evidence: animation.ts:139 watch(speed, …) restarts the loop but never checks prefers-reduced-motion. useCurveTransition.ts:36-53 runs the rAF loop unconditionally. useCanvasHover.ts has no reduced-motion check. The @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) guard in GalleryMarquee.vue:129-133 is the only existing PRM handling in the entire codebase.
findings.current_state: Every JS-driven animation (epicycle clock, convergence plot, curve transition, hover scale, morph) runs at full fidelity under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The RAFPlayback.play(..., { respectReducedMotion: true }) and SpringProgress({ respectReducedMotion: true }) options auto-snap to the rest frame — but these options are inaccessible at the current ^2.2.0 pin AND are not wired even after the pin bump.
findings.proposed: After the ^4.2.0 bump: (1) animation store: if (window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) { t.value = 0; return; } before startLoop(); (2) RAFPlayback.play() with respectReducedMotion: true on all three-phase morph transitions; (3) SpringProgress with respectReducedMotion: true on the hover scale spring; (4) Sequence with respectReducedMotion: true on the morphTo Sequence. The withReducedMotion gate inside RAFPlayback is a single check the library already implements — fourier just needs to opt in.

glassui_asks.name: spring-scrubber-integration
glassui_asks.what: Expose a SpringProgress-driven variant of the Slider scrub thumb — when the user releases the scrub thumb mid-drag, the thumb should spring-settle to the dropped position rather than snapping. This requires the glass-ui Slider to accept an optional SpringProgress instance for the value-settle phase.
glassui_asks.why: GlassTimeline.vue (web/src/components/visualization/GlassTimeline.vue) drives the animation scrub bar. The value-commit event currently snaps the t value to the dropped position. A spring-settle on the thumb (while the underlying t value commits instantly to keep the epicycle frame correct) would give the Slider a premium feel consistent with glass-ui's spring vocabulary without fourier needing to reach into Slider internals.
