E4.dimension: E4 — value.js 0.12.0 leverage: colour + motion adoption surface
E4.verdict: fourier pins @mkbabb/value.js ^0.10.0 (installed 0.10.0); the published library is 0.12.0 — two major-minor releases ahead. The gap contains six high-leverage capabilities fourier does not use: perceptual-space colour mixing (mixColorsN), OKLCH-safe contrast helpers (computeSafeAccent / safeAccentColor), per-frame zero-alloc WAAPI colour serialisation (toAnimationString + cssColorInterpKeyword), a cusp-aware gamut-mapping upgrade, and the computed-endpoint cache perf tier. Fourier's colour stack is a bespoke island of hand-rolled HSL templating, per-file spectrumColor quadruplication, and a 118-line custom CSS-var-to-hex parser — all of which value.js 0.12.0 supplants cleanly. Bumping the pin unlocks perceptually-uniform harmonic-colour ramps, OKLab-interpolated dark-mode toggle, contrast-safe swatch accents, and a forward adoption seam for the planned sampleColorRamp (0.13.0). Zero new science required; all leverage is composition over shipped kernels.

findings.title: Version pin ^0.10.0 leaves two minor releases of leverage on the table
findings.evidence: web/package.json:18 — @mkbabb/value.js ^0.10.0; web/node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/package.json — version 0.10.0 installed. Published version: 0.12.0 (npm view @mkbabb/value.js version = 0.12.0). Gap spans 0.11.0 (F-tranche hand-off: computedEndpointCache B3+B5, lerpArray SoA D2, formatColor alpha-omit B1b, O(1) color dispatch A1, maximal-munch unit A2) and 0.12.0 (N.W7.A: toAnimationString, cssColorInterpKeyword, computeSafeAccent, safeAccentColor, mixColorsN, gamutMap wide-gamut egress, light-dark/currentColor sentinels, PathGeometry, bumpLayoutEpoch/getLayoutEpoch, LRU memoize, ParsedColorUnit).
findings.current_state: Fourier installs 0.10.0. All N.W7.A capabilities (the keyframes next-slice) are absent. The 0.11.0 perf tier (computed endpoint cache, SoA lerp, per-frame zero-alloc) is also absent despite being a direct dependency of every colour animation the canvas renderer runs.
findings.proposed: Bump web/package.json to ^0.12.0, run npm install, regen package-lock.json. This is a pure fourier-local action (inv-16; value.js already published). Verify npm ci resolves single-copy lock (glass-ui 4.0.0 / keyframes 4.2.0 / value.js 0.12.0 must co-exist in package-lock without duplication). No API breakage: the 0.10.0→0.12.0 delta is additive-only for fourier's current callers (easeInOutSine, timingFunctions — both unchanged).
findings.wave_hint: M.W1 (version-bump wave, prerequisite of all other E4 findings)

findings.title: spectrumColor quadruplication — four independent HSL-template implementations across the codebase
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/transforms.ts:3-7 (hsl(${hue}, 85%, 55%), no alpha param); web/src/components/equation/FrequencyGraph.vue:42-45 (identical, no alpha); web/src/components/shared/CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:47-49 (identical, no alpha); web/src/components/equation/lib/harmonics.ts:81-88 (adds alpha param, uses hsla). Four independent copies, three of which lack an alpha param and one of which carries it — guaranteed future drift.
findings.current_state: Each call site hand-rolls `hsl(${(1 - i / Math.max(total - 1, 1)) * 300}, 85%, 55%)`. The colour space is sRGB-HSL — perceptually non-uniform (equal hue steps have unequal perceived chroma, especially at the warm/cool boundary around hue 60). The 'rainbow' array in VIZ_COLORS is six hand-chosen hex strings; the harmonic-animation colour ramp and the epicycle-circle colour ramp are unrelated aesthetically.
findings.proposed: Delete all four local spectrumColor definitions. Author a single `src/lib/spectrum.ts` that uses value.js 0.12.0's `OKLCHColor` + `color2` + `gamutMap` to produce a perceptually-uniform OKLCH sweep: fixed L≈0.70 (perceptually 'pop' lightness), C≈0.18 (vivid but in-gamut sRGB), H sweeps 0→300° via `interpolateHue(..., 'shorter')`. Emit `toFormattedString()` for CSS contexts and the raw `RGBColor` channels for Canvas fillStyle. This replaces HSL arithmetic with OKLCH geometry — colour contrast stays proportional, chroma stays vivid across the full hue arc, and dark-mode reads correctly. The alpha variant is a parameter on the single function.

findings.title: 118-line bespoke CSS-var-to-hex parser in colors.ts duplicates value.js 0.12.0 parseCSSColor
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/colors.ts:22-54 — cssVarToHex() hand-parses hsl(...), bare 'h s% l%' triplets, and rgb(...) via regex chains. hslToHex (lines 56-68) and rgbToHex (lines 70-74) are custom implementations. hexToRgba (lines 101-106) and hexToRgb (lines 111-117) are bespoke. resolveVizColors() (lines 89-96) calls cssVarToHex five times on CSS custom properties. Total: ~70 lines of colour arithmetic that value.js 0.12.0 handles at its parseCSSColor + colorUnit2 + color2 layer.
findings.current_state: Fourier maintains its own colour parser that understands only four syntax variants. It fails silently on oklch(...), color(...), or any CSS Color 4 form a future token upgrade might emit. The hexToRgba call sites (epicycles.ts:258,283, golden-shimmer.ts:55,58, BasisCanvas.vue:261) produce rgba() strings by string-joining integer channels — correct but bypasses value.js's gamut-aware path.
findings.proposed: Delete colors.ts's hslToHex, rgbToHex, cssVarToHex bodies. Replace resolveVizColors with: `parseCSSColor(getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue(varName).trim())` — the 0.12.0 `ParsedColorUnit` covers every syntax the browser can emit. Replace hexToRgba with `color2(parseCSSColor(hex).value!, 'rgb')` then `toFormattedString()` with alpha injected, or simply emit `oklch(L C H / α)` directly via `OKLCHColor.toFormattedString()`. hexToRgb callers that feed Canvas ctx can use `RGBColor` channel values directly (0–255 range via `getColorSpaceBound`). net: delete ~80 lines, replace with 5–8 lines of value.js calls.

findings.title: DarkModeToggle lerpColor uses raw sRGB channel arithmetic — perceptual mudding on warm-to-cool transition
findings.evidence: web/src/components/layout/DarkModeToggle.vue:30-32 — SUN_COLOR=[232,136,69] (#E88845, warm orange), MOON_COLOR=[192,132,252] (#c084fc, cool violet). lerpColor (lines 39-43) lerps r/g/b independently in sRGB, producing a desaturated grey-brown midpoint around t=0.5 — a known perceptual artefact of sRGB straight-line interpolation through the hue gap between orange and violet.
findings.current_state: The dark-mode toggle morph (useFourierMorph, ~200–400ms) visually muddies through a muted brownish-grey at the midpoint. This is the highest-visibility colour animation in the app (every page, every mode toggle).
findings.proposed: Replace lerpColor with value.js 0.12.0's `mixColors(sunColor, moonColor, 1-t, t, 'oklch', 'shorter')` where sunColor and moonColor are `new OKLCHColor(...)` built once from the two hex literals via `parseCSSColor` + `color2(..., 'oklch')`. OKLCH 'shorter' hue interpolation sweeps through the vivid orange→red→violet arc, keeping chroma high throughout. Emit via `Color.toAnimationString(4)` for the SVG stroke attribute (zero-alloc, the 0.12.0 B1 perf path). This is a gestalt transposition: same hex anchors, perceptually correct arc, one import line.

findings.title: energyColor and notation.ts use HSL threshold literals — not tied to the token system or perceptual scale
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/equation/notation.ts:14-16 — three HSL literals for notation modes (hsl(6,72%,49%), hsl(224,58%,46%), hsl(286,46%,47%)). Lines 22-42 — TIER_INFO uses hsl(142,71%,45%) for green, hsl(38,92%,50%) for amber, hsl(0,84%,60%) for red. energyColor() lines 44-48 returns three HSL strings by threshold. These six HSL literals define the only 'audacious pop' colours shown outside the canvas (notation pills, energy ring, tier badge) and they are unconnected to VIZ_COLORS or CSS tokens.
findings.current_state: The three notation mode colours and three tier/energy colours are tuned by eye in HSL. They have no relationship to `--viz-fourier` (tomato, hsl 6 72% 49% — identical to the trig notation colour by coincidence), `--viz-amber`, or the OKLab contrast floor. In dark mode these colours are not adjusted — `TIER_INFO.symbolic.color = hsl(142,71%,45%)` is the same string in both modes; dark-surface contrast is untested.
findings.proposed: Transpose these six colours to OKLCH literals (e.g. `oklch(0.64 0.18 150)` for the symbolic green, `oklch(0.72 0.17 60)` for amber, `oklch(0.62 0.22 20)` for the red tier). Use value.js 0.12.0's `computeSafeAccent(L, C, H, bgLightness)` at the call site in components that render these colours — e.g. in EquationView.vue's `eColor` computed, call `safeAccentColor(baseColor, isDark ? 0.15 : 0.92).toFormattedString()` so the colours auto-shift lightness in dark mode without duplicating token values. The TIER_INFO map stays a plain record but its values become OKLCH strings the browser renders natively (CSS Color 4, baseline 2023).

findings.title: mixColorsN (0.12.0) enables harmonic-weighted colour sweeps absent in current fourier — the colourful-pops unlock
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/epicycles.ts:162 — `const color = colorOverride ?? spectrumColor(i, nVis)` — each epicycle gets a hue indexed by position. value.js 0.12.0 exports `mixColorsN` (src/units/color/mix.ts:28) which takes an array of Color objects + optional per-color weights, returning a perceptual blend in a named space. This function did not exist in 0.10.0. Fourier currently has zero callers of mixColorsN; the capability is entirely unexercised.
findings.current_state: The epicycle spectrum, convergence-plot harmonic colours, and frequency-graph bar colours all use the same `spectrumColor` HSL sweep — an equal-step hue rotation. There is no amplitude-weighted or energy-weighted colour blending: the dominant (large-amplitude) component and a trace harmonic get the same chroma/lightness regardless of their contribution to the approximation. The 'colourful audacious pops' directive has no OKLCH substrate today.
findings.proposed: Build an `amplitudeWeightedColor(components, index, totalVisible)` helper in `src/lib/spectrum.ts` that uses `mixColorsN` with amplitude-derived weights: map each component's amplitude to a weight, then blend a set of anchor colours (e.g. `--viz-fourier` tomato, `--viz-amber`, a cool violet from `--viz-legendre`) proportional to spectral energy. The dominant component pulls toward the tomato anchor; equal-energy harmonics blend to the full arc. Separately, use `mixColorsN` in the convergence-plot for the 'current partial sum' colour: blend all active harmonic colours weighted by amplitude, producing a single 'gestalt' colour for the reconstructed curve that shifts visually as harmonics are added. This is a direct no-legacy use of the 0.12.0 API; zero duplication with the existing spectrumColor sweep.

findings.title: computeSafeAccent / safeAccentColor (0.12.0) absent — no contrast-safe accent logic on any coloured swatch
findings.evidence: value.js 0.12.0 exports `computeSafeAccent`, `safeAccentColor`, `needsContrastAdjustment`, `getOklchLightness` (src/units/color/contrast.ts; re-exported src/index.ts:151-155). Fourier 0.10.0 install: these four symbols absent. Fourier applies spectrumColor() swatches directly as backgroundColor in CoefficientsSpectrum.vue:94 and ConvergenceLegend.vue:36 with text/icons overlaid — no contrast check. In dark mode the HSL `hsl(h, 85%, 55%)` swatches can fall within 0.15 OKLab lightness of the dark surface, failing perceptual readability.
findings.current_state: Legend dots and amplitude bars are coloured by `spectrumColor()` in `background` or `strokeStyle` with adjacent text in `--foreground`. No contrast floor is enforced. The HSL `85% saturation / 55% lightness` formula is not anchored to a perceptual scale; some hue bands (yellow-green ~hue 90–120) produce near-white swatches that read poorly on a white background, while the cool end (hue 270–300) can muddify against a mid-grey surface.
findings.proposed: After bumping to 0.12.0, wrap every `spectrumColor(i, total)` call in the HTML/CSS swatch context with a `safeAccentColor(parsedColor, bgLightness).toFormattedString()` pass. bgLightness is read once from the surface token via `getOklchLightness(parseCSSColor(getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--background').trim()).value!)`. This produces a minimum ΔL of 0.35 (the default) against the surface, auto-adapting to light/dark mode without separate token branches.

findings.title: toAnimationString (0.12.0) absent — WAAPI colour keyframes still emit legacy sRGB strings
findings.evidence: value.js 0.12.0 adds `Color.toAnimationString(digits, outputSpace)` (src/units/color/index.ts:399-431) — a zero-alloc per-frame serialiser that emits CSS-valid colour strings in the requested space with the `color(<space> …)` wrapper for WAAPI/non-legacy spaces. It also adds `cssColorInterpKeyword(space, hueMethod)` (src/units/color/dispatch.ts:337-341) producing the WAAPI `<color-interpolation-method>` keyword. fourier 0.10.0 install: absent. The DarkModeToggle lerpColor emits `rgb(${r},${g},${bl})` strings per frame (DarkModeToggle.vue:43). The golden-shimmer oscillation (golden-shimmer.ts:11-13) and tip-dot pulse (epicycles.ts:280-283) hand-compute rgba strings.
findings.current_state: Every per-frame colour string in fourier is assembled via template literals with integer-rounded channels. The DarkModeToggle emits sRGB strings; the shimmer emits hexToRgba strings; all of these allocate a new string per frame. Under a 60Hz rAF loop on a 1000-component epicycle chain this is measurable GC pressure (the same N.W7.B-perf problem value.js solved for keyframes.js).
findings.proposed: Replace all per-frame rgba string assembly with `color.toAnimationString(4)` on a pre-built Color instance. For the dark-mode toggle, construct two `OKLCHColor` anchors once at module level and call `mixColors(sun, moon, 1-t, t, 'oklch', 'shorter').toAnimationString(4)` per frame — zero intermediate string allocation. For the shimmer glow and tip-dot pulsation, construct an `RGBColor` at module level and mutate its `.alpha` channel per frame, then emit `.toAnimationString(4)` — the ANIMATION_SCRATCH buffer in value.js 0.12.0 makes this branch zero-alloc (the single shared scratch is reused across all per-frame calls).

findings.title: gamutMap wide-gamut egress (0.12.0) absent — canvas epicycle colours cannot safely target Display P3
findings.evidence: value.js 0.12.0 adds wide-gamut egress to `gamutMap(color, targetSpace)` (src/units/color/dispatch.ts:269-307): non-sRGB RGB-family targets (display-p3, rec2020, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, srgb-linear) use the binary-search OKLCh chroma-reduction path rather than the Ottosson sRGB-specific map. `EMIT_GAMUT_SPACES` (src/units/color/index.ts:135-142) gates this per egress. fourier 0.10.0 install: gamutMap exists but only sRGB-exits; Display P3 egress would silently emit out-of-gamut values on an Apple M-series display where the Canvas 2D context has a Display P3 colour space.
findings.current_state: The Canvas 2D rendering context on Apple Silicon Safari runs in Display P3 by default when the display reports a P3 colour profile. fourier's spectrumColor(i, n) hsl strings are valid sRGB; the browser maps them to P3 on paint. An OKLCH ramp (proposed in E4-F2) at C≈0.18 sits safely inside sRGB, but a 'more audacious' pop (C≈0.25–0.30, the design directive's desire for higher chroma) can exit sRGB while staying in P3. Without the 0.12.0 wide-gamut gamutMap, a future higher-chroma ramp would silently clip on sRGB-only displays.
findings.proposed: After bumping to 0.12.0, use `gamutMap(color, 'display-p3')` as the egress when the Canvas context's colorSpace is 'display-p3' (detected via `canvas.getContext('2d', { colorSpace: 'display-p3' })`). For sRGB contexts use `gamutMap(color, 'rgb')` as before. This future-proofs the higher-chroma ramps the colourful-pops wave will introduce — they stay in-gamut on every display. The gamutMap API is unchanged from 0.10.0 → 0.12.0 except the targetSpace param now works correctly for non-sRGB targets.

findings.title: sampleColorRamp (planned 0.13.0) — forward adoption seam must be booked now to unblock M.W3's harmonic-sweep design
findings.evidence: value.js docs/tranches/N/GRAMMAR-FOLD.md (PART I, ratified 2026-06-15) + docs/tranches/N/waves/N.W11.md (lane D) — `sampleColorRamp(from, to, n, {space, hueMethod, endpoints?, gamutMap?})` returns a `Color[]` of n perceptually-equidistant stops in the given space with per-stop `gamutMapOKLab` egress. Target: value.js 0.13.0 (N.W11 color-SOTA wave + N.W11.D fold). Not shipped at 0.12.0 (grep of dist/value.js = ZERO). The function's born-RED gate is verified absent at 0.12.0 (src/units/color/mix.ts has `mixColorsN` but no `sampleColorRamp`).
findings.current_state: Fourier's proposed OKLCH harmonic spectrum (E4-F2) requires sampling n equidistant OKLCH stops between two anchor colours. With mixColorsN (0.12.0) this is possible but requires N-colour equal-weight folding (not a linear ramp). sampleColorRamp IS the right primitive — a linear ramp from anchor-A to anchor-B with n stops, hue-method encoded. It cannot be substituted correctly today.
findings.proposed: For M.W3 implementation: use mixColorsN with equal weights as a temporary OKLCH ramp (n stops at equal intervals, via a loop calling mixColors at t=k/(n-1)). Book the sampleColorRamp adoption for the M.W3-followup or the first M.Wx that targets 0.13.0. The value.js N.W11 wave is RATIFIED (2026-06-15) and targets 0.13.0; the book should have a hard kill-date = 0.13.0 publish (not yet on npm; verify with `npm view @mkbabb/value.js version` at adoption time). When it ships, replace the mixColorsN loop with a single `sampleColorRamp(from, to, n, {space:'oklch', hueMethod:'shorter'})` call — fewer allocations, the gamutMapOKLab per-stop egress included.

open_questions: value.js 0.13.0 (sampleColorRamp / N.W11.D) is RATIFIED (2026-06-15) but not yet published — what is the estimated ship date for N.W11 so M can sequence its adoption correctly?

The proposed OKLCH harmonic ramp (E4-F2) uses fixed L≈0.70 / C≈0.18 anchors. Does the design directive's 'audacious pops' target a higher chroma (C≈0.22–0.28) that would require Display P3 egress (E4-F9), or does sRGB-safe chroma satisfy the proportion constraint?

resolveVizColors() is called imperatively on mount and dark-mode toggle. With parseCSSColor replacing cssVarToHex, the CSS custom-property values may arrive as oklch(...) strings in future token upgrades. Is the current call site (resolveVizColors in AppHeader) the canonical hook, or should colour resolution move to a VueUse watcher on the color-scheme media query?

The computedEndpointCache tier (value.js 0.11.0 B3+B5) is most valuable in keyframes.js animation contexts. fourier's colour animations currently run via manual rAF in the canvas stores rather than keyframes.js. Should the 0.12.0 bump be paired with a keyframes.js 4.2.0 bump to enable WAAPI colour keyframes (toAnimationString + cssColorInterpKeyword) as the canonical per-frame path, or does the canvas rAF loop remain separate?

E5.verdict: Fourier runs six distinct animation surfaces: (1) a manual rAF ping-pong clock in the animation store driving the epicycle canvas at 60 fps, (2) a separate manual rAF loop in ConvergencePlot (equation page) that is an independent and architecturally redundant twin of the store clock, (3) a third manual rAF tween engine in useCurveTransition for coefficient transitions, (4) two concurrent hover-scale + shimmer rAF sub-loops inside useCanvasHover that fire on mousemove outside the main clock, (5) a CSS-only surface (six @keyframes across four components plus View Transitions and Transition wrappers), and (6) the keyframes.js Animation engine used narrowly for the Fourier morph sequence. The rAF budget is high: at peak (epicycle canvas with hover active) four concurrent rAF loops run simultaneously on the main thread. The store clock is the only one gated by IntersectionObserver; the ConvergencePlot loop has no visibility gate. PRM coverage has three gaps: rainbow-slide in ImageUpload, golden-shimmer in ContourEditorCanvas, and the main-thread shimmer rAF in useCanvasHover which fires unconditionally. Proportionality is broadly maintained but the play-button rainbow-drift, the ConvergencePlot's always-on auto-play, and performance.now-based shimmer sampling during the main 60 fps draw call each push toward gaudy or INP-risk territory.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot: autonomous rAF clock duplicates animation store, no visibility gate
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:49-75 — local `rafId`, `loopStartTime`, `startLoop()`/`stopLoop()` with its own ping-pong logic. Mounted at line 324 with `playing.value = true; startLoop()`. No IntersectionObserver, no `anyCanvasVisible` gate. The store already has an identical mechanism (animation.ts:51-75).
findings.current_state: A second, independent 60 fps rAF clock runs whenever the /equation page is mounted, regardless of whether the canvas is visible. It does not consult the animation store or share the visibility-gated infrastructure the epicycle canvas uses.
findings.proposed: Transpose ConvergencePlot's playback to consume `useAnimationStore` — the store's `t` / `easedT` reactive refs are already the canonical clock. Remove `rafId`, `loopStartTime`, `playing`, `startLoop`, `stopLoop` from ConvergencePlot. Wire `draw()` to a Vue `watch(() => [anim.t, hoveredCurve], draw)` — the store's rAF clock already calls into Vue reactivity. The ConvergencePlot has its own custom `animDuration` and `eT` easing (easeInOutSine); expose these as a store `setDuration(ms)` + `setEasing(fn)` call, or maintain a local `easedT = computed(() => easeInOutSine(anim.t))` without duplicating the clock. The store's visibility gate then protects both canvases for free.

findings.title: useCanvasHover: two concurrent rAF sub-loops (hover-scale + shimmer) independent of main clock
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-82 — `hoverAnimFrame` drives a lerp loop for epicycle scale; `shimmerRafId` drives a perpetual `shimmerTick` calling `onRedraw()` (which is `drawFrame()`) as fast as the display allows. Both are separate from the animation-store clock. When the user hovers a label, three rAF loops fire simultaneously: store clock + hover-scale + shimmer.
findings.current_state: The shimmer loop calls `onRedraw` every frame for as long as a basis label is hovered. `goldenShimmerAlpha()` samples `performance.now() / 200` on every canvas draw regardless — even during the 60 fps main clock. This gives no frame budget for other tasks, conflicts with INP, and has no PRM check.
findings.proposed: Consolidate into the main store clock. The shimmer's alpha is already sampled inside `drawFrame()` which the store clock drives; the separate `shimmerTick` rAF is redundant — it causes a *second* `drawFrame()` call per animation frame while the store loop is playing. Remove `shimmerRafId` entirely: when `hoveredBasis` is set while the store is playing, the main clock already redraws. When the store is paused (scrubbing or idle), replace the shimmer rAF with a CSS `@keyframes` shimmer driving a `--shimmer-alpha` custom property via `@property` animation, which the canvas reads via `getComputedStyle`; or use keyframes.js `springLinearStops` to generate the oscillation as a `linear()` value for a CSS animation. The hover-scale lerp loop (`hoverAnimFrame`) is a bespoke spring; replace with `SpringProgress` from keyframes.js 4.x (`respectReducedMotion: true`), ticking inside the main draw call.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot canvas: canvas resized (width/height set) on every draw frame at 60 fps
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:84-94 — `draw()` always executes `const rect = container.getBoundingClientRect(); canvas.width = Math.round(rect.width * dpr); canvas.height = ...; ctx.setTransform(...)` unconditionally. BasisCanvas.vue uses `useCanvasSetup` which separates resize (ResizeObserver) from draw; ConvergencePlot does not.
findings.current_state: Setting `canvas.width` triggers a GPU texture reallocation and context reset on every draw call (60 fps while playing). This is a serious GPU/CPU jank source: the browser must discard and reallocate the canvas backing store every frame, even when dimensions are stable.
findings.proposed: Extract canvas sizing into a ResizeObserver callback exactly as `useCanvasSetup` does for BasisCanvas. Introduce a `surface` ref holding `{ ctx, width, height, dpr }` updated only when size changes. `draw()` reads from `surface` and clears/renders without touching `canvas.width`. This mirrors the existing `useCanvasSetup` composable — extract ConvergencePlot into the same composable or create `useEquationCanvasSetup` following the same pattern.

findings.title: useCurveTransition: third bespoke 500ms rAF tween alongside two existing rAF clock architectures
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:36-53 — `startTransition()` runs its own `requestAnimationFrame` loop for 500ms eased lerp of harmonic data. Triggered from ConvergencePlot.vue:312-313 on coefficient change.
findings.current_state: Three independent rAF loop patterns exist in the codebase: the animation store (ping-pong), ConvergencePlot (ping-pong), and useCurveTransition (tween). Each reinvents `performance.now` timestamping and easing application.
findings.proposed: Replace with keyframes.js `Animation` engine already loaded lazily for the morph composable (`useFourierMorph.ts:39-44`). The engine promise is already cached: `getAnimationCtor()` → `createTweenAnimation()`. Map `useCurveTransition`'s 500ms `easeInOutSine` tween to a `new Animation({ duration: 500, timingFunction: 'ease-in-out-sine', iterationCount: 1 })` with a single frame callback — identical to the morph composable's `createTweenAnimation`. This converges all JS-timed transitions onto one engine.

findings.title: ImageUpload: rainbow-slide infinite CSS animation has no prefers-reduced-motion guard
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/ImageUpload.vue:159 — `animation: rainbow-slide 1.4s linear infinite` on the upload progress stripe. No `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block present in the file. GalleryMarquee and GalleryCard both add PRM guards for their infinite animations; ImageUpload does not.
findings.current_state: Users who have requested reduced motion see the infinite rainbow stripe during image upload. The animation is decorative (purely a progress indicator) and non-essential.
findings.proposed: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .upload-progress-bar { animation: none; } }` immediately after the `@keyframes rainbow-slide` block. Optionally replace the animation with a solid progress bar driven by actual upload progress (fetch `onprogress`) — a static fill is more informative and entirely PRM-safe. The rainbow is currently decorative; making it functional (actual %) would be the idiomatic step.

findings.title: ContourEditorCanvas: golden-shimmer infinite CSS animation has no prefers-reduced-motion guard
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/ContourEditorCanvas.vue:324-330 — `.editor-svg:hover .spline-path { animation: golden-shimmer 1.2s ease-in-out infinite }`. No PRM media query guard. ContourEditorCanvas also uses bare `ease-in-out` keyword rather than a canonical token.
findings.current_state: Hovering the SVG contour editor spline triggers an infinite glow animation with no PRM suppression.
findings.proposed: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .editor-svg:hover .spline-path { animation: none; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 4px hsl(40 90% 55% / 0.5)); } }` to give a static highlight without motion. Replace the bare `ease-in-out` easing keyword with `var(--ease-standard)` to align with the canonical token vocabulary established in A.W3.d.

findings.title: performance.now() shimmer sampling runs on every 60 fps canvas draw call — no clock memoization
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/golden-shimmer.ts:11-12 — `goldenShimmerAlpha()` returns `0.85 + 0.15 * Math.sin(performance.now() / 200)`. Called from BasisCanvas.vue:170, 255; canvas-drawing/labels.ts:37; canvas-drawing/epicycles.ts:280 (inline variant). Every draw frame — fired by the 60 fps rAF — calls this multiple times to compute a value that changes at ~5 Hz.
findings.current_state: The shimmer value is sampled 3-5 times per draw frame with separate `performance.now()` calls. At 60 fps this means ~180-300 `Math.sin` evaluations per second for a decorative oscillation that visually resolves at ~5 Hz. The `performance.now()` call itself forces a timing read per canvas op.
findings.proposed: Memoize the shimmer value once per rAF tick: compute it at the top of `drawFrame()` (or at the animation store `tick`) and pass it as a parameter to all draw helpers. This reduces the cost to one `performance.now()` + one `Math.sin` per frame. Longer term the oscillation itself belongs in a CSS `@property` `@keyframes` animation (`--shimmer-alpha: 0.85; to { --shimmer-alpha: 1.0 }`) driven off-main-thread; the canvas reads the computed value once via `getComputedStyle`. This is the platform-native approach for a periodic decorative signal.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot rAF loop has no IntersectionObserver gate — burns CPU when scrolled off-screen
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:323-326 — mounts with `playing.value = true; startLoop()` unconditionally. No IntersectionObserver. BasisCanvas (animation.ts:42-46, BasisCanvas.vue:432-452) has an explicit off-screen gate. ConvergencePlot is on the /equation page but could scroll below the fold or be behind a tab.
findings.current_state: The convergence plot's 60 fps rAF loop runs even when the plot is not visible. Combined with E5-01 (separate clock) this means two ungated 60 fps loops fire simultaneously on the equation page.
findings.proposed: If E5-01 is resolved (plot delegates to animation store), this problem dissolves — the store's `anyCanvasVisible` gate already handles it via `setCanvasVisible`. If the plot retains its own clock, add an `IntersectionObserver` on `containerRef` calling `playing.value = entry.isIntersecting` (or a dedicated `clockRunning` ref that gates `startLoop`), mirroring BasisCanvas.vue:435-452.

findings.title: keyframes.js pinned at ^2.2.0 — two major versions behind 4.2.0; morph composable uses legacy Animation class API
findings.evidence: web/package.json: `"@mkbabb/keyframes.js": "^2.2.0"`. Published: 4.2.0. `useFourierMorph.ts:14` — `import { loadAnimationEngine, type Animation } from "@mkbabb/keyframes.js"`. keyframes 4.x ships `SpringProgress` (native `(response, dampingFraction)` physics, `respectReducedMotion` flag, `RAFPlayback` driver) and `springLinearStops` for CSS `linear()` generation — neither is accessible on ^2.2.0.
findings.current_state: The morph composable uses the `Animation` class with a WAAPI-disabled tween (`useWAAPI: false`) as a manual ticker. The 4.x `SpringProgress` class would replace the hand-rolled lerp loops in useCanvasHover (hover-scale) and useCurveTransition with spring physics and built-in PRM support, which are not available at the installed version.
findings.proposed: Bump `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` to `^4.2.0`. The `loadAnimationEngine` import in `useFourierMorph` is forward-compatible (it still exists in 4.x per the source grep). After bumping: replace `useCanvasHover`'s manual `diff * 0.12` exponential lerp loop (`composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-62`) with `new SpringProgress({ response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.85, respectReducedMotion: true })` ticking inside the main draw call; replace `useCurveTransition`'s rAF tween with keyframes.js engine. This is a prerequisite for E5-02 and E5-04 idiomatic proposals.

findings.title: play-btn rainbow-drift: `background-size: 300% 300%` background-position CSS animation — INP boundary risk on low-end devices
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/AnimationControls.vue:163-176 — `.play-btn::before` has a 7-stop conic gradient at `300% 300%` cycling via `@keyframes rainbow-drift { background-position: ... }` at `2.5s infinite`. This is a `background-position` animation on a large pseudo-element with `backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(1.4)` on the parent. On low-end mobile the compositor cannot promote `backdrop-filter` layers; `background-position` is a paint-tier property.
findings.current_state: The is-playing state triggers a GPU-bound composite + repaint cycle every 2.5s (at minimum) on a backdrop-blur surface. On Adreno 5xx and below, this causes jank during the animation. The PRM guard exists (`animation: none` under PRM) but the base cost remains for non-PRM users on constrained hardware.
findings.proposed: Replace the `background-position` animation with a `transform: rotate()` or `hue-rotate()` animation on a separate positioned pseudo-element — both are compositor-promoted. The gradient itself can remain; only the motion needs to move to the transform/filter axis. For example: `@keyframes hue-spin { from { filter: hue-rotate(0deg); } to { filter: hue-rotate(360deg); } }` applied to `::before` at `6s infinite linear`. This is equivalent visual effect at zero paint cost. Additionally replace the five inline rgba() color literals on the `::before` gradient with `--viz-*` tokens for dark-mode coherence.

findings.title: Scattered bare `ease` keyword in transitions across 10+ components — inconsistent with canonical token vocabulary
findings.evidence: Grep evidence: PaperArticleWindow.vue:199 `0.2s ease`, EquationResult.vue:97 `0.15s ease`, EquationView.vue:418 `0.12s ease`, ConvergenceTimeline.vue:142 `0.1s ease`, FourierMorphDemo.vue:299+323 `0.15s ease`, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:239 `0.15s ease`, MorphShapePreview.vue:97 `0.2s ease`, AppHeader.vue:180+211+283+296+330 `0.12-0.25s ease`, ContourEditorCanvas.vue:320+311 `ease/none`, ContourSettings.vue:346+397+444 (no easing keyword). A.W3.d established `var(--ease-standard)` / `var(--ease-out-expo)` / `var(--ease-apple-spring)` as the token vocabulary. Bare `ease` is the CSS keyword equivalent of `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)` — distinct from all glass-ui tokens.
findings.current_state: 10+ components mix bare `ease` keyword with canonical tokens. Transitions on the same logical surface (e.g., hover color) use different timings in different components.
findings.proposed: Mechanical substitution: map bare `ease` → `var(--ease-standard)` for all UI micro-transitions (color, background, border, opacity at 0.1-0.2s). For directional enter/exit transitions (translateY, scale) use `var(--ease-out-expo)` on enter and `var(--ease-standard)` on leave. For spring-feel interactions (morph button, like-bounce) use `var(--ease-apple-spring)`. Consolidate in a single M tranche wave (e.g., M.W3 with the PRM fixes) as a sweep.

findings.title: FullscreenViewer `<Transition name='fs'>`: no View Transition integration — misses the native compositor path
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/FullscreenViewer.vue:106 — Vue `<Transition name='fs'>` drives the fullscreen open/close with CSS `opacity + scale(0.95)` transitions at 250ms. The router already uses `document.startViewTransition` (router/index.ts:146) for route swaps. VisualizationView.vue:310-316 names `.canvas-stage` with `view-transition-name: viz-canvas-stage` under PRM guard. But the fullscreen overlay toggle is a within-page state change — not a route swap — and never goes through the VT path.
findings.current_state: The fullscreen expand/contract animation (scale + opacity) runs on the main thread via CSS transition. This is a same-page transition between two views of the same canvas content — the ideal use case for View Transitions' cross-fade + geometry morph.
findings.proposed: Wrap the `show.value` toggle in `document.startViewTransition(() => { show.value = v; })` where the VT engine is available (guarded by `'startViewTransition' in document`). Give `.fs-backdrop` a `view-transition-name: fullscreen-overlay` scoped to its presence. Remove or keep the CSS `<Transition>` as the PRM/unsupported floor. The morph from the inline canvas to fullscreen reads as a native expand rather than a fade-from-nothing. This aligns with the I-tranche inv-29 progressive-enhancement-floor: CSS Transition is the fallback, VT is the enhancement.

findings.title: useScrollNavigation: rAF correction loop for virtual-section scroll — up to 20 frames of main-thread positioning
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/useScrollNavigation.ts:133-163 — `teleportTo()` runs a correction loop `requestAnimationFrame(correct)` that can iterate up to `MAX_CORRECTIONS = 10` times (line 154) or `frames++ < 20` times (line 138) per teleport, calling `opts.recalculate()` and `scroller.scrollTo` each frame.
findings.current_state: Far-jump paper navigation runs up to 20 sequential rAF frames with `recalculate()` and `scrollTo` per frame. This is intentional (virtual section measurement convergence) but represents 20 * 16ms = 320ms of main-thread rAF on every long jump. The overlay hides the jank but the budget is spent.
findings.proposed: This is architectural and tied to the latex-paper virtual scroll system — a full redesign is out of scope for a single wave. Immediate improvement: reduce `MAX_CORRECTIONS` from 10 to 5 and `frames < 20` guard to `< 8` — the stability check (`STABLE_TARGET = 2`, `STABILITY_PX = 6`) typically converges in 2-3 frames once the section mounts. Add a `performance.now()` budget cap: if total correction time exceeds 200ms, call `finish()` unconditionally. This bounds worst-case jank regardless of section layout complexity.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot auto-plays on mount unconditionally — no user-intent gate
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:324 — `nextTick(() => { draw(); t.value = 0; playing.value = true; startLoop(); })`. The convergence animation auto-starts whenever the equation result renders.
findings.current_state: Every function submission auto-plays the convergence animation. Users navigating quickly or comparing results get immediate CPU-intensive 60 fps motion without opt-in.
findings.proposed: Gate auto-play on `!window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`. Store a `userHasManuallyPaused` flag: if the user pauses and then re-submits, do not auto-restart. This is proportionate — the convergence animation is the primary visual payoff of the equation page, so auto-play is appropriate for non-PRM users on first load; it should not re-trigger on each re-submission.

glassui_asks.name: CSS @property shimmer token
glassui_asks.what: Ship a `@property --shimmer-alpha` animation in glass-ui's animations.css: a CSS custom-property keyframe oscillating 0.85→1.0 at a configurable period (default 200ms). Components consuming the shimmer read `var(--shimmer-alpha)` in Canvas 2D `globalAlpha` or SVG `opacity` without any JS `performance.now()` call.
glassui_asks.why: Three fourier canvas surfaces (BasisCanvas, ConvergencePlot labels, epicycles.ts) call `performance.now() / 200` every draw frame to compute a decorative 5 Hz oscillation. Moving this to a compositor-timed CSS custom property eliminates the JS sampling cost and makes the shimmer honourably PRM-suppressible via the standard `prefers-reduced-motion` cascade.

E6.dimension: E6 — Animation-Architecture Transposition (gestalt, no-legacy): consolidate fourier's fragmented motion into one idiomatic architecture over keyframes.js 4.2.0 + value.js 0.12.0 + glass-ui 4.0.0 motion primitives + native scroll-driven CSS + View-Transitions
E6.verdict: fourier's motion is fragmented across at least 8 independent hand-rolled rAF loops, 7 bespoke @keyframes, two duplicated ping-pong clocks, raw value.js easing imports, and a manual scroll-progress writer — while the sibling libraries now ship the exact canonical replacements: glass-ui 4.0.0 exposes a complete `/motion` + `/motion-core` composable suite (`useRAFLoop`, `useScrollProgress`, `useViewTransition`, `useIntersectionPause`, `useSpring`, `useAnimatedNumber`, `useStaggerReveal`) plus `scroll-driven.css`/`view-transition.css`, and keyframes.js 4.2.0 ships a value.js-free light tier (`RAFPlayback`, `NumericAnimation`, `SpringProgress`, `SmoothProgress`, `Timeline`/`ScrollTimeline`, `springTimingFunction`). fourier imports ZERO of these. The gestalt M-motion CORE is a three-layer architecture — CSS-first (native scroll/VT/@keyframes, compositor) over glass-ui motion composables (the Vue-reactive managed tier) over keyframes.js light primitives (the canvas/data-driven tier) — with value.js owning only colour/easing curves. This retires the manual rAF store (the named legacy), collapses the two ping-pong clocks into one, and removes ~20 raw requestAnimationFrame call-sites. Everything proposed is no-legacy: each hand-rolled loop is DELETED, not wrapped.

findings.title: Manual rAF store is the named legacy — transpose the epicycle clock onto keyframes.js RAFPlayback + glass-ui useIntersectionPause
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/animation.ts:32-145 — hand-rolled rafId loop with manual ping-pong (cycle%2), manual visibility ref-count (visibleCanvases), manual scrub-pause/speed-restart watch; lines 46-50 comment admits a prior keyframes.js Animation graph was ripped out leaving the bespoke loop as 'sole driver'
findings.current_state: The epicycle playback clock is a Pinia store driving a raw requestAnimationFrame tick that recomputes forward/reverse fraction by hand, reference-counts canvas visibility through setCanvasVisible (IntersectionObserver wiring lives in the canvas), and re-arms the loop on speed/scrub changes. value.js easing is applied as a post-hoc computed (easedT). It is the exact 'manual rAF loop not keyframes.js' the memory flags as legacy.
findings.proposed: Make the store a pure STATE atom (t, playing, speed, duration, easing, scrubbing) and move the DRIVE into keyframes.js light tier. Use RAFPlayback.loop(cb) (the generation-guarded, bind-proof managed driver) as the single clock; express the 20s ping-pong as a NumericAnimation with iterationCount:Infinity, direction:'alternate' queried via .at(progress) (zero-alloc) OR a ManualTimeline whose eased value the renderer reads — value.js easing flows in via springTimingFunction/resolveEasing ONCE up front, not a per-frame computed. Replace the hand-rolled visibleCanvases ref-count with glass-ui useIntersectionPause (it already owns IO + document-visibility pause and exposes pause/resume) bound to RAFPlayback.stop/start. Scrub becomes ManualTimeline.set(t). Net: the store holds intent+state, glass-ui owns the gate, keyframes owns the clock — no requestAnimationFrame in fourier source.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot duplicates the store's ping-pong clock verbatim — collapse the two clocks into one driver
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:57-73 — a SECOND hand-rolled startLoop with the identical cycle%2===0 ? frac : 1-frac ping-pong math and its own rafId, distinct from stores/animation.ts:58-72 which has the same algorithm
findings.current_state: The equation page's convergence plot and the workspace epicycle canvas each maintain their own independent rAF ping-pong loop with byte-for-byte duplicated forward/reverse fraction arithmetic and separate playing flags. Two clocks, one concept.
findings.proposed: Both consume ONE shared playhead primitive. Extract a single useFourierPlayhead() composable backed by keyframes.js NumericAnimation/ManualTimeline + RAFPlayback (per E6-1) that yields a reactive eased t and a playing flag; the canvas renderer and ConvergencePlot both subscribe. The alternate (ping-pong) cycling is a NumericAnimation direction:'alternate' config, defined once. Deletes ConvergencePlot.vue's startLoop/stopLoop entirely. One clock, two consumers.

findings.title: useFourierMorph builds tween animations on the HEAVY keyframes engine via a string-px hack — transpose to the light NumericAnimation + Sequence tier
findings.evidence: web/src/composables/useFourierMorph.ts:122-143 — createTweenAnimation constructs a heavy Animation (via loadAnimationEngine, useWAAPI:false) whose only purpose is a 0→1 progress tween, faked with addFrame('0%',{v:'0px'}) / '100%' {v:'1px'} and reading time/duration; three sequential awaited phases each spin up one such tween
findings.current_state: The morph subsystem pulls the value.js-bearing HEAVY engine (loadAnimationEngine) purely to get a duration-clocked 0→1 progress callback, abusing a dummy v:'0px'→'1px' keyframe to extract t. This drags the full CSS-keyframe parser + value.js into the morph path for what is a scalar tween, and re-implements phase sequencing by hand-chaining three Promises.
findings.proposed: Drop the heavy engine from morph entirely. Each phase is a keyframes.js light NumericAnimation([{p:0},{p:1}], {duration, timingFunction}) — value.js-free, zero-alloc, with a real .play(onTick) that resolves on completion (no dummy-px hack). The three-phase settle-out→morph→settle-in chain is exactly keyframes.js Sequence (the master-playhead orchestrator) — author the phases as a declarative sequence with per-segment easing resolved once via resolveEasing. value.js easing curves still flow through, but as timingFunction not a bundled engine. Removes loadAnimationEngine + getAnimationCtor + the enginePromise singleton from this file.

findings.title: useCurveTransition hand-rolls a third rAF lerp clock — fold into the shared light tier
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:36-54 — startTransition spins its own requestAnimationFrame tick computing easeInOutSine(elapsed/500) and calling onFrame, returning a manual cancel closure
findings.current_state: The equation curve cross-fade (500ms eased interpolation on function change) is yet another bespoke rAF loop with its own performance.now timing and a hand-returned cancel function, importing easeInOutSine raw from value.js.
findings.proposed: Replace with keyframes.js SmoothProgress (exponential smoothing toward a target — frame-rate independent via the managed .play(onTick) that owns its own rAF until settled) OR a NumericAnimation 0→1 with the value.js easeInOutSine as timingFunction. The state snapshot (prevHarmonics/prevY-bounds) stays; only the clock is replaced. SmoothProgress is the more idiomatic fit because curve changes can interrupt mid-flight — it re-seats toward the new target continuously rather than restarting a fixed-duration tween.

findings.title: Canvas hover-scale + shimmer are two more hand-rolled rAF loops with a magic-number exponential lerp — transpose to SpringProgress/SmoothProgress
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-82 — updateHoverScale does currentScale += diff*0.12 per rAF frame (a hand-rolled exponential smoother) plus a separate shimmerTick rAF loop; both manage their own hoverAnimFrame/shimmerRafId
findings.current_state: Epicycle hover-scale is a hand-tuned diff*0.12 exponential approach with a 0.002 settle threshold (a re-implemented SmoothProgress), and the shimmer is its own perpetual rAF loop — two more independent requestAnimationFrame sites in one composable.
findings.proposed: The hover-scale smoother is precisely keyframes.js SmoothProgress({damping:0.12, snapThreshold:0.002}) — set target on hover-enter/leave, read .current in the redraw; its managed .play owns the loop and auto-stops on settle (deletes the manual threshold check + frame bookkeeping). For an audacious-pop register prefer SpringProgress({response, dampingFraction}) so the scale overshoots/settles (proportion-governed, PRM-honoured via respectReducedMotion). The shimmer is a continuous phase advance — drive it off the SHARED canvas playhead (E6-1/E6-2) rather than a private loop, gated by glass-ui useIntersectionPause so it parks off-screen.

findings.title: PaperView keeps a manual rAF scroll-progress writer behind a hand-rolled @supports gate — adopt glass-ui useScrollProgress / .scroll-progress recipe
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperView.vue:150-185 — manual progressRaf writeProgress loop with a hand-written CSS.supports('animation-timeline','scroll()') gate; glass-ui ships dist/styles/scroll-driven.css (.scroll-progress) + useScrollProgress.ts which already implement exactly this dual-path-single-writer pattern
findings.current_state: The paper reading-progress bar duplicates, by hand, the dual-path (native scroll() timeline vs JS fallback) logic that glass-ui's scroll-driven.css + useScrollProgress already ship — including the same @supports feature-detection and the same single-writer discipline, re-authored locally.
findings.proposed: Adopt the glass-ui .scroll-progress CSS recipe (compositor-driven scaleX bar on a scroll() timeline) as the primary, with glass-ui useScrollProgress as the ≤20-LOC feature-detected fallback — glass-ui already gates the composable OFF when the native path attaches (no double-run). Delete fourier's writeProgress/progressRaf and the local @supports gate. This moves the bar off the main thread and removes a fourier-owned rAF site. Author the paper's other entrance reveals via the [data-scroll-reveal] view()-timeline recipe (implicit stagger, no setTimeout cascade).

findings.title: Seven bespoke @keyframes re-implement glass-ui motion idioms — retire to glass-ui tokens/recipes or scroll-driven CSS
findings.evidence: web/src/style.css:84-94 (tab-slide-in) + GalleryMarquee.vue (marquee-scroll-left/right, marquee-left/right), style.css (rainbow-slide, rainbow-drift, golden-shimmer, like-bounce); GalleryCard.vue:295-306 like-bounce uses var(--ease-apple-spring) — already a glass-ui token, proving the recipe layer is available but only half-adopted
findings.current_state: Seven hand-authored @keyframes scattered across style.css and gallery components re-create slide-ins, infinite marquee scroll, rainbow drifts, shimmer and bounce — motion idioms that glass-ui 4.0.0 either ships as recipes (animations.css, scroll-driven.css) or backs with spring tokens (--spring-*, --ease-apple-spring already in use at GalleryCard.vue:295).
findings.proposed: Audit the seven against glass-ui's animations.css / scroll-driven.css and the --spring-{smooth,snappy,bouncy,gentle} tokens. The infinite marquee is the strongest candidate for the native scroll-driven path (or a glass-ui marquee recipe if shipped) — a JS-free compositor loop. tab-slide-in and like-bounce should consume glass-ui spring tokens for their timing rather than literal ease-out/0.3s so motion is design-language-consistent. Keep only genuinely fourier-specific keyframes (e.g. math-domain rainbow-drift) but re-source their easing from the shared tokens. NO !important overrides of glass-ui internals; if a recipe is missing, BOOK it (see glassui_asks) rather than hand-rolling.

findings.title: View-Transitions are wired ad-hoc in the router with raw double-rAF — adopt glass-ui useViewTransition + the shipped view-transition.css substrate
findings.evidence: web/src/router/index.ts:124-174 — hand-rolled document.startViewTransition wrap + double requestAnimationFrame release; VisualizationView.vue:307-313 hand-writes @supports(view-transition-name) + view-transition-name; glass-ui ships useViewTransition.ts on /motion-core (instant fallback + finished promise for focus routing) and dist/styles/view-transition.css (--vt-* tokens, PRM carve, .gl-list-item recipe)
findings.current_state: fourier hand-rolls the View-Transition swap (router guard + raw double-rAF release) and hand-authors the view-transition-name CSS, duplicating glass-ui's useViewTransition helper and view-transition.css substrate which already own the instant fallback, the finished-promise for a11y focus routing, the PRM carve, and the --vt-* token set.
findings.proposed: Route the router-guard swap and any in-view VT (gallery list re-rank, the J diff-viewer reveal) through glass-ui startViewTransition/useViewTransition from /motion-core — it returns finished so fourier can await-then-focus (the a11y mandatory the helper deliberately leaves to the consumer). Adopt the view-transition.css --vt-* tokens + view-transition-class: gl-list-item recipe instead of hand-written ::view-transition rules. Delete the local double-rAF release (the helper's fallback handles non-supporting engines). This interlocks with J's e2e: the glass-dock dup-VT-name blocker is resolved by the glass-ui bump, so the VT layer lands clean.
findings.wave_hint: M-W7 (View-Transition consolidation) — interlocks with J e2e close

findings.title: Dependency pins are 1-2 majors behind the shipped siblings — the bump is the hard predecessor of the entire motion CORE
findings.evidence: web/package.json: @mkbabb/glass-ui ^3.1.0 (shipped 4.0.0), @mkbabb/keyframes.js ^2.2.0 (shipped 4.2.0 — TWO majors), @mkbabb/value.js ^0.10.0 (shipped 0.12.0). npm view confirms 4.0.0 / 4.2.0 / 0.12.0. The /motion composable suite + the light RAFPlayback/Timeline/SpringProgress tier this CORE depends on do not exist at the pinned versions.
findings.current_state: Every transposition in E6-1..E6-8 depends on APIs that only exist at glass-ui 4.0.0 (the /motion suite, scroll-driven.css, useViewTransition) and keyframes.js 4.x (the value.js-free light surface: RAFPlayback.loop, NumericAnimation direction:alternate, SpringProgress.fromDuration, ScrollTimeline). The pins predate all of it. RUN-BOARD.md is 11 days stale and still treats glass-ui 3.x as the ceiling.
findings.proposed: M-W1 is a SOURCE-LEVEL re-pin + lock-regen: glass-ui ^3.1.0→^4.0.0, keyframes.js ^2.2.0→^4.2.0, value.js ^0.10.0→^0.12.0, verified by a cited green CI run (inv-27, not a blind bump — two keyframes majors and a glass-ui major can surface latent fault). Confirm single-copy in the lockfile (keyframes is now a DIRECT dep AND glass-ui's peer; the value.js engine boundary must stay externalized). This bump is the keystone: it unblocks the motion CORE, the J e2e close (dock-VT useId is in 4.x), and the scroll/VT recipe adoption simultaneously. It goes FIRST.

findings.title: value.js easing is imported raw and twice-cataloged — unify on the keyframes.js easing boundary + spring twins, with value.js as the curve authority
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/easings.ts:9-16,55-84 — two parallel catalogs (EASING_PRESETS comprehensive + ANIMATION_EASINGS compact) both wrapping value.js timingFunctions/easeInOut* directly; useCurveTransition.ts:8 and others import easeInOutSine raw; no use of keyframes.js resolveEasing/toEasing or springTimingFunction
findings.current_state: fourier maintains two hand-curated easing catalogs that wrap value.js timing functions directly, and individual files import value.js easings ad-hoc. There is no spring vocabulary at all (no springTimingFunction/springLinearStops), so all motion is curve-flattened — no overshoot/settle, which the audacious-pop design language wants.
findings.proposed: Keep value.js as the CURVE AUTHORITY (it owns the cubic-bezier/linear()/oklab math) but route resolution through keyframes.js resolveEasing/toEasing (the easing boundary that yields the typed Easing all light primitives accept) so one catalog feeds NumericAnimation, SmoothProgress, ElementMorph, and CSS alike. Add a spring vocabulary via springTimingFunction({response,dampingFraction}) whose .css linear() twin and .fn callable are ONE solver — the same overshoot runs on the WAAPI compositor (CSS) and in canvas (JS). This gives the design-language pops a real settle curve, proportion-governed and PRM-gated. Collapse the two catalogs into one keyed table; consumers stop importing value.js easings directly.

findings.title: The teleport correction loop in paper navigation is a manual stabilize-rAF — leave as platform scroll, do NOT migrate to a motion primitive
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/useScrollNavigation.ts:133-164 — a requestAnimationFrame correction loop re-measuring section offsets until stable; this is layout-stabilization, not motion
findings.current_state: The paper teleport uses rAF to re-measure and re-snap scroll position as heavy sections mount — it is a measurement-convergence loop, not an animation. Two other rAF sites (the overlay paint-wait) are also layout-sync, not motion.
findings.proposed: EXCLUDE from the motion CORE — correctly. This is the platform's scroll + a measure-converge loop; routing it through a motion primitive would be a category error (the same judgement scheduler.ts makes about not yielding mid-render-frame). Document it as deliberately-platform in the M charter so a future sweep does not 'consolidate' it. The genuine motion sites are E6-1..E6-8; this and the overlay paint-wait are layout-sync and stay as raw rAF. Marking the boundary explicitly is part of the no-legacy discipline (no over-reach).
findings.wave_hint: M-W0 (charter — boundary doc; not a migration)

glassui_asks.name: fourier-shaped-playhead-orchestrator (confirm useRAFLoop covers the ping-pong/alternate case)
glassui_asks.what: Confirm whether glass-ui's useRAFLoop (or a motion composable composition) cleanly expresses an infinite forward/reverse ping-pong playhead with reactive eased t, scrub-seek, and speed-scaling — the epicycle/convergence clock shape. If not, a small usePlayhead-style composable wrapping keyframes.js NumericAnimation(direction:'alternate') + RAFPlayback + useIntersectionPause would serve every fourier viz and likely other media consumers.
glassui_asks.why: fourier has TWO duplicated ping-pong clocks (stores/animation.ts, ConvergencePlot.vue). If glass-ui already covers this via useRAFLoop+useIntersectionPause composition, fourier composes existing primitives (no ask). If it is a common shape not yet a single composable, it belongs IN glass-ui as the canonical media-playhead — fourier books the ask rather than re-authoring locally (inv-16: fourier does not write glass-ui).

glassui_asks.name: marquee-as-scroll-driven recipe
glassui_asks.what: Whether glass-ui ships (or should ship) an infinite-marquee recipe in scroll-driven.css / animations.css backed by a compositor loop with hover-pause and a reduced-motion carve — the GalleryMarquee shape.

If glass-ui owns a canonical marquee recipe, fourier adopts it; if absent, this is a net-new motion recipe primitive that belongs upstream (every gallery-style surface in the constellation wants it). fourier books the ask, does not author it locally as a bespoke keyframe.

glassui_asks.name: canvas-targeted spring guidance (DOM composables vs keyframes light primitives)
glassui_asks.what: Confirm the intended division of labour: glass-ui useSpring/useSpringPress for DOM/Vue-reactive transform targets, keyframes.js SpringProgress/SmoothProgress (light tier) for canvas/imperative numeric targets such as fourier's hover-scale and shimmer phase.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's hover-scale writes to a Canvas 2D draw, not a DOM element. Clarifying the boundary prevents fourier from mis-adopting a DOM-shaped composable for a canvas target. Guidance ask, not a code ask.

keyframes.js is currently a transitive/peer dep reached only via loadAnimationEngine in useFourierMorph. The light tier (RAFPlayback, NumericAnimation, SpringProgress) requires keyframes.js as a DIRECT dependency. Confirm fourier should add the direct dep (it should — the light tier is value.js-free, so no bundle regression) and that the lock stays single-copy against glass-ui's keyframes peer range.

Does the design language want canvas micro-motion (hover-scale) to OVERSHOOT (SpringProgress, audacious pop) or merely smooth (SmoothProgress)? The proportion directive permits audacious-but-not-gaudy; the spring twin makes overshoot free, but the call is a design choice to ratify in M-W0.
